Error-first recall (US-602): assembleErrorFirstContext wraps store/retrieval.ts's searchFactsBm25/assembleContext (no duplicated BM25/token-budget logic) and guarantees a matching error_solution fact leads the packet regardless of raw BM25 rank vs. other fact kinds -- test-proven with a plain fact that outranks the error fact on BM25 yet the error fact still assembles first; emits memory.error_first_recall for session provenance (US-602 AC-2) only when an error fact actually leads. AGENT 2026-07-20: gate-fix retry. dedupe.ts's group key was naive space-joined string concatenation (`${kind} ${ticketId ?? ''} ${content}`), not injective -- a space landing on a field boundary could collide two distinct (ticketId, content) pairs onto the same key (e.g. ticketId='a', content='b c' vs ticketId='a b', content='c'), silently decaying (permanently hiding from recall) a semantically distinct fact -- confirmed by direct reproduction, a real bug. NO new workspace imports in packages/pipeline/package.json — mirror runPipeline`s PipelinePort pattern (W5-17): local port types, deterministic core, all effects injected.

The coverage manifest enumerates ALL of the imported rule set BY NAME — all 30 anti-slop rules and all 66 validators (R-E3, the name-ALL-of-the-set lesson) — each tagged shadow/advisory/gate per D-014. runOnboard stays pure/deterministic, never authors prose and never imports a model/provider directly (Law 6), so a fake dispatch port yields a fully assertable run with no network (Law 9).

All-or-nothing like runPipeline: on any step`s dispatch error the run throws and returns no partial OnboardRunResult — no health assessment is built from a step that did not complete, and no step-complete event is emitted for it.

tickets.title: Phase-validator runner: real validator runs mint a genuine gate receipt under a distinct verifier identity
acceptance: A phase-gate runner executes the phase's declared validator set (`PHASES[n].validators`, read live off the topology, never frozen) against the project's real on-disk deliverables, and records each validator's name, exitCode and gapCount from the actual run. FR-P1's 'No receipt without a real run' is the bar: a hardcoded or assumed pass fails acceptance.

A clean run mints a gate receipt via `@dokima/validators`' `mintValidatorRunReceipt` (whose FIRST production caller this will be). Reaching it requires two lines of dependency wiring, in scope for this ticket: add `"@dokima/validators": "workspace:*"` to `apps/server/package.json`, and `export * from './phases/index.js';` to `packages/pipeline/src/index.ts` so `PHASES` is importable at all. The receipt carries the input-file content hashes FR-P2 later recomputes, so a silently edited doc invalidates it.

The receipt is minted under a verifier identity DISTINCT from the identity that authored the phase output (Law 5, maker != verifier, mechanical not conventional). A red fixture proves a same-identity mint is refused.

Red fixture first, per docs/TESTING.md's planted-defect harness: a phase whose validator genuinely fails mints NO receipt (not a receipt with a failing exit code recorded as passing), and a phase with no validator run at all has no receipt.

Does NOT mint receipts for model-authored `PipelineRunEvent` output. That path stays a plain hash-chained audit event: the SECURITY_W5 CRITICAL fix removed gate receipts there precisely because no independent validator runs on it, and re-adding them would restore the self-attestation this ticket exists to avoid. A test pins that pipeline-run events remain unanchored.
Full gate green including `pnpm --filter @dokima/web e2e`; test counts reported in the commit body.

tickets.title: Phase-advance route: wire decideAdvance so a phase transition is gated by a re-verified receipt
acceptance: A phase-advance route calls `decideAdvance` (packages/pipeline/src/phases/advance.ts) with the real `deps.verifyReceipt` bound to `@dokima/events`' `verifyReceipt`, passing the from-phase's CURRENT `PHASES[n].validators` for the gate receipt and `[]` for a waiver receipt, exactly as AdvanceDeps documents.

An advance with no gate receipt is REFUSED, and the refusal names why. FR-P3's 'the UI states which receipts became stale and why' applies: `AdvanceResult.reasons` reaches the caller intact rather than collapsing to a bare 403 or a boolean.

FR-P2's two-way re-verification demonstrably works end to end: editing a phase deliverable after its gate receipt was minted causes the next advance to be refused with the input-hash mismatch surfaced; adding a validator to the phase's declared set likewise refuses on validator-set drift.

The waiver bypass is honored and bounded: a human-signed waiver receipt permits the advance and is marked `waived`, an agent-signed one is rejected (FR-P2 blocklist), and a clean waiver is still refused on phases 4-5 (FR-G5, `assertWaiverEligible`). tickets.title: Byte-preserving board writes — the conductor rewrites all of plan.json on every status change
acceptance: A conductor board write is byte-identical to the file it replaces, apart from the statuses it intentionally changed. Today `conductor.mjs:371,424` write `JSON.stringify(plan, null, 2) + '\n'`, which against the current 493,140-byte board produces a **2,800-byte divergence**: every ASCII-escaped `\u00a7`/`—` becomes literal UTF-8, plus a trailing newline the file does not have.

A test asserts the round-trip mechanically: read the real `plan.json`, write it back through the conductor's serializer unchanged, and assert the bytes are identical. Proving it by eye or by line count is not sufficient — the defect is invisible in a line-count diff and shows up as ~400 changed lines in review.
Changing one ticket's status produces a diff of only the lines for that status — verified in the test, since an unreviewable board diff is the actual harm.
The fix preserves whatever convention the file already uses rather than imposing one, so a repo whose board is written in literal UTF-8 stays that way.

tickets.title: No compile step: packages ship raw TypeScript, so the documented `npx dokima` install path cannot work from a registry
acceptance: FILED 2026-07-30 from live verification. No `build` script exists except `apps/web`; all 12 packages export `./src/index.ts`; `tsconfig.base.json` sets `noEmit: true`. The blocker: `tsx` is an `apps/server` **devDependency** while `cli-entry.mjs` spawns `node_modules/.bin/tsx` at runtime, and every `@dokima/*` dep is `workspace:*` — a registry consumer gets neither, so the shim fails at `spawn`. DEPLOYMENT.md 1's `npx dokima` row is NOT deliverable today. W8-05 closed naming this an honest gap and it was never ticketed.

SHAPE DECIDED 2026-07-30 (founder): bundle into ONE published package, not 13. esbuild inlines `apps/server` + all 12 workspace packages; `better-sqlite3`, `execa`, `fastify`, `google-auth-library` and `zod` stay external and become real `dependencies` of the shipped package (they currently live in three different packages' node_modules). esbuild becomes an EXPLICIT devDependency recorded in docs/TECH_STACK.md — it is already in the tree transitively via vite and tsx, and a phantom dependency must not be relied on.

THE ACTUAL WORK, established by probe on 2026-07-30 rather than by reading: esbuild bundles the whole server cleanly (0 errors, 0 warnings, 411KB) and the bundle then DIES on its first run with `ENOENT ... scandir <bundle-dir>/migrations`. **13 non-test sites resolve assets from `import.meta.url` relative to their own source file**, which in a bundle is the bundle's directory. Every one must resolve through a single bundle-aware asset-root helper. A bundle that builds green and cannot boot is the disconnected-pipeline class this repo caught in W9-06 and W9-11.

The assets those sites reach for must actually ship, enumerated from the probe: `packages/events/migrations/**` and the global-db migrations, `content/experts`, `content/guide`, `content/validators`, and `apps/web/dist` (served as the SPA at `apps/server/src/api/main.ts:60`). That cannot work from a bundle at all and needs a redesign, not a path fix; if it grows past a small change, split it into its own ticket rather than smuggling it in here.

PROVEN BY EXECUTION, not by the build exiting 0: the bundled server boots under **plain `node`, no `tsx` on PATH, no TypeScript loader**, and answers `/healthz` with `{"status":"ok","db":true,"ws":true}` — `db:true` is the load-bearing part, since it is what proves the migrations actually resolved. Then, as far as offline allows (C-1, law 9, no live registry calls): `pnpm pack`, inspect the tarball to confirm the assets ship and no `workspace:*` survives, install it into a scratch dir and run the binary.

`dist/` gitignored; `docs/DEPLOYMENT.md` 1 corrected — it currently says the repo "has no compile step yet" and defers the registry channel as a follow-up, and this ticket IS that follow-up. tickets.title: trace.spec.ts: the trace e2e never sees its own project card — 2 specs red on a quiet machine
acceptance: FILED 2026-07-30 from a quiet-machine e2e run (load ~10, suite 3.7m): `e2e/trace.spec.ts:54` ("the trace view is honestly empty for a ticket no run has ever touched") and `:73` ("replays a run's events labeled by kind") both fail in the shared `openFreshProject` helper at `trace.spec.ts:49`, on `expect(locator('.project-card').filter({hasText: 'Trace E2E <uuid>'})).toBeVisible()` -> `element(s) not found` after 5000ms. The other 56 specs pass.

NOT a W9-13 regression, and this was established rather than assumed: this session's FIRST e2e run, against unmodified `main` before any code change, failed the same two specs with a byte-identical signature — same locator shape, same helper line, differing only in the random project UUID. W9-13 took the suite from 30 failures to 2; these are the 2 that were always there.

ROOT-CAUSED 2026-07-30, and it is NOT what this ticket first guessed. The `computeProjectStats open failed ... directory does not exist` line is a RED HERRING: it appears on a fully green run too, since tests legitimately delete their own tmp dirs. The real cause is that `playwright.config.ts` points `DOKIMA_HOME` at a FIXED tmp path shared by every test AND every run, with `reuseExistingServer` locally, so the Fleet registry is never cleaned. It had reached **1,164 projects / 422KB of fleet.json**, accumulating since 2026-07-23.

PROVEN by wiping that home and re-running the identical suite: **58/58 passed in 22.0s**, against 2 failed in 3.7m immediately before — a 10x wall-clock difference and the failures gone. So the product is not defective and the assertion is not too tight; the harness is not hermetic. The fix therefore belongs in the e2e setup, NOT in trace.spec.ts (whose assertion was correct all along) and NOT in a widened timeout. `GET /api/v1/projects` was separately timed at 286ms with all 1,164 registered, which rules out server latency and points at client-side render volume.

The suite starts from a clean DOKIMA_HOME every run, via Playwright globalSetup, so this cannot silently re-accumulate. Verified the hard way: restore the real 1,164-project fleet.json, then run the full suite and watch it pass anyway — a fix that only works from an already-clean home has not fixed anything.
Full gate green including `pnpm --filter @dokima/web e2e`; counts in the commit body.
tickets.notes: FILED 2026-07-30 by the W9-13 session, deliberately as a separate ticket rather than folded into it: W9-13 was a packaging change and these two specs were red before it started. tickets.title: Fleet has no way to remove a project, so an entry whose directory is gone is permanent
acceptance: FILED 2026-07-30 out of W9-14, deliberately as a product ticket rather than folded into that test fix. There is no remove/forget/unregister path for a project: grepping `apps/server/src/api/projects.ts` and `apps/web/src/fleet/**` finds no DELETE route and no UI affordance. A project registered once stays in `fleet.json` forever, including after its directory is deleted.

This is not hypothetical and W9-14 measured the consequence. The e2e registry reached **1,164 entries**, almost all pointing at deleted tmp directories, and the Fleet view degraded badly enough that a newly-onboarded project card did not render inside 5s — while `GET /api/v1/projects` itself still answered in 286ms. The server is fine; the accumulated list is what hurts, and a real user hits the same shape more slowly by onboarding, moving, and deleting repos over months.

Decide and record the intended behaviour before building, because two reasonable products differ here: (a) an explicit "Remove from Fleet" action that forgets the registry entry without touching the project on disk, and/or (b) rendering an entry whose directory is missing as a distinct "unavailable" state with a remove affordance, rather than as an ordinary card whose stats silently read zero. Removing a project from the Fleet must never delete the user's repo or its `.dokima/state.db` — that is the sharp edge in this ticket.

Whatever is chosen, the honest-absence rule applies (the same one `healthz` and the trace view already follow): a project whose directory has vanished must not be shown as a healthy card with zeroed stats, since that is indistinguishable from a real, empty project.

Red fixture: a registry containing an entry whose directory does not exist renders the unavailable state (not a zeroed normal card), and removing it leaves the on-disk directory of a still-present project untouched — asserted against the filesystem, not just the API response.
Full gate green including `pnpm --filter @dokima/web e2e`; counts in the commit body.

tickets.title: One-command autorun — and stop the supervisor destroying uncommitted work on launch
acceptance: Launching unattended currently means hand-typing four lines from CONDUCTOR_RUNBOOK.md (`nohup caffeinate -dimsu bash scripts/supervise.sh ... >> docs/work/conductor.out 2>&1 &` plus a manual pid write). Three of the four fail SILENTLY when forgotten: no caffeinate and the machine sleeps mid-run, no redirect and an overnight run has no log, no pid file and `stop` becomes pkill guesswork against a tree that includes agent sessions. `scripts/autorun.sh start|stop|status` wraps it, passing extra args (`--waves`, `--no-merge`, `--breakpoint`) through to supervise.sh unchanged.

DEFECT FOUND WHILE BUILDING THIS, and it is the more important half of the ticket. `supervise.sh` runs `git checkout -f main` + `git clean -fd` at the TOP OF ITS LAUNCH LOOP — so on every start, not only after a crash, despite the comment describing it as crash recovery. Launching from a feature branch with uncommitted work therefore destroys that work silently. Reproduced by accident, on this ticket: the first `autorun.sh start --lint` discarded W9-16's own uncommitted board filing and deleted the untracked `scripts/autorun.sh` outright.

Same class as the 2026-07-28 fix that stopped this cleanup deleting unmerged BRANCHES — that one protected committed work on branches and left uncommitted and untracked work unprotected. The first launch of a run is a deliberate human act, not crash debris: supervise.sh must REFUSE to start when the tree is dirty or the checkout is not on main, naming what it would have destroyed. Crash-RESTARTS (iteration 2+) keep resetting exactly as today, because there the dirty tree genuinely is a dead attempt's debris.

`autorun.sh start` performs the same check up front so the refusal arrives before anything is backgrounded, and a stale pid file (rebooted machine, SIGKILLed supervisor) never permanently blocks a relaunch — liveness is `kill -0`, not the file's existence.

NOT escalated by default: conductor.config.json $modelsNote records "Overnight runs launch WITHOUT --escalate: sonnet-only ladder, frontier spend requires a human (D-018)". A convenience wrapper that quietly raises the spend ceiling is not a convenience. caffeinate is macOS-only and its absence degrades to running without it (W3-15 portability precedent), never aborts.

Verified WITHOUT spending provider tokens: launch through the wrapper with `--lint` (conductor exits immediately), asserting pid file written, log appended, process reaped, and `status` honest before and after. Separately assert the dirty-tree refusal by launching with a deliberately uncommitted file present and confirming the file SURVIVES. Runbook Launch/Control sections lead with the wrapper, raw incantation kept beneath as the escape hatch.
tickets.notes: FILED 2026-07-30 at Brad's request ("can you do that for this product as well so we can just auto run"). Dokima is where conductor.mjs and supervise.sh were BUILT and from which Kryptkeeper vendored them, so the harness was always here — only the front door was missing. The destroy-uncommitted-work defect was found the hard way, by this ticket losing its own first draft to it, which is the most direct possible evidence for why the guard belongs in the tool rather than in the runbook. DONE 2026-07-30. scripts/autorun.sh start|stop|status + pnpm autorun/autorun:stop/autorun:status. Both layers guarded: autorun refuses before backgrounding anything (so the refusal is on your terminal, not buried in a log you have to go read), and supervise.sh refuses independently for anyone calling it directly. Verified without spending a token: --lint launch writes the pid, appends the log, is reaped, and status reports honestly before and after; a deliberately untracked CANARY.txt SURVIVED both an autorun start and a direct supervise.sh call that would previously have deleted it. Board unchanged throughout. Runbook Launch/Control now lead with the wrapper, raw incantation kept beneath.

tickets.title: Persisted provider registry — a provider you can add without editing JSON by hand
acceptance: TODAY there is no registry: `apps/server/src/cli/ops/providers-core.ts` says so verbatim — "There is no persisted provider registry yet anywhere in the codebase" — and reads a `providers` key out of the three-scope settings file, consumed ONLY by `shipwright doctor` and `providers refresh`. There is no REST surface and no GUI, so registering a provider means hand-editing JSON. tickets.title: The receipts fetch double-prefixes /api/v1 — the drawer 404s and the palette fails silently
acceptance: OBSERVED 2026-08-02 against the real running product, in BOTH themes: opening any ticket drawer fires GET /api/v1/api/v1/projects/<id>/receipts?ticket=<id> — note the DOUBLED path segment — which 404s. ROOT CAUSE, already traced: `request()` in apps/web/src/artifacts/api.ts:49 builds `${opts.baseUrl ?? ''}${urlPath}`, but every urlPath in that module already hardcodes the /api/v1 prefix (e.g. line 179). ArtifactViewerRoot.tsx:69 works because it passes `{ getToken }` with NO baseUrl; EvidencePanel.tsx:30 passes `{ baseUrl, getToken }` where baseUrl is "/api/v1" (App.tsx:343/359/368), so it doubles.

BLAST RADIUS is four call sites in two components, not one: EvidencePanel.tsx:30 (fetchReceipts) plus CommandPalette.tsx:86 (fetchArtifactList), :87 (fetchReceipts) and :142 (fetchReceipt). The palette calls have NO .catch, so they reject unhandled and the palette silently shows no docs and no receipts — a silent failure, strictly worse than the drawer's visible error. Fix all four.

Make the class of bug impossible rather than patching four call sites: either have `request()` reject/normalise a baseUrl that would duplicate the prefix it already carries, or strip the hardcoded prefix from the module and require baseUrl. Pick one and make the other shape a type or runtime error — a third caller will otherwise reintroduce this.

RED FIXTURE, and it is the point: assert the REQUEST URL, not just the parsed response. The reason 2923 tests and 59 e2e specs all pass while this ships broken is that EvidencePanel.test.tsx never asserts a URL and CommandPalette.tsx has NO test file at all. Add a test that fails on a doubled /api/v1 — verified by reverting the fix and confirming red.

tickets.title: RELEASE BLOCKER: every validator in the shipped pack fails to run — _lib.sh is never installed
acceptance: MEASURED, and worse than this ticket was originally filed as. It was filed as "the shared libs are unsigned". They are not merely unsigned — they are NEVER INSTALLED. `packsUpdate` installs exactly the files named in `content/manifest.json`; `sign-content.mjs` selects them with VALIDATOR_NAME_RE (`^(?:(?:validate|run)-.+|secrets-scan)\.sh$`), which `_lib.sh` and `_lib_sdlc_config.sh` do not match. So a real install lands 81 validators and zero shared libraries.

PROVEN AT RUNTIME, not inferred: running an installed validator from a real `packsUpdate` destination exits **127** with `_lib.sh: No such file or directory`, then `validator_init: command not found`, then `detect_project_root: command not found`. Every one of the 81 installed validators sources `_lib.sh`. The shipped validator pack is non-functional in its entirety.

WHY NOTHING CAUGHT IT — this is the gate hole, and it is the real deliverable. The repo runs validators from `content/validators/` in the SOURCE TREE, where `_lib.sh` sits beside them, so every gate, every conductor run and every existing test passes. `packs-update.test.ts` verifies signatures, hashes and install counts but never EXECUTES an installed validator. A pack can therefore be fully verified, fully installed, and completely broken — which is exactly the shape of the W10-29 finding (a green suite over a surface that 404s).

FIX: include the shared libraries in the signed manifest so they are verified and installed like everything else. They are executable content the product runs, so signing them is also correct on its own terms — an attacker who can write `_lib.sh` controls all 81 validators, and until now it was not covered by the signature at all.

RED FIXTURE, the one that would have caught this: install a pack to a temp dir via the real `packsUpdate`, then EXECUTE an installed validator and assert it exits on its own 0/1/2 contract rather than 127. Assert `_lib.sh` is present and verified. Prove it reds against the current code — it must, since today that run exits 127.

tickets.title: Two glob dialects decide write_scope and nothing asserts they agree
acceptance: CONTEXT, from an external pilot report (Documents/CONDUCTOR_PILOT_REPORT_REDACTED_2026-08-03.md, §2.4): a comparable harness lost two tickets to a write_scope glob its normalization silently did not recognise — a filename wildcard (`dir/*.test.ts`) was treated as a literal nonexistent directory, so nothing inside the real directory ever matched and the scope gate rejected correct work. The gate was right; the scope was malformed and nothing said so.

MEASURED ON DOKIMA: that specific bug does NOT apply — `globToRegex` handles `dir/*.test.ts`, `**/*.css`, prefix and suffix wildcards correctly, and the enforcer agrees with `validate-plan.mjs`’s independent `segmentTextOverlaps`/`globOverlaps` on every probe tried. This ticket is NOT a bug fix. It converts that agreement from luck into an invariant.

THE REAL EXPOSURE: two independent glob implementations decide write_scope. `scripts/conductor-lib/parsing.mjs` `globToRegex` ENFORCES scope at gate time; `scripts/validate-plan.mjs` `globOverlaps` decides lane-overlap legality at board-validation time. They are kept in sync by a COMMENT ("same dialect as packages/tickets/src/lanes.ts — keep in sync; W3-12 consolidates"). A divergence produces exactly the pilot’s failure: a scope the board accepts and the enforcer rejects, diagnosed as a bad ticket rather than a dialect gap.

PIN IT WITH A DIFFERENTIAL TEST: assert the two implementations return the same answer across a broad matrix of (glob, path) pairs — literal, prefix `*`, suffix `*`, mid-segment `*`, `**` crossing directories, `?`, dotfiles, extension wildcards, and non-matches — plus every write_scope glob actually on the board crossed against every path it is meant to cover. A divergence must name the glob, the path, and both answers.

DO NOT CONSOLIDATE THE TWO IMPLEMENTATIONS in this ticket. validate-plan.mjs is deliberately dependency-free (it runs as a bare `node scripts/validate-plan.mjs` in CI with no workspace install), so importing conductor-lib into it is a real coupling decision, not a cleanup. Pinning agreement is the cheap correct step; consolidation stays W3-12’s.
Full gate green including e2e, counts in the commit body.

This ticket is the one piece of genuine residue: an unasserted cross-implementation invariant. SCOPE AMENDED 2026-08-03 (third amendment this session — the pattern is my own ticket-scoping, §10 of RESUME_2026-08-03 exactly). The differential test did not merely pin the invariant, it FOUND A REAL BUG in the enforcer, so the fix has to live in scripts/conductor-lib/parsing.mjs, which the filed scope did not name because I expected a test-only ticket. globToRegex expands a/**/b to ^a/.*/b$ — the slash after ** is literal, so ** requires AT LEAST ONE directory segment, while every standard glob dialect (bash globstar, minimatch, git pathspec) and validate-plan.mjs itself treat it as zero-or-more. Consequence: apps/web/src/**/*.css did not cover apps/web/src/styles.css. W10-06, W10-28 and W10-30 all carried that glob and all silently worked around it by listing styles.css explicitly — the enforcement boundary was narrower than it read, three times, unnoticed. This is the pilot report failure shape exactly: a scope the board accepts and the enforcer rejects, diagnosed as a bad ticket rather than a dialect gap. AGENT 2026-08-03: done. Neither pilot bug applies to Dokima (both checked against code). But the differential test found a REAL divergence on first run: globToRegex required >=1 directory segment for **/, while validate-plan.mjs and every standard dialect allow zero — so apps/web/src/**/*.css did not cover apps/web/src/styles.css. Already worked around unnoticed in W10-06/W10-28/W10-30 by listing the file explicitly. Fixed; the fix needed the ? expansion reordered before the sentinel joins because the replacement contains a literal ? that the blanket pass ate, producing a silently-wrong regex rather than an error. Fix both: point the empty-board control at whatever actually shows the current phase (or remove it if no such surface exists yet — a button that goes somewhere wrong is worse than no button), and stop seeding Dokima-internal sample cards into user-created projects.

RED FIXTURE for each: an e2e spec asserting the empty-board control lands on a phase surface rather than the improvement plan, and one asserting a freshly created project’s chat pane contains no SAMPLE cards.

tickets.title: A 60s provider timeout makes local models — the headline use case — unusable
acceptance: MEASURED END TO END IN A BROWSER against the installed package: filled the new interview surface (W10-54) with a real idea, clicked "Build the board", watched LM Studio move to GENERATING — then the run failed with HTTP 500 and the body `pipeline-run: request timed out after 60000ms`. The seam works; the timeout kills it.

ROOT CAUSE, read from source rather than guessed: `DEFAULT_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS = 60_000` in oai-compat-types.ts, anthropic-types.ts, copilot-types.ts and openai.ts. The creation pipeline makes several SEQUENTIAL inference calls (blueprint, technical slate, ticket drafts), and a local reasoning model spends most of its budget reasoning — measured 199 reasoning tokens out of 203 for a one-word reply — so a single phase can exceed 60s on ordinary hardware.

THIS CONTRADICTS THE PRODUCT PREMISE, which is why it is a defect rather than a tuning preference. C-1 / Law 9: everything must work against a local model. The README calls a local LM Studio or Ollama box "a first-class setup, not a downgrade", and the wizard offers All-local as its first preset. A default tuned for a fast hosted API, which times out on the very model the wizard just configured, is the opposite of local-first.

RAISE THE DEFAULT and make it configurable per provider registry entry, so a slow local box and a fast hosted endpoint are not forced to share one number. Cloud kinds may keep 60s; the local kinds must not.

RED FIXTURE, both directions: a provider whose fetch takes longer than the OLD 60s default must now succeed, and one that exceeds the NEW default must still raise ProviderTimeoutError. A timeout that never fires is not a timeout.
Full gate green including e2e, counts in the commit body.

tickets.title: The creation pipeline is a synchronous HTTP request that a local model cannot finish inside any sane timeout
acceptance: RE-MEASURED 2026-08-04 (the previous wording was taken on qwen3.5-9b and overstated the case; this replaces it, and the ticket survives the correction). The timeout argument is now WRONG and must not be used to justify this: W10-57 raised the local default to 300s and made it per-entry configurable, and no run measured today came close to it — one blueprint call on qwen3.6-35b-a3b took 42s, a resume spending two calls took 73s, and a full three-phase run took ~91s. THE CONTRACT ARGUMENT IS UNTOUCHED AND IS THE REAL ONE: that is still one-and-a-half to three minutes of a synchronous HTTP request the founder must hold a browser tab open for, with no progress, no cancel and no resume.

WHY, from measurement rather than inference: a single pipeline-sized call to qwen3.5-9b on this hardware took **33 seconds and 3,088 completion tokens, of which 2,987 were reasoning**. The pipeline issues several of those sequentially (blueprint, technical slate, ticket drafts) over progressively larger prompts. There is no timeout value that is both large enough for a local reasoning model on modest hardware and small enough to still mean "something is wrong".

THE SHAPE IS THE DEFECT, not the constant. A request a user must hold a browser tab open for, for minutes, with no progress and no way to resume, is the wrong contract — and it is exactly the shape that made every earlier failure invisible: one opaque 500 at the end, with nothing to show for the work already done.

MAKE IT A JOB: `POST .../pipeline/run` accepts and returns immediately with a run id; phases execute in the background appending real events as they complete; the UI subscribes and shows per-phase progress. The event log and WebSocket transport this needs are already built and already carry board updates — this is wiring an existing spine, not new infrastructure.

PARTIAL PROGRESS MUST SURVIVE, and W10-67 already built the precedent to copy rather than invent: a run that pauses on a founder decision persists its blueprint INPUT to `<project>/.dokima/runs/<id>.json`, keeps its slates in the event-logged decisions store, and resumes by re-synthesising for free and spending only the two calls it had not yet paid for — measured at 73s, two gateway calls not three. Generalise that, do not re-solve it. Today a phase-3 failure still discards phases 0-2 entirely, so a founder who waited three minutes gets nothing.

RED FIXTURE: with a deliberately slow provider, assert the route returns promptly with a run id AND that phase-completion events land afterwards. A test that only checks the fast path would pass today and prove nothing.

tickets.title: The creation pipeline dies on a fenced JSON response — the most common shape an instruct model returns
acceptance: MEASURED IN A BROWSER against a real local model, not inferred. Registered LM Studio through Settings -> Providers, routed coding-agent/reasoning to `qwen3.6-35b-a3b`, filled all nine Describe questions with a real product idea and clicked "Build the board". The blueprint and technical-slate phases BOTH completed against the live model (~76s of real inference). The run then died with: `pipeline model port produced malformed output for phase "ticket-drafts": response was not valid JSON: Unexpected token BACKTICK, " ```json { "... is not valid JSON (HTTP 502)`.

ROOT CAUSE, read from source and confirmed by the error text itself, not guessed: `chatJson` (apps/server/src/api/pipeline/gateway-model-port/chat-json.ts) calls `JSON.parse(content)` on the raw message content with no handling for a markdown code fence. The error message quotes the model output starting with a fence — ` ```json { ` — so the model returned exactly what it was asked for, wrapped the way instruct models almost always wrap it. Ruled out: truncation at max tokens (would fail mid-string, not at offset 0 on a backtick) and reasoning-content leakage (would show a think tag, not a fence).

THIS IS NOT A MODEL-QUALITY PROBLEM AND MUST NOT BE FIXED BY PROMPTING HARDER. Every system prompt in gateway-model-port already says "respond with ONLY a JSON object". Three of them. A local model complying 95% of the time still fails the pipeline 95%-cubed of the time across three sequential phases, and the failure discards every phase before it. Tolerating a fence is the fix; asking more loudly is not.

DELIVER, IN ONE SHARED HELPER CALLED BY BOTH CALL SITES — there are two and they are identical. `chatJson` and `onboard-dispatch-port.ts:240` (the onboard/analysis path W10-45 wired to the same provider construction) each parse a model completion with a bare `JSON.parse` and raise the same `MalformedModelOutputError`; fixing only the first leaves a known-identical defect live in production. The helper strips a leading/trailing markdown fence (```json / ``` / ~~~ variants, with or without a language tag, with surrounding whitespace and any prose before it) and only then parses. The refusal must stay real — output with no JSON object in it at all still raises, with the phase named. Do NOT reach for a general "JSON repair" library: this is fence stripping, and a repairer that silently invents structure is exactly what law 4 exists to keep out of a trust boundary.

RED FIXTURE, both directions: a fenced response parses to the same object its unfenced twin does (```json, bare ```, ~~~, leading prose before the fence), AND a genuinely malformed response still raises MalformedModelOutputError naming its phase. A tolerance that tolerates everything is not a parser.
Full gate green including e2e, counts in the commit body.

tickets.title: The model picker offers 8 of 23 models the resolver then refuses — splitModelRef splits on the first slash
acceptance: READ FROM SOURCE against a real catalog, not hypothesised. `splitModelRef` (apps/server/src/api/pipeline/model-resolution.ts) implements the `<providerId>/<model>` convention by splitting on the FIRST slash. Model ids routinely contain a slash of their own: of the 23 models a live LM Studio served this machine, 8 do — `qwen/qwen3-coder-next`, `qwen/qwen3.5-9b`, `google/gemma-4-12b-qat`, `google/gemma-4-26b-a4b`, `google/gemma-4-26b-a4b-qat`, `google/gemma-4-e4b`, `nvidia/nemotron-3-nano`, `nvidia/nemotron-3-nano-omni`, `mlx-community/nemotron-3-nano-omni-30b-a3b-reasoning`.

THE FAILURE IS A REFUSAL AGAINST A SETTING THE UI ITSELF OFFERED. Picking `qwen/qwen3.5-9b` in the W10-04 Providers & Models panel stores it verbatim; `bindProvider` then reads providerId `qwen`, finds no enabled provider with that id, and throws ModelResolutionError `unknown-provider`. The panel populates that dropdown from the provider catalog it just fetched, so the product offers a model and then refuses it. Note this is the model the previous session actually ran the pipeline on — via the env fallback, which never calls splitModelRef, which is why it worked there and only breaks on the registry path W10-03 built.

DECIDE THE CONVENTION RATHER THAN PATCHING THE SYMPTOM. A first-slash split cannot distinguish a provider prefix from a vendor-namespaced model id, and no amount of care at the call site changes that. Options, to be chosen and recorded: only treat a prefix as a providerId when it matches a REGISTERED provider id (cheap, resolves every case above, keeps unprefixed ids working); or store the binding as a structured pair rather than a string; or require a delimiter that cannot occur in a model id. Whichever is chosen, the model-matrix row written by the UI must round-trip through the resolver.

RED FIXTURE: a matrix row naming a slash-containing model id from a single enabled provider resolves to that provider with the FULL model id sent on the wire (not a truncated one), and a genuinely unknown provider prefix still raises `unknown-provider`. Both directions, because a resolver that never refuses is not a resolver.
Full gate green including e2e, counts in the commit body.

Sibling: W10-59. — CLOSED 2026-08-03. CONVENTION DECIDED per acceptance 3: a prefix is a providerId only when it names a REGISTERED provider; otherwise the whole value is the model id and reaches the wire intact. `splitModelRef` now takes `knownProviderIds` as a REQUIRED argument rather than an optional convenience, because the ambiguity is not resolvable without it and a default would reintroduce the bug for whoever forgot to pass it. Recognition uses ALL registered ids, not just enabled ones, so a matrix pointing at a disabled provider still reports it rather than reinterpreting `off-box/model` as a model name and sending it to whichever provider happens to be the only enabled one — asserted. It was rewritten to assert the new convention WITH the trade stated in the test body, not deleted. The structural fix is filed as W10-68.

tickets.title: A successful board build looks like a failure — the Canvas shows empty panes until you reload by hand
acceptance: MEASURED IN A BROWSER on the run that first proved the pipeline works end to end (W10-59). "Build the board" completed successfully: 9 rows in `plan_items`, 26 events, no error. The Canvas it returned to rendered Chat, Board and Artifacts as three EMPTY panes. A manual page reload then showed all nine tickets. The run had already succeeded; the UI simply never said so.

THIS IS THE WORST POSSIBLE MOMENT FOR IT. It lands at the end of the single longest wait in the product — 91 seconds of held-open tab on this hardware, longer on slower boxes — and the payoff screen is indistinguishable from the failure the previous two sessions actually hit. A user who reloads gets their board; a user who concludes it failed and clicks "Build the board" again pays for a second full pipeline run.

A SECOND, SEPARATE LOSS ON THE SAME SCREEN: the interview answers do not survive a reload either. Returning to Describe after the run shows nine empty fields. Every answer the user typed is gone, so the natural recovery action for the first defect (reload) destroys the input for a retry. Fix or explicitly scope out, but do not leave both true at once.

ROOT CAUSE IS NOT YET ESTABLISHED — do not fix the first plausible theory. The event log and WebSocket transport already carry board updates (they are what W10-58 proposes to reuse), so the candidates are at least: the Canvas mounts before the run commits its rows; the WS subscription is not established for a project whose board was empty at mount; or the run completes without emitting the event the board listens for. Verify which, with evidence, before changing code.

RED FIXTURE: an e2e spec that runs the interview to completion against the fake-model gateway and asserts the board is non-empty WITHOUT a page reload. Note this is the same assertion W10-54 acceptance 5 still owes, and it cannot be satisfied by a spec that reloads to get green — a reload is the workaround, not the behaviour.
Full gate green including e2e, counts in the commit body.

THE EVIDENCE THAT PICKS THIS OVER THE OTHER THEORIES: all THREE panes were empty, not just the board — a data-timing, WebSocket-subscription or missing-event explanation cannot make the Chat and Artifacts panes vanish too, and a page reload fixes it because fresh state re-runs the effect. BROADER THAN FILED: the same stale-node bug applies to returning from Roster, Plan, Notifications and Trace, so this is not an interview defect at all — the interview is merely where a seven-minute wait made it unmissable. write_scope corrected accordingly BEFORE editing: the fix is in App/paneNodes.ts, and the ticket had scoped apps/web/src/onboarding/**, where the defect does not live. — write_scope widened again before editing, to AppShell.tsx: the three hooks no longer take projectId (the dependency was the bug), so their only call sites must drop the argument. The alternative — keeping a parameter the hook deliberately ignores — is a vestigial API that documents a dependency which is precisely what this ticket removed. — CLOSED 2026-08-03. Both W10-61 and the acceptance inherited from W10-54 are satisfied by one e2e spec with no page.reload() in it. Also fixed the SECOND defect this ticket named: the interview answers surviving a reload is now moot for the success path, because the user is never asked to reload — the run returns to a Canvas that renders. RED PROOF DONE TWICE, because the first was wrong: reverting to an empty dep array broke 8 specs, which is strictly worse than the shipped code and would have overstated the fixtures. Against the EXACT pre-ticket file restored from HEAD (dep [projectId]), 1 of the 2 new e2e cases fails — the one asserting the board renders without a reload — and 4 of the 5 unit fixtures fail. The Roster round-trip case passes against the old code, so it is a guard rather than a reproduction, and is reported that way.

tickets.title: There is no machine-wide provider registry — the CLI reads a global scope the pipeline resolver never looks at
acceptance: READ FROM SOURCE, both paths. `listProviders(projectPath)` (providers-store.ts) calls `getProjectSettings`, which is `loadProjectSettings` and nothing else — it reads `<project>/.dokima/settings.json` ONLY. `dokima doctor` and `dokima providers refresh` (cli/ops/providers-core.ts:43) read the same `providers` key through `getEffectiveSettings`, which loads global AND project and resolves run > project > global. The two disagree about where a provider may live.

THE CONSEQUENCE IS A CONFIGURATION THAT REPORTS HEALTHY AND DOES NOTHING. A `providers` entry written to `~/.dokima/config.json` is visible to `dokima doctor`, which will happily report it; `resolveModelTarget` sees zero providers for the project, takes the "nothing configured is a normal first-run state" branch, and silently falls back to `envTarget`. The user is told their provider is fine and gets a different model than the one they registered.

THIS IS THE EXACT DIVERGENCE providers-store.ts WAS WRITTEN TO PREVENT, one level down. Its own header: "Writing anywhere else would have created a second source of truth where the GUI and the CLI disagree about which providers exist." Reusing the key achieved that; reading it at a different SCOPE than the CLI reintroduces the same disagreement.

THE USER-FACING GAP IS THE POINT, not the internal inconsistency. Today a provider and its model must be configured per project, so registering LM Studio once does not make it the default for the next product you create — you repeat the whole registration in every new workspace. That is a defensible product decision and an indefensible accident; decide it deliberately and record which.

RED FIXTURE: a `providers` entry present ONLY at global scope resolves for a project that has no project-scope registry, and a project-scope entry still WINS over a global one of the same id (precedence is run > project > global, FR-S1). Both directions, because a global fallback that overrides an explicit project choice is a worse bug than the one being fixed.
Full gate green including e2e, counts in the commit body.
tickets.notes: Found 2026-08-03 immediately after W10-59, when the model selected through the Providers & Models panel turned out to exist only inside the one test project it was configured in. The machine-wide default that DOES work today is the env fallback (`DOKIMA_MODEL_BASE_URL` + `DOKIMA_MODEL_ID`), which `envTarget` reads and which never touches the registry — so the documented CI/fixture override is currently also the only way to set a default for every project, which is backwards. Note the model matrix has the same shape of problem and is not in this ticket scope: `listModelMatrix` reads the project state.db, so there is no global matrix at all. — DECISION RECORDED (acceptance 4 asks for one). Global-scope providers are a FALLBACK, not a default: project rows win, so a global registry can never quietly beat an explicit per-project choice. Scope-resolution reading now matches what dokima doctor already did, which is what closes the divergence. Measured honestly at close: this delivers no user-visible change on its own, because resolveModelTarget also requires matrix rows and listModelMatrix has no global scope — filed as W10-64 rather than implied by this one. Fixtures proven red against the old project-only read, not just green against the new one.

tickets.title: Nothing asserts the pipeline USES the fence-tolerant parser — reverting one line stays fully green
acceptance: THE GAP, stated exactly. W10-59 added 20 tests for `parseModelJson` in `model-json.test.ts`, all of which exercise the helper in isolation. If `chat-json.ts` is reverted to `JSON.parse(response.message.content)`, every one of those 20 stays green, the whole 3176-test suite stays green, all 61 e2e stay green — and the defect that killed every creation-pipeline run is back in production.

THIS IS THE SHAPE OF EVERY DEFECT THIS MONTH. RESUME_2026-08-03-B §3: "the missing assertion is and then it actually worked." A unit test proving a parser parses is not an assertion that the pipeline calls it.

DELIVER: one case in `gateway-model-port.test.ts` alongside its existing `startFakeGatewayServer(['not json at all'])` refusal — feed the fake gateway a FENCED valid response and assert `resolveBlueprintInput` (or any phase) returns the parsed object rather than raising. This file was deliberately left out of W10-59's write_scope, which is why this is a separate ticket rather than a reopen.
Full gate green including e2e, counts in the commit body.
tickets.notes: Filed 2026-08-03 immediately after W10-59 landed, from a review of that ticket rather than from a failure. Related honesty note on W10-59: the after-run cannot distinguish "the model emitted a fence and stripping saved it" from "the model happened to emit clean JSON that attempt" — temperature is 0 with identical prompts, so the former is very likely, but it is inference and this ticket is what would make it a measurement.

tickets.title: Register once, use everywhere is still half true — the model matrix has no global scope and no way to write one
acceptance: THE REMAINING HALF, stated exactly. W10-62 made `listProviders` read the effective settings, so a provider registered at global scope is now visible to the resolver. That alone changes NOTHING a user can see, and the ticket says so: `resolveModelTarget` short-circuits on `rows.length === 0 || providers.length === 0` (model-resolution.ts:180), and `listModelMatrix` reads the project `state.db` — there is no global matrix at all. A new product therefore still falls back to the env target however the providers are registered.

AND THERE IS NO WRITE PATH, which is why this is not a one-line mirror of W10-62. The Providers & Models panel writes matrix rows through the project-scoped settings route; nothing in the UI or the CLI can write a global matrix, so adding a global READ fallback on its own would be dead code. The scope has to be selectable where the rows are edited.

THE ACCEPTANCE TEST IS A SECOND PRODUCT, not a unit test. tickets.title: One missing field in one phase throws away the whole run — the pipeline never retries a model that almost complied
acceptance: MEASURED IN A BROWSER on a second, different product idea, with the model resolved through the env fallback and no project configuration at all. The run reached the model, the model returned well-formed JSON of the right general shape, and the run died on ONE field: `pipeline model port produced malformed output for phase "blueprint-input": "openQuestions[0].slate.recommendedId" must be a non-empty string (HTTP 502)`. The state afterwards: `plan_items 0`, `events 0` — not even a record that a run was attempted. The SAME code had completed this phase cleanly on the previous idea minutes earlier, so this is input-dependent model variance, not a systematic bug.

THE MODEL WAS NOT WRONG IN AN INTERESTING WAY. `BLUEPRINT_SYSTEM_PROMPT` asks for an `openQuestions[].slate.recommendedId`, and an empty one is a plausible reading of "I have no recommendation for this fork" — which the prompt itself half-invites by saying "Never fabricate a resolution". `requireString` rejects it, and there is no path back.

THE PRODUCT ALREADY OWNS THE MECHANISM IT IS NOT USING. W1-03 built a micro-loop whose whole purpose is criterion -> gaps -> feedback -> retry, and `packages/loop/src/anchors.ts` carries specific gap descriptions for exactly this. `gateway-model-port.ts` has no retry of any kind (grepped: zero occurrences of retry/attempt). A one-shot call to a local model, with a strict schema, across three sequential phases, and no feedback loop, is the least forgiving arrangement available on the least reliable component.

DECIDE BETWEEN TWO FIXES AND RECORD WHICH, do not do both by reflex. (a) RETRY WITH THE VALIDATION ERROR FED BACK — re-issue the phase once with the `MalformedModelOutputError` message appended, which is the micro-loop pattern and costs one extra call only on the failure path. (b) LOOSEN THE SCHEMA where the strictness is not earned — an unrecommended open question is meaningful, and `recommendedId`/`recommendedReasoning` may be legitimately absent. These are not equivalent: (b) alone still dies on the next field, (a) alone keeps a schema stricter than the domain.

RED FIXTURE: a fake gateway that returns a schema-deviating completion FIRST and a valid one second must produce a completed phase, and one that deviates every time must still raise `MalformedModelOutputError` naming the phase and the field. A retry that never gives up is a hang, not a fix.
Full gate green including e2e, counts in the commit body.

tickets.title: The blueprint prompt asks for a "key" without saying it is a slug, and a strict marker grammar then refuses the title the model writes
acceptance: MEASURED IN A BROWSER, as the failure that appeared once W10-65's retry cleared the previous one. Same idea, same model: the run got PAST blueprint-input and died with `invalid open-question key "Offline Sync & Conflict Resolution Strategy" — must match ^[A-Za-z0-9][\w.-]*$ (HTTP 422)`. Note the status: 422 from the route, not the port's 502, so it is raised after the port returned and W10-65's retry does not and should not reach it.

THE CONSTRAINT IS LOAD-BEARING — do not loosen it. `OPEN_QUESTION_KEY_RE` (packages/pipeline/src/blueprint/markers.ts:23) exists because the key becomes a bare token inside an HTML-comment sentinel, `<!-- FOUNDER-DECISION: <key> UNRESOLVED -->`, matched by a strict grammar that is deliberately fail-closed ("an unparseable marker must block the gate exactly like a genuine unresolved one"). A key containing spaces and an ampersand would break FR-P7's phase lock.

THE PROMPT IS WHAT IS WRONG. `BLUEPRINT_SYSTEM_PROMPT` asks for `openQuestions: [{key: string, ...}]` and says nothing about the format. A model given a field called "key" next to a field called "title" reasonably writes a human-readable one. The system enforces a schema stricter than the schema it describes — and that gap, not the model, is the defect.

DELIVER: state the constraint where the model can act on it — the key must match `^[A-Za-z0-9][\w.-]*$`, with a worked example (`deployment-shape`, `offline-sync`) rather than the regex alone. Consider ALSO slugifying defensively at the parse boundary and record the decision either way; a prompt is guidance and a boundary is a guarantee, and this key crosses a trust boundary into a gate.

RED FIXTURE: a completion whose open-question key is a human-readable title is handled per the decision above (rejected with the phase named, or slugified deterministically — not silently dropped), and a well-formed slug still round-trips into a marker `parseMarkers` accepts.

tickets.title: The gate correctly asks the founder to decide, and throws away the slates they would decide on

THE FOUNDER CANNOT ANSWER, WHICH IS THE DEFECT. The project state.db afterwards: `decisions 0`, `clarifications 0`, `events 0`. The slates the model produced — titles, 2-4 options each, tradeoffs, a recommendation and its reasoning — existed only in memory and were discarded with the rest of the run. The Decisions UI built in W5-13/W5-14 has nothing to show. The system asks a question it did not keep.

AND IT IS REPORTED AS A FAILURE. The interview surface renders it in the error style, prefixed "The run failed:", identical to a genuine 502. A correct decision gate presented as a crash, at the end of a seven-minute wait, with no affordance to do the thing it is asking for, is the single worst first-run outcome available — the user concludes the product is broken when it is in fact working.

DELIVER: persist the slates when the gate fires, surface them where the founder can answer (the Decisions surface already exists — this is wiring, not new machinery), and resume decomposition once they are answered rather than re-running the whole pipeline. The blueprint that produced them must survive too; re-deriving it would produce different slates and silently invalidate the answers.

tickets.title: Store the matrix binding as a structured pair — a slash in a string cannot tell a provider from a vendor namespace
acceptance: THE AMBIGUITY IS IN THE DATA MODEL, not in any call site. A matrix row stores one string and the resolver has to guess whether the part before the first slash is a providerId or a vendor namespace. `ghost/model` (a typo, or a provider since removed) and `qwen/qwen3-coder-next` (a real model id from a live LM Studio catalog) are the same shape. No parsing rule distinguishes them, so W10-60 had to pick a winner.

W10-60 PICKED THE VENDOR READING AND PAID A PRICE, which this ticket exists to refund. Consulting the registry resolves all 8 slash-carrying models in a real catalog and keeps the `copilot/` convention working, but a matrix row whose provider prefix is a typo or names a removed provider now binds to the single enabled provider instead of refusing. That regression is bounded — two or more enabled providers is still `ambiguous-provider`, a registered-but-disabled prefix is still `unknown-provider` — and it is documented in a rewritten W10-03 test rather than quietly dropped. It is still a regression.

DELIVER: `model_matrix` carries `provider_id` and `model` as separate columns, so a row says which provider it means instead of encoding it in punctuation. An absent `provider_id` keeps today's meaning (bind to the single enabled provider, ambiguous if several), so nothing has to be requalified by hand.

MIGRATE WHAT EXISTS rather than reinterpreting it lazily. Existing single-string rows must be read once and split using the same registry-consulting rule W10-60 established, so a board configured before this ticket resolves identically after it. A migration that changes which model a run calls is worse than the bug.

RED FIXTURE: a row with an explicit `provider_id` and a model whose own id contains a slash resolves to exactly that provider with the full model id intact; a row with a `provider_id` naming an unregistered provider raises `unknown-provider` again — restoring the refusal W10-60 had to trade away; and a pre-migration string row resolves to the same target before and after migrating.

tickets.title: RELEASE BLOCKER: the creation pipeline never reads the provider registry — the model you pick in the panel is not the model that runs
acceptance: READ FROM SOURCE AND CONFIRMED ON THE WIRE, twice. `pipeline-routes/index.ts:115` builds its port with `createRealGatewayPort(opts.gatewayConfig ?? resolveGatewayConfigFromEnv())` — the ENV resolver. `resolveGatewayConfigForProject`, the registry+matrix resolution W10-03 exists to provide, has exactly ONE production caller in the whole repo: `onboard-dispatch-port.ts:195`. The creation pipeline — the product's headline path, the one behind "Build the board" — never reads the provider registry or the model matrix at all.

MEASURED, not inferred. A project was configured through the Providers & Models panel (LM Studio registered and Reachable, 23 models discovered, `coding-agent`/`reasoning` set to `qwen/qwen3.5-9b`, verified persisted in `model_matrix`). A run was then started from the Describe surface against a core with NO `DOKIMA_MODEL_ID` set. LM Studio received `"model": "local-model"` — `envTarget`'s hardcoded default. Not the selected model, and not an error either.

THIS IS W10-03'S OWN HEADLINE ACCEPTANCE, UNMET ON THE MAIN PATH. That ticket is titled "Wire the seam: the model the user picks is the model that runs", and `model-resolution.ts`'s header says the resolution order exists so that an explicit selection BEATS the environment. It does — in the function. The route never calls it. W10-45 wired the onboard/analysis twin and this call site was left behind, which is the same build-then-wire gap W10_PLAN §6a traces the original defect to.

IT ALSO SILENTLY INVALIDATES EVERY MODEL-SELECTION FEATURE BUILT ON TOP. W10-01 (persisted registry), W10-02 (catalog), W10-04 (the picker), W10-60 (slash-carrying ids), W10-62 (global providers) are all correct and all unreachable from this route. A user configuring a model gets no error and no effect — the worst combination, and the reason this sat undetected through a full end-to-end browser session.

DELIVER: the run route resolves per project — `resolveGatewayConfigForProject(projectPath, ...)` with the env config as the documented fallback, exactly as `onboard-dispatch-port.ts` already does. `opts.gatewayConfig` must keep winning so the e2e fake-model gateway is unaffected. A `ModelResolutionError` must surface as a named refusal, never a silent fallback to localhost.

RED FIXTURE, and it must assert the MODEL ON THE WIRE, not the config object: a project whose matrix selects a model sends THAT model id to the fake gateway (`server.requests[0].model`), and a project with no registry still sends the env default. Asserting the resolved config would have passed all along — the config was always resolvable; nothing asked for it.

tickets.title: Providers can be READ globally but only WRITTEN per project — the other half of register-once
acceptance: THE EXACT GAP, measured in a browser. W10-62 made `listProviders` read the EFFECTIVE settings, so a global provider resolves. W10-64 did the same for the matrix AND shipped its write path. Providers never got one: `putProviders` calls `putProjectSetting` unconditionally and the panel has no scope control, so the only way to create a global provider entry is to hand-edit `~/.dokima/config.json`. A read path with no write path is the definition of dead code.

VERIFIED CONSEQUENCE: after W10-64, a second product DOES inherit the model — confirmed in the browser, `scope: "global"`, rows `coding-agent/code` and `/reasoning` both `qwen3.6-35b-a3b`, with the panel showing "These rows come from your every-project defaults". That product still shows "No providers yet", so `resolveModelTarget` hits its `providers.length === 0` branch and falls back to the env target. The model is inherited and unusable.

THIS IS W10-64 ACCEPTANCE 4, WHICH THAT TICKET COULD NOT MEET. It asks: configure a provider and a model once, create a NEW product, run the interview without touching its settings, and the run must use the configured model. The model half is done and proven; the provider half is this ticket. W10-64 was closed stating exactly that rather than self-grading the pair as complete.

DELIVER, mirroring W10-64 so the two halves cannot diverge: `PUT /providers` accepts `scope` of "project" or "global", absent means project so every existing caller is unchanged, an unknown scope is a 400; the panel gets the same "Use for every project" control; and GET reports which scope served the entries so an inherited provider is not silently editable as if it were local.

RED FIXTURE: a provider registered globally is visible to a project with no registry of its own and a run resolves through it; a project-scope entry of the same id still wins; and an unknown scope is refused. Plus the isolation guard W10-64 learned the hard way — any test writing global scope MUST pin `DOKIMA_HOME`, or it writes the developer's real `~/.dokima/config.json` (it did, once).

tickets.title: The suite reads the developer's real ~/.dokima — four tests go red the moment anyone configures a global default
acceptance: REPRODUCED, not theorised, and self-inflicted. W10-62/W10-64/W10-70 made `listProviders` and `listModelMatrix` resolve the GLOBAL scope, which lives in `~/.dokima/config.json`. Nothing in the apps/server suite pins `DOKIMA_HOME`, so every test that asserts a "nothing configured" state now reads whatever the developer has actually configured. Registering a provider through the panel to verify W10-70 turned `main` red: 4 failures — providers-store "round-trips through the SAME providers settings key", onboard-cli-integration's real-gateway run, onboard-dispatch-port's "falls back to the env config when nothing is configured (C-1)", and pipeline-routes/run.test.ts's own env-fallback case.

THE GATE WAS GREEN WHEN EACH TICKET LANDED, which is the part that matters. The failures depend on machine state that did not exist yet at commit time, so this is not a test anyone wrote badly — it is a global read introduced under tests that were written when no global scope existed. CI would have stayed green indefinitely and every developer who configured a default would have seen a broken suite.

DO NOT FIX BY DELETING THE CONFIG. `~/.dokima/config.json` is legitimate state, created through the product exactly as a user creates it, and removing it to get green would hide the fragility and destroy the evidence W10-70 was verified against.

DELIVER: pin `DOKIMA_HOME` to a throwaway directory for the whole apps/server suite via `setupFiles`, so no individual test has to remember and no future one can forget. Tests that want their own scoped home still set it themselves and must keep working. The two store test files that already pin it by hand can then say why the belt-and-braces is deliberate, or drop their local copies — decide and record which.

RED FIXTURE, and it must be honest about what it can assert: with a global provider AND a global model matrix present in the real home, the full suite passes. Verify by RUNNING it with `~/.dokima/config.json` populated, not by reasoning about it — that is exactly the check that was missing.

tickets.title: A paused run has no human path through it — the Decisions UI is never mounted, and nothing calls resume

tickets.title: The morning queue says "Nothing needs you." while a run waits on a founder decision — pending_decide_count is always 0
acceptance: MEASURED 2026-08-04, with a real creation run paused on two founder decisions and both slates status=open in the event-logged store: `GET /api/v1/projects` returned `pending_decide_count: 0` for that project, the notification centre's morning queue rendered "Nothing needs you.", and the Decide tab was empty. The one surface whose entire job is "what needs a human" was blind to the only thing that did.

THE FIELD IS A HARDCODED ZERO, NEVER A COMPUTATION. `projects/stats.ts` declares `EMPTY_STATS` with `pendingDecideCount: 0` and `computeProjectStats` returns `{ ...EMPTY_STATS, board: stats }` on its success path — so the count is literally the constant 0 for every project in every state, and no code anywhere derives it. `berthsRunning`, `heartbeatAgeMs` and `spendTodayUsd` are the same constant on the same line; whoever takes this should say which of the four they fixed rather than leave the others looking computed. The data needed is already served by `GET /api/v1/projects/:id/slates?status=open`, which the Decisions board (mounted in W10-72) renders from.

THE HEADER BADGE DEPENDS ON THE SAME NUMBER. `AppHeader` renders `decideBadgeCount` on the bell with the aria-label "Notifications, N awaiting a decision", so today it announces 0 to a screen reader while two decisions wait. Fixing the count fixes the badge with it.

DELIVER: `pendingDecideCount` is derived from the open slates rather than pinned at 0, so a project with a paused run appears in the morning queue and the Decide filter. RED FIXTURE: `apps/server/src/api/projects/` has NO test file at all today — the first one is part of this ticket. A project with one open founder slate must report a non-zero count, failing against today's code, which returns the constant no matter what is open.
tickets.notes: Split out of W10-72 rather than widened into it: W10-72 is lane ui with an apps/web-only write_scope, and this is a server-side projection. W10-72 acceptance 4 names the same measurement and explicitly leaves the wiring to a ticket of its own. — WRITE_SCOPE CORRECTED BEFORE ANY WORK: filed against board-project.ts and api/notifications/** by guess, both wrong. `pending_decide_count` is serialized in projects/cards.ts from `pendingDecideCount`, which is only ever the constant in projects/stats.ts. Verified by grep, not assumed. — write_scope widened before editing and named. Tracing the two surfaces showed this ticket has TWO halves with two different sources, which the filed scope did not cover. The Fleet card badge AND the fleet sort order come from `pendingDecideCount`, a hardcoded 0 in `projects/stats.ts`. The morning queue and the header bell come from the `notifications` table (tier=decide), and NOTHING creates a decide notification from an open slate — `refreshAndListProjectNotifications` only emits trust-graduation suggestions and promotes existing rows. Fixing one half would leave the headline symptom, the queue saying nothing needs you, exactly as it is. Both are in scope. `types.ts` came OUT of scope: the field already exists and is typed, it is simply never computed. — write_scope widened a second time and named: closing a card whose slate was answered elsewhere needs resolve.ts, whose resolveNotification is private. Adding a purpose-named export there beats duplicating its transaction (status + resolved_at + appended event, atomically) inside decide-slates.ts. — CLOSED 2026-08-04, PROVEN IN A BROWSER on a real project with one genuinely open founder slate. THREE surfaces lit up at once, two of which I had not realised were on this wire: the Fleet card shows "1 needs you"; the Fleet SORTS by the count, so Loopdemo jumped from last to FIRST in the list; the header bell shows 1 (it announced "0 awaiting a decision" to a screen reader before); and the morning queue shows a DECIDE / CLARIFICATION card naming the question and its project, where it previously said "Nothing needs you." — TWO HALVES, TWO SOURCES, both needed. The badge, the sort and the API field come from `pendingDecideCount`, which was a literal 0 in `EMPTY_STATS` and computed nowhere. The morning queue and the bell come from the `notifications` table, and NOTHING turned a slate into a notification — `refreshAndListProjectNotifications` only derived trust-graduation suggestions and promoted existing rows. Fixing one half would have left the headline symptom exactly as it was. — DERIVED ON REFRESH rather than emitted at `createSlate` time, and the reason is the product shape: slates are created by writers with no business knowing about the notification surface (the creation pipeline, the CLI, a future berth), deriving picks up slates that already existed rather than only new ones, and it stays correct when a slate is answered elsewhere because the same pass closes the card. Idempotent by construction — it reconciles against what is open rather than appending — which matters because it runs on every refresh. — THE FIXTURE THAT MATTERS drives `refreshAndListProjectNotifications`, not just the function: the four unit cases all stayed GREEN with the wiring deleted, which is precisely the gap that let W10-72, W10-74 and W10-78 ship unreachable code. The wiring case goes red when the call is removed. — WHAT I DID NOT COMPUTE, said plainly because the acceptance asked: `berthsRunning`, `heartbeatAgeMs` and `spendTodayUsd` are still the constants they always were, on the line below the one I fixed, and a fixture pins them as unimplemented rather than merely zero today. — FOUND BY DRIVING IT, filed as W10-80: the morning-queue card offers Approve/Reject, but a founder slate is "choose one of these options". Clicking Approve resolves the CARD without answering the SLATE, so the card correctly reappears on the next refresh — honest, and confusing. My change surfaced it; it was unreachable before. — write_scope widened twice mid-work and named both times: `notifications/decide-slates.ts` + test for the queue half, then `notifications/resolve.ts` to add a purpose-named export rather than duplicate its transaction. `types.ts` came out — the field was always typed, just never computed. Fixtures proven RED: 3 of 8 (2 count cases, 1 wiring case); the rest are guards — the honest-quiet state, the missing-table degrade, idempotency, and the three uncomputed fields — which must pass both ways. tickets.title: RELEASE BLOCKER: nothing an installed user has can execute a ticket — the lifecycle CLI is never built and there is no HTTP route
acceptance: MEASURED 2026-08-04 by driving the product end to end. `dokima run` on the shipped binary answers `dokima: unknown command 'run'` and prints a help text listing only boot/doctor/backup/packs/providers/service. The same is true of `board`, `claim`, `start`, `close`, `accept`, `release`, `comment` and `verify-chain`.

THE COMMANDS EXIST AND WORK. `apps/server/src/cli/index.ts` is a complete `#!/usr/bin/env node` entry that calls `runCli` and answers `usage: dokima <board|verify-chain|claim|start|close|accept|release|comment|run> ...`. Driven through `tsx` it closed a real ticket against a real project: `PLAN-T-001 close -> in_review`, then `accept -> done`, with `verify-chain` reporting `chain OK`. This is not missing machinery — it is unreachable machinery.

THE REASON IS TWO LINES OF PACKAGING. Root `package.json` has `bin.dokima` pointing at `apps/server/src/bootstrap/cli-entry.mjs`; `apps/server/package.json` declares no `bin` at all; and `apps/server/build.mjs` has exactly ONE entryPoint (`src/bootstrap/main.ts` -> `dist/main.js`), so `cli/index.ts` is never compiled into the published tarball. `bootstrap/cli.ts` wires only the ops subset and falls through to `unknown command` for everything else.

AND THERE IS NO HTTP ROUTE EITHER, so the browser cannot do it. `openapi.ts` enumerates `/api/v1/tickets/{id}/{verb}` (lifecycle verbs, which the board uses) but no run-dispatch route; `GET /api/v1/tickets/:id/runs` is read-only. `cli/run-cmd.ts`'s own comment calls itself "the same verbs a `POST /projects/{id}/runs`-shaped route WOULD call (FR-C7)" — that route was never built. Harbormaster is imported by the scheduler and the CLI, never by the API.

REACHABILITY ALONE IS NOT ENOUGH, so do not stop at "no longer unknown command". The lifecycle verbs take `--db <path>`, while `run` takes `--project <id>`. An installed user has a project id from the Fleet; they do not know the on-disk path of that project's `state.db`. A `dokima close PLAN-T-001 --db …` that is reachable and still unguessable has not delivered the journey. Every verb must accept `--project <id>` resolved through the fleet registry, with `--db` kept as the explicit escape hatch it already is.

Watch the bundle: `build.mjs` declares five externals and folding `runCli` in pulls `@dokima/harbormaster` into `dist/main.js`, so assert the build reports zero warnings and the bundle still boots.

tickets.title: A ticket the founder is not moving never moves on screen — the board is a live projection of HTTP verb calls, not of the event log
acceptance: MEASURED 2026-08-04 with the Canvas open and connected. A ticket was closed out-of-band (`dokima close PLAN-T-001 … -> in_review`, exit 0, receipt minted). The open board did not move: the card sat in In Progress indefinitely. A page reload showed In Review with a filled close-receipt dot, so the write had landed — only the push was missing.

THE CAUSE IS WHERE THE PUBLISH LIVES. `wsHub.publish('board:' + projectId, …)` is called inside the `POST /api/v1/tickets/:id/:verb` handler in `board-routes.ts`. Any writer that is not that route — the CLI, the conductor, a harbormaster berth, an agent session, a second core — appends to the event log without notifying a single connected client. The projection is of one HTTP handler, not of the log.

WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN IT LOOKS: the product's premise is agents doing work while you watch. Every state change worth watching is, by construction, made by something other than the founder's browser. On the current wiring the Canvas is live for exactly the changes the founder made themselves and stale for all the rest — and it is stale SILENTLY, with no reconnect notice and no "this board may be out of date" affordance.

DELIVER: a board change reaches connected clients regardless of which writer made it. The event log already carries a monotonic `seq` and `ws-client.ts` already sends `resume` with `last_seq` on reconnect, so the machinery for catch-up exists; what is missing is a notification path for out-of-band appends. RED FIXTURE: append a ticket transition directly to the log (not via the verb route) and assert a subscribed client receives it — failing today.

tickets.title: The decomposer accepts prose where write_scope requires globs — 8 of 8 tickets on a real board, and no validator objects
acceptance: MEASURED 2026-08-04 on two real boards built minutes apart, same prompt, same model (qwen3.6-35b-a3b), same session. Board A: every ticket has real globs — `["infrastructure/**","config/**"]`, `["src/db/schema.ts","src/types/models.ts"]`. Board B: **8 of 8** tickets have prose — `["Setup Turborepo workspace structure","Configure TypeScript strict mode and paths",…]`, `["Initialize Supabase project on free tier",…]`. The model is inconsistent and nothing downstream cares.

THE FIELDS ARE ALSO SWAPPED ON THE PROSE BOARD. The same ticket carries `acceptance: [{id:"AC-1", text:"npx supabase db push --confirm"}]` — the verify command wearing an acceptance criterion's clothes — while `verify` holds that same string. So the acceptance criteria went into `writeScope`, the verify command went into `acceptance`, and the real write scope was never produced at all.

NO VALIDATOR OBJECTS. `decompose/linter.ts` checks semantic seams only — missing package.json scope, unowned interfaces, lane overlap. There is no check that a `writeScope` entry is path-SHAPED. Worse, a prose scope makes the linter QUIETER: `findMissingPackageJsonScope` fires only when `globOverlaps(pattern, ownPackage + "/package.json")` fails to match, and prose matches nothing, so board A reported 5 violations and board B reported none. Wrong input produced a cleaner report. (`scripts/validate-plan.mjs`'s P5 glob rule guards this repo's own plan.json and never sees a generated board.)

CORRECTED 2026-08-04 BEFORE ANY WORK, because I filed this clause wrong. It said a prose scope fails "in the direction of permitting rather than refusing". It is the OPPOSITE, and the direction matters. `globToRegExp` only treats `*`/`?` specially, so a sentence compiles to `^Initialize Supabase project on free tier$` and matches no path at all; `detectScopeViolations` returns every changed path that matches NO glob, so EVERY file an agent touches is flagged out of scope and the close gate's diff-scope check (R-F4) refuses. Fail-CLOSED. The real consequence is therefore not "containment is silently disabled" but "a ticket with a prose scope can never be worked at all" — the agent does the work, the gate refuses it, the ticket auto-blocks and is released, forever. On the board this defect produced, that is 8 of 8 tickets. Still serious, still this ticket, but the honest severity is an unworkable board rather than an unsafe one.

THE FOUNDER SEES IT AND CANNOT TELL. The ticket drawer renders the prose faithfully under a "Write scope" heading, and shows the verify command under "Acceptance" — so the surface looks populated and correct while carrying neither.

DELIVER: a `writeScope` entry that is not path-shaped is a lint violation, and the ticket-drafts prompt says plainly that write_scope is file paths or globs and acceptance is criteria (the blueprint prompt got exactly this treatment in W10-66 for the same class of confusion). Decide and state whether a prose scope is a REFUSAL or a reported violation the founder can see. RED FIXTURE: a draft whose writeScope is a sentence produces a violation — failing today, where it produces silence.
tickets.notes: Found 2026-08-04 driving the product end to end in a browser, by opening the ticket drawer and noticing "Write scope" held prose. The difference is that W10-66 broke loudly (a marker grammar refused it) and this one breaks silently. — PREMISE CORRECTED BEFORE IMPLEMENTING: I asserted fail-open when filing and verified fail-closed when claiming, by reading globToRegExp and detectScopeViolations rather than repeating myself.
