tickets.title: No agentic loop exists: the whole execution engine is unexported, has no session spawner, and no Fleet project is even a git repo
acceptance: MEASURED 2026-08-04 against a real 8-ticket board with a ticket sitting `ready`. `dokima run start --project <id> --mode new_product --breakpoint never --berths 1 --actor operator` printed `run-<ts> started -> running (breakpoint=never berths=1)` and returned in under a second — on a box whose local model takes ~30s for one call, so nothing was asked of it. Twenty seconds later: board unchanged, zero new events, no berth or session process. `run-cmd.ts` confirms it — `createRun` is bookkeeping and only `command.mode === 'onboard'` goes on to dispatch; `new_product`/`feature`/`improve` fall through to `return 0`, and `--berths <n>` is validated, stored, and never read.

PIECE 1 — LANDED AS W10-78, 2026-08-04, and left here for the record because it is what made the other four invisible. `packages/harbormaster/src/index.ts` exported only `breakpoints` and `resume`; `runLandLoop`, `runClaimLoop`, `runCloseGate`, `defaultHandoffBuilder` and `createFileStopSwitch` are now on the public surface with a fixture asserting it. The remaining pieces below are unchanged and none of them is a keystroke.

PIECE 2 — THERE IS NO PRODUCTION SESSION SPAWNER. `runClaimLoop` requires a `SpawnSession`, and the only implementation in the repo is `createChildProcessSpawn` (`packages/loop/src/session.ts`), which runs an external agent CLI. Nothing outside tests calls it. `packages/loop` may not import `gateway` (ARCHITECTURE §4), so the module deliberately leaves the choice to "whoever wires this up" — and nobody has.

PIECE 3 — AND A GATEWAY CALL CANNOT BE THAT SPAWNER, which is the trap to avoid. `runSession` detects work by `git diff` in the ticket worktree (SC-01 scope violations, the Completion Manifest). A chat completion returns text and changes no files, so a gateway-backed spawn would produce zero changed paths, exhaust `maxSessionsPerTicket`, auto-block every ticket and release it back to `ready`. That path LOOKS like execution and lands nothing — worse than not wiring it. A real coding agent needs tools, i.e. an external agent CLI or a tool-using loop this repo does not have.

PIECE 4 — NO PROJECT THE FLEET CREATES CAN HOST A WORKTREE. `ClaimLoopOptions.repoRoot` is required and each ticket gets `createWorktree`, but "New Product" creates a bare directory with a `.dokima/` in it and never runs `git init`. Verified on every scratchpad project made through the UI this session. So even a fully wired loop would fail on its first claim for anything built the documented way.

DELIVER, and the ORDER matters because piece 3 is a trap: export the engine (1), then drive `run start` on a build mode through claim -> close gate -> land with an INJECTED spawner (2), `git init` new products (4), and prove the whole path under law 9 with a fake agent — a local script that edits a file in the worktree and prints a Completion Manifest, no network and no quota spend. Configuring a REAL agent command is then a settings question, not missing machinery, and is a founder decision because it spends their money. RED FIXTURE: a board with one ready ticket reaches `done` after `run start` against the fake agent — failing today, where nothing moves at all.
tickets.notes: Found 2026-08-04 driving the product end to end in a browser and then at the CLI, at the user's request for a working end-to-end. acceptance: TRANSFERRED VERBATIM FROM W10-77 acceptance 4, which closed 2026-08-04 without it because this lives in a scope that ticket never claimed: "PIECE 4 — NO PROJECT THE FLEET CREATES CAN HOST A WORKTREE. `ClaimLoopOptions.repoRoot` is required and each ticket gets `createWorktree`, but 'New Product' creates a bare directory with a `.dokima/` in it and never runs `git init`. tickets.title: Dokima's own agent session: a tool loop that produces a Completion Manifest
acceptance: (FR-H6) DELIVER a `SpawnSession` (the `@dokima/loop` contract `runSession` already takes) that is backed by the GATEWAY rather than a child process: render the HANDOFF, send it with the tool schema through the role's configured model, execute the returned tool calls against the ticket worktree, feed results back, and iterate until the model emits a Completion Manifest or the budget stops it. IT LIVES IN `packages/harbormaster`, corrected by a challenge pass before any code. The first draft put it in `apps/server`, justified by "`packages/loop` may not import `gateway`, so no package can host it" — which is false: harbormaster already DECLARES `@dokima/gateway` and `@dokima/loop` in its own package.json, and it already owns `runClaimLoop`/`runLandLoop`, the callers that consume a `SpawnSession`. Putting it in the app would have pushed the product's core loop out of the packages layer for a reason that was not true.

THE TOOL SET IS CLOSED AND LEAST-PRIVILEGE (SC-18), AND IT REUSES `packages/mcp` — also corrected by the challenge pass. W6-04 already ships per-role allowlists, an approval policy and audited tool-call events (`setRoleAllowlist`, `decideToolCall`, `requestToolCall`, `DynamicApprovalPolicy`); the first draft specified a parallel mechanism beside it. The set is read, list, search, write, edit, commit and the ticket's own declared `verify` — no free-form shell, no network, no installs. The model chooses tool CALLS; it never chooses the tool SET. NOTE: harbormaster does not currently declare `@dokima/mcp`, which is part of W11-05's seam. — AND CONTAINMENT IS PART OF LEAST PRIVILEGE, which is the only reason this ticket did not land: In `agent-session/fs-tools.ts`, `assertRealWithinWorktree` calls `realpathOfNearestAncestor`, which starts at `path.dirname(absPath)` and reassembles the leaf component through `path.join` WITHOUT resolving it. A pre-existing leaf symlink pointing outside the worktree therefore passes containment and the following `fs.writeFile` follows it (Node has no O_NOFOLLOW default) — a full sandbox breakout on the trust boundary, found independently twice: the per-ticket reviewer verified it empirically at 2026-08-05T20:49Z (the function returns ALLOWED for `worktree/evil.txt -> /outside/leak.txt`) and the wave-W11 security pass confirmed it in the source at 20:53Z. FIX: attempt `fs.realpath()` on the FULL target first and check containment against that; fall back to nearest-ancestor resolution only when the leaf genuinely does not exist (the write-new-file case). RED FIXTURE: a pre-existing leaf symlink inside the worktree pointing outside it must make `write` and `edit` throw `ToolPathEscapeError` — failing today, where the write succeeds. Note that attempt 1 already shipped one symlink hardening commit that did NOT cover this case; a fix that only re-checks the ancestor is the same bug again.

EVERY CALL GOES THROUGH THE GATEWAY, which is the entire point of D-023 — the role→model matrix decides the model, the R0–R4 ladder can escalate, the W2-07 breakers can break, and the spend ledger sees every token. RED FIXTURE: after a session, the run's spend is non-zero and attributable to the role, which is exactly what a shelled-out CLI could never provide.

THE SESSION COMMITS ITS OWN WORK, and this is the correction that would otherwise have sunk the ticket. `runCloseGate` READS commits (`commitsSince`) and refuses with "no commits found on the ticket branch since its fork point" when there are none — it does not create them; its own comment calls them "the untrusted, already-exited session's own commits". The first draft's tool set had no commit tool, so every session built to it would have been refused by the gate 100% of the time. `commit` is therefore a first-class tool, scoped to the ticket branch inside the worktree.

RED FIXTURE for the loop itself, against the fake gateway (law 9): a scripted sequence of tool calls edits a file in the worktree, commits nothing, and returns a manifest — and the EXISTING close gate accepts it unchanged. If the gate needs changing to accept our own agent, that is a finding to report, not a licence to loosen it.
AND A SESSION THAT NEVER CONVERGES MUST STOP (T-27): assert an iteration/budget cap produces a parked ticket with evidence rather than an unbounded loop.
notes: The piece W10-77 named and could not build: its acceptance 3 said a gateway CALL cannot be an agent because runSession detects work by git diff and a completion changes no files. True of a completion, false of a tool loop — this is the resolution, and W10-77 should be read alongside it. — REWRITTEN BY A CHALLENGE PASS 2026-08-04, before a line was written: placement was wrong (harbormaster, not apps/server), the tool layer duplicated packages/mcp, and the tool set could not commit — which the close gate requires. CLAUDE.md law 1 calls that a schema bug to report, not route around, so the dependency declaration stays W11-05s and this ticket now depends on it. — round 2 of the challenge pass also corrected which fake this uses: the acceptance said the fake gateway, but that is the HTTP one in apps/web/e2e/fixtures, which this ticket does not own and which could not emit tool calls anyway until W11-01. — CONSEQUENCE OF W11-05, recorded 2026-08-04 so this does not surface as a confusing mid-ticket failure: W11-05 made package.json authoritative, corrected the ARCHITECTURE matrix to match todays declarations, and added a validate-plan P10 check that FAILS when a package declares a dependency the matrix forbids. The corrected matrix does NOT permit harbormaster -> mcp, and harbormaster does not declare it. So reusing packages/mcp for the tool allowlist now requires an explicit matrix amendment AND the declaration, together, as a deliberate architectural change — not a dependency add. Decide that first; a P10 failure mid-implementation reads like a broken validator rather than an unmade decision.

tickets.title: OpenAiProvider.chatStream silently drops tools — the exact thing FR-G9 says an adapter must never do
acceptance: (FR-G9) RAISED BY THE CONDUCTOR'S OWN REVIEWER as a MEDIUM advisory on W11-01, and verified independently before filing: `openai.ts` contains a hand-duplicated copy of the OpenAI wire format in `streamEvents()`, which W11-01 did not touch. It never serializes `request.tools` and never parses `choice.delta.tool_calls`, so tool calling silently no-ops on the cloud OpenAI streaming path. Grepping the file for `tools` returns a single `case 'tool_calls':` — a finish-reason mapping, nothing more.

IT CONTRADICTS THE REQUIREMENT W11-01 SHIPPED. FR-G9 says in terms: "an adapter that cannot do tools must refuse the field rather than silently drop it." This drops it. A requirement violated by the same wave that introduced it is worse than one not yet met, because the contract now claims a guarantee the adapter does not keep.

AND THE NEW HEADER COMMENT IS MISLEADING, which is the part most likely to cost someone an afternoon: `providers/types.ts` says `openai.ts` "delegates to it", true only for `chat()` with streaming disabled — `chatStream()` always uses the local duplicate regardless of the `streamEnabled` flag. Fix the comment or fix the delegation; do not leave prose that reads as a guarantee.

NOT REACHABLE FROM PRODUCTION TODAY, and say so rather than overstating: `gateway-model-port/provider.ts` refuses to construct the `openai` kind at all (`kind-not-constructible`), so nothing in the running product can hit this. It is live PUBLIC API (`createOpenAiProvider`/`chatStream`, exercised by `openai.test.ts`) and will bite whichever ticket wires the cloud adapter up for real.

DELIVER either honestly: make `chatStream` serialize and parse tools like `oai-compat` now does, OR make it refuse a request carrying `tools` with a named error. Both satisfy FR-G9; silently continuing does not. If the duplication is the root cause, deleting it in favour of real delegation is the better fix and should be said out loud rather than assumed.
RED FIXTURE: a `chatStream` call carrying `tools` either round-trips them or throws — failing today, where it returns a normal stream and the caller never learns the field was ignored.

tickets.title: The conductor can lint a ticket's scope at filing time and Dokima has every such rule switched off — W10-68 self-blocked twice for want of one
acceptance: THE EVIDENCE IS TWO IDENTICAL SELF-BLOCKS ON ONE TICKET, both correct, both avoidable at filing time. W10-68 blocked 2026-08-04 because its write_scope could not reach `bindProvider`; the scope was widened; it blocked again 2026-08-05 because acceptance 3 requires a new SQL column and no `packages/events/migrations/*` glob was in scope. THE MACHINERY ALREADY EXISTS AND THIS REPO HAS IT OFF, which is the actual finding — verify it rather than taking this on trust: `scripts/conductor-lib/lint-rules.mjs` exports `testSiblingWarning` and `pageMountWarning`, `scripts/conductor/lint.mjs` calls both plus `migrationCollisions`, and every one of them is gated on a config key (`CONFIG.testSibling`, `CONFIG.pageMount`, `CONFIG.migrationVersions`) that `scripts/conductor-lib/config.mjs` defaults to `null` and `conductor.config.json` never sets. They were built for Kryptkeeper and Dokima never enabled them. `testSiblingWarning` skips `done` tickets, so switching them on costs a handful of warnings on the open board, not 185.

ADD THE MISSING RULE, modelled on `testSiblingWarning` (same file, same shape, same `status === 'done'` guard, same config-key gate so a ported repo without migrations is unaffected): when a ticket's acceptance text demands a schema change — a new column or table — but no `write_scope` glob covers the project's migrations directory, warn at lint time. The precedent for what a correctly-filed ticket looks like is on the board already: W0-05 (`migrations/**`), W3-03 (`migrations/*runs*`, `*clarifications*`), W5-13 (`migrations/*decisions*`).

DO NOT SOLVE THIS BY LOOSENING THE MAKER PROMPT, and record the reasoning so the next person does not re-open it. `conductor.config.json`'s `alwaysOk` does list `packages/events/migrations/**`, which makes it look as if the maker was allowed to write one — but `alwaysOk` is a GATE-SIDE amnesty consumed by the conductor's gates chapter, and the maker never sees it. Teaching MASTER_PROMPT.md about `alwaysOk` would have stopped both blocks, and both blocks were RIGHT: the same sentence that would have unblocked W10-68 licenses silent scope drift on every other ticket. The fix belongs at filing time, not in the maker's instructions.

RED FIXTURE: a synthetic ticket whose acceptance says 'add a `provider_id` column' with a write_scope containing only application files produces exactly one warning; the same ticket with a migrations glob added produces none; a `done` ticket in the first shape produces none. DECIDE `testSibling` AND `pageMount` EXPLICITLY IN THE SAME CHANGE rather than leaving them silently null: either enable them for Dokima with the globs this repo actually uses, or record in `conductor.config.json` why they stay off here. A dormant rule that nobody knows is dormant is worse than no rule.

tickets.title: alwaysOk exempts migrations by path, not by git status — any ticket can rewrite a shipped migration in place and the scope gate stays silent
acceptance: (C-6) RAISED AS HIGH BY THE WAVE-W11 SECURITY PASS and verified at the source before filing: `scripts/conductor/gates.mjs` computes `changed` from `git diff --name-only main...branch` and exempts anything matching `ALWAYS_OK`. That is pure path matching with NO added-vs-modified distinction, so `packages/events/migrations/**` — exempted since 2026-07-16 so that any ticket adding a table can drop in a new numbered file — also lets any ticket EDIT an already-shipped migration in place without ever tripping the out-of-scope gap.

WHY THAT PARTICULAR HOLE IS THE DAMAGING ONE, rather than a tidiness complaint: an in-place edit to a committed migration silently does not re-apply to any `state.db` that already ran it (`applyMigrations` keys off `PRAGMA user_version` plus the file's numeric prefix). So the change appears applied in a fresh checkout and CI, and is absent on every existing project database. W10-68's own notes reason through this at length. The append-only numbered-file authority IS the invariant, and the gate that should protect it is blanket-open exactly there.

DELIVER the narrower exemption: read `git diff --name-status` and exempt only status `A` under the migrations glob, keeping `M` and `D` on an existing numbered file as out-of-scope unless that path is explicitly in the ticket's `write_scope`. An equivalent dedicated check is acceptable if it is stated why it was preferred.

SCOPE THE FIX TO THIS PROPERTY, not to alwaysOk in general. The other alwaysOk entries (the board, the lockfile, tsconfig) are genuinely modify-in-place infra and must keep working; a rule that exempts only additions would break every one of them. The added-vs-modified distinction belongs to append-only paths, so it needs to be expressible per-entry rather than globally.

RED FIXTURE: a branch that ADDS `packages/events/migrations/999_x.sql` with no migrations glob in write_scope still passes the scope gate; the same branch MODIFYING an existing committed migration fails it with that path named; and a ticket whose write_scope explicitly covers that existing file passes. Assert through the conductor's integration test, which already drives real branches.

REPORT WHETHER THE HOLE WAS EVER USED, since the history is available and the answer is cheap: `git log --diff-filter=M -- packages/events/migrations/` over the project's life. If some ticket did rewrite a shipped migration, that is a data-integrity finding to file separately, not something to fix inside this ticket.

tickets.title: Migration 013 trades a loud error for silent data loss — a re-applied recreate resets every provider_id it was written to preserve
acceptance: (C-6) RAISED AS A MEDIUM ADVISORY ON W10-68 by the conductor's reviewer, which APPROVEd anyway because advisories do not block a land — so this reached main. Reproduced independently before filing rather than taken on the reviewer's word: applying `013_model_matrix_provider.sql` to a seeded `model_matrix`, setting `provider_id='lm-studio'`, then applying the same file again returns `provider_id: null`. The recreate's `INSERT INTO model_matrix_new (role, task_type, model, fallback, updated_at) SELECT ...` never carries `provider_id` across.

IT CONTRADICTS ITS OWN COMMENT, which is what makes it costly rather than merely wrong: the file says the recreate 'keeps applyMigrations able to reapply this file to a db whose provider_id column is already present without erroring.' It does avoid the error — by silently reverting exactly the data the ticket existed to introduce. W10-68's own acceptance says a migration that changes which model a run calls is worse than the bug it fixes; this is that, one level down.

UNDERSTAND WHY IT IS SHAPED THIS WAY BEFORE CHANGING IT, because the first shape was correct and got rejected for a different reason. W10-68's attempt 1 used a plain `ALTER TABLE model_matrix ADD COLUMN provider_id`. That made `boot-sequence.test.ts`'s rewound-`user_version` fixture re-apply the migration and hit 'duplicate column name'. The maker was out of scope for that test file, so it reshaped the migration instead. The reshape is the defect. The honest question this ticket must answer is which invariant is real.

DECIDE AND STATE IT, rather than patching the SQL until the suite is green. Either (a) migrations are genuinely re-appliable, in which case 013 must preserve `provider_id` across the recreate and `db.test.ts` gets a fixture proving a populated column survives re-application; or (b) they are not, `user_version` is the sole authority, and the boot-sequence fixture that rewinds it without undoing the migration's effect is the thing to fix. DATABASE.md's forward-only claim is evidence for (b) but does not settle it — say which reading was taken and why.

RED FIXTURE: seed `model_matrix` with a populated `provider_id`, apply migration 013 a second time, and assert the value survives (under reading a) or that re-application is refused outright rather than silently succeeding (under reading b). Failing today, where it returns NULL and reports success.

SCOPE NOTE, checked before filing so the maker does not discover it mid-session: `packages/events/src/migrate.ts` and `apps/server/src/bootstrap/boot-sequence.test.ts` are both in this write_scope precisely because either reading may need them — W10-68 could reach neither, which is why it reshaped the SQL instead. The one collision found was real and is resolved by LANE, not by narrowing: W10-58 (ui) claims `packages/events/src/**`, which covers `migrate.ts` and `db.test.ts`, so filing this as `infra` produced a P8 cross-lane overlap. Lane set to `ui` to match — same-lane tickets never run in parallel, which is the actual constraint wanted here, and it is the same reasoning W10-68's notes record for pairing with W10-64. Narrowing the scope instead would have reproduced W10-68's exact defect: a ticket that cannot reach the file its fix must live in.

tickets.title: The agent session's tool results are neither redacted nor honest about what they dropped
acceptance: (FR-S2, SC-06) VERIFY OUTPUT REACHES THE MODEL WITHOUT PASSING THE REDACTION LAYER THAT EXISTS. `verifyTool` (git-tools.ts) puts the ticket's verify-command stdout/stderr into the tool-result text that is appended to `messages` and sent to the routed model on the next turn — which may be a cloud provider. `@dokima/shared` already exports `redactString`/`redactDeep` (SC-06, W3-13) and `renderHandoff` already runs `redactDeep` over every handoff, so the session's OTHER path into a prompt is covered and this one is not. CLAUDE.md law 8 says secrets never reach prompts; a failing test run that prints a connection string or a token in its output is the ordinary case, not a contrived one.

CORRECT THE ADVISORY THAT RAISED IT, because repeating a wrong detail into a ticket is how folklore starts: the reviewer described the output as 'raw, untruncated'. It is NOT untruncated — git-tools.ts:15-19 caps it at `MAX_OUTPUT_CHARS = 4000` with a `\u2026(truncated)` marker. Truncation is not redaction and the substantive finding stands, but the fix is to add a redaction pass, not to add a cap that is already there.

SECOND SUBJECT, SAME PRINCIPLE — `fs-search.ts`'s `walk()` swallows per-file `fs.readFile` failures with a bare `catch { continue; }` and surfaces no counter. The same function is otherwise deliberate about honest degradation (it reports `matchMode` and `skippedLongLines`), so a directory the session cannot read produces search results that are silently incomplete and indistinguishable from a genuine no-match. An agent that believes it searched the tree and did not is a correctness problem, not a cosmetic one.

DELIVER BOTH AS THE SAME RULE: a tool result states what it contains and what it dropped. Redact verify output through the shared layer, and give `searchTool`'s response an unreadable-file count alongside the existing degrade fields. Where redaction removes something, say so in the result rather than silently shortening it.

RED FIXTURE for each: a verify command whose stdout contains a credential-shaped string produces a tool result with the secret replaced and the redaction stated; and a search over a directory containing one unreadable file returns results WITH a non-zero unreadable count rather than a clean empty match. Both failing today.

SCOPE NOTE: `fs-tools.test.ts` is in scope because `fs-search.ts` is covered by that suite rather than a sibling of its own — checked before filing so this ticket cannot self-block for want of a test file, which cost W10-68 two sessions.

tickets.title: The agent session's tool loop cannot talk to a real provider — ChatMessage has no tool role and no toolCalls echo
acceptance: (FR-G9, C-1) DISCLOSED BY W11-03's MAKER IN A FILE COMMENT rather than by a failing test, and verified at the source before filing: gateway-session.ts's tool loop echoes tool calls and results back through mcp-wiring.ts's runToolCalls, which satisfies the fake-provider harness and W11-03's own red fixtures — but `ChatRole` in providers/types.ts:9 is `'system' | 'user' | 'assistant'` with no `'tool'`, and `ChatMessage` carries no `toolCalls` field to echo an assistant turn back. `toolCalls` exists only on `ChatResponse` (types.ts:62). So a real OpenAI-compatible provider cannot be given the conversation the loop produces.

THIS IS THE FAILURE MODE LAW 9 MAKES EASY TO MISS, which is why it is worth its own ticket rather than a line in someone's notes: everything is green against the fake gateway, and the first thing that breaks is the first real run. Dokima's own agent session is currently local-fixture-only for multi-turn tool use, and nothing in the suite says so.

DELIVER the round trip: `ChatRole` gains `'tool'`; `ChatMessage` gains the fields an assistant tool-call turn and a tool-result turn need (`toolCalls` on the assistant turn, a tool-call id on the tool turn); both OpenAI-compatible adapters serialize and accept them. Follow W11-06's precedent for where shared wire helpers live — types.ts, not duplicated per adapter.

COORDINATE WITH W11-07, which is queued against the same file for the opposite reason (it deletes oai-compat.ts's private duplicates of the wire helpers in favour of the exported pair). Same lane, so they cannot run in parallel; whichever lands second should say in its commit body what it had to rebase over. Do not silently re-add a duplicate helper here.

RED FIXTURE: a two-turn exchange — assistant returns tool_calls, the caller sends back a tool-role message carrying the result, the provider produces a final answer — round-trips through oai-compat and openai against a RECORDED fixture (never a live call, C-1). Failing today, where the message shape cannot even be constructed.

SAY WHAT REMAINS OUT OF SCOPE rather than implying the loop is then production-ready: this ticket makes the wire format expressible. Whether harbormaster's session actually drives a cloud provider end to end is a separate claim needing its own evidence.

tickets.title: runCloseGate checks the manifest against the diff but never the diff against write_scope — the escape-hatch runner has no equivalent guard
acceptance: (SC-17, C-2/C-3) FILED BY W11-03's MAKER AS AN EXPLICIT HANDOFF, because `packages/harbormaster/src/loop-gates.ts` sits outside that ticket's write_scope (`agent-session/**` only). `runCloseGate` checks only that `manifest.files` is a SUBSET of the real diff/commit set — that the session did not claim work it did not do. It never checks the reverse: that the real diff/commit set stays INSIDE `ticket.writeScope`. A session that changed more than it declared passes.

IT IS ALREADY CLOSED FOR ONE RUNNER AND OPEN FOR THE OTHER, which is the whole point of filing it: W11-03's `refuseIfSessionExceededScope` means a violating gateway-backed session never produces a manifest and never reaches `runCloseGate` at all. But `createChildProcessSpawn`, the spawner in the loop package — D-023's escape-hatch runner, the one that shells out to an external CLI — has no equivalent guard and relies on `runCloseGate`'s asymmetric check alone.

DELIVER the symmetric check at the gate itself, as defense in depth across EVERY `SpawnSession` implementation rather than per-runner: real `changedPaths`/`committedFiles` checked against `ticket.writeScope` via `checkWriteScope` and `HARD_EXCLUSIONS` (`@dokima/git`, the same functions both existing checks already use — do not write a third scope matcher), refusing close on any violation.

THE GATE IS THE RIGHT PLACE PRECISELY BECAUSE IT IS OUTSIDE THE SESSION. W11-03's retry had to fix exactly this confusion once already: its first attempt satisfied 'the out-of-session diff' with `commitTool`'s own check, which the untrusted model reaches only by choosing to call it. A check the session can decline to invoke is not a gate (Law 4).

RED FIXTURE: a close attempt whose real diff contains a path outside `ticket.writeScope` is refused even when `manifest.files` is a perfect subset of that diff — i.e. an honest manifest that under-reports nothing but whose underlying work escaped scope. Plus one shape from `HARD_EXCLUSIONS` (`.github/workflows/**`). Both failing today.
DO NOT REGRESS THE EXISTING ASYMMETRIC CHECK while adding its mirror; the subset test catches a different lie (claiming work not done) and both must hold.

tickets.title: Verify-output redaction is pattern-only — a secret whose shape SECRET_PATTERNS does not know still reaches the model
acceptance: (FR-S2, SC-06) W11-11 CLOSED THE PATH AND LEFT A RESIDUAL IT NAMED HONESTLY, in a KNOWN LIMITATION block at git-tools.ts:17-23: `redactString` runs there with NO `secretValues`, so only known-shape patterns (SECRET_PATTERNS: gh/AWS/OpenAI-style keys, PEM blocks, DB connection strings) are caught. The exact-value pass that `renderHandoff` gets via `collectSecretValues(vault, projectDir)` is absent, because threading it needs a vault handle on `AgentSessionToolContext` — out of W11-11's write_scope.

WHAT THAT LEAVES EXPOSED, stated plainly rather than as a theoretical gap: a credential that does not match a known shape — a bespoke internal token, a rotated key with a new prefix, a password — printed by a failing verify command still reaches the routed model's next turn, which may be a cloud provider. Law 8 says secrets never reach prompts, and the session's OTHER path into a prompt already has both passes.

DELIVER the exact-value pass on this path too: `AgentSessionToolContext` carries the secret values (or the vault handle to collect them), `gateway-session.ts` supplies them where it constructs `toolCtx` (:183), and `verifyTool` passes them to `redactString` alongside the pattern set. Scope pre-checked before filing: `collectSecretValues` is exported from `@dokima/shared`'s secrets barrel and harbormaster already declares `@dokima/shared`, so no dependency or ARCHITECTURE matrix change is needed.

PRESERVE W11-11'S ORDERING, which is load-bearing and easy to undo by accident: redaction runs over the FULL untruncated text BEFORE the MAX_OUTPUT_CHARS cap, so a secret cannot leak half-matched across the cut point. Any refactor here keeps that order, and the result keeps stating both `redacted` and `truncated`.

RED FIXTURE: a verify command whose stdout contains a vault-registered value that matches NO pattern in SECRET_PATTERNS (e.g. a plain word registered as a secret) comes back redacted, with `redacted: true`. Failing today — W11-11's fixture uses a credential-SHAPED string, which the pattern pass already catches, so this ticket's fixture must deliberately not look like a credential.

SAY WHETHER THE SAME GAP EXISTS ON ANY OTHER TOOL RESULT rather than fixing only the one that was reported: the search, read and git tools all return content the model sees next turn. If they need the same pass, do it here; if they do not, say why.

tickets.title: Anthropic and Vertex must refuse a tool-role message with a named error, not be widened to mis-serialize one
acceptance: (FR-G9) UNBLOCKS W11-12, WHICH SELF-BLOCKED WITH ITS WORK COMPLETE AND GREEN. Adding 'tool' to `ChatRole` makes workspace typecheck fail at exactly two out-of-scope sites: `anthropic-helpers.ts:50` (`splitSystem`'s `rest.push({role: m.role, ...})`, typed `Array<{role: 'user'|'assistant'}>`) and `vertex-chat.ts:58` (`mapRole(message.role)`, accepting only 'user'|'assistant'). Both narrow on ChatRole-minus-'system' and now see the new member. Reproducible from repo state: the implementation and its passing tests are committed on `blocked/w11-12`.

WIDENING THE ANNOTATIONS WOULD BE THE BUG, NOT THE FIX, and this is the whole reason a separate ticket exists rather than a two-character edit. Anthropic sends tool results as `tool_result` content blocks INSIDE a user-role message carrying `tool_use_id`; `splitSystem`'s return shape (`Array<{role, content: string}>`) has nowhere to put a `toolCallId`, so accepting 'tool' there would map a tool-result turn to plain user text and silently drop the id. Gemini carries tool results as `functionResponse` parts, not text parts — same silent drop if `mapRole`'s signature were merely widened. Either would type-check, look done, and be wrong on a real run.

DELIVER THE REFUSAL, which FR-G9 already sanctions: W11-06's acceptance blessed 'refuse the field with a named error' as an equally valid delivery to real serialization. tickets.title: A misconfigured external agent silently becomes the built-in one, and the test that covers it is named for a refusal it does not assert
acceptance: (FR-H6) THE TEST NAME CLAIMS A REFUSAL IT DOES NOT ASSERT, raised as a LOW advisory on W11-04 and read in full before filing: `run-build.test.ts:195` is titled 'an empty external command (misconfigured setting) refuses rather than spawning nothing' and asserts `expect(code).toBe(0)` — success, the built-in agent ran. Its own inline comment is honest about this ('parseAgentRunnerSetting already degrades an empty `command` to the built-in default'), so only the title lies. A title that names a guarantee the body does not check is how a codebase comes to believe it is covered.

THE BEHAVIOUR UNDERNEATH IS THE REAL QUESTION, and this ticket exists to settle it rather than to rename a test: `parseAgentRunnerSetting` (settings-types.ts:239) degrades `{kind: 'external', command: ''}` to the built-in agent SILENTLY. A user who chose an external runner and mistyped its command gets a different agent than the one they picked, with no signal — while W11-04's whole point was that choosing the external runner must state plainly what it gives up. Silent substitution is the inverse of that.

DECIDE AND SAY WHICH, rather than patching the name: either (a) the degrade is right, in which case it must be VISIBLE — a warning on the run and a settings-surface indication that the configured runner was not used — and the test is renamed to what it actually proves; or (b) an empty command is a misconfiguration that should refuse, matching the W10-77 contract W11-04 replaced only for the NOT-CONFIGURED case, not the MISCONFIGURED one. Note that those are different cases and W11-04 only ruled on the first.

WHICHEVER IS CHOSEN, THE TEST NAME MUST MATCH THE ASSERTION. If (a), the test is 'an empty external command degrades to the built-in agent and says so'; if (b), it keeps its name and finally earns it.

RED FIXTURE follows the decision: under (a) the run's output/log contains the substitution notice and the settings surface reflects it; under (b) the run exits non-zero with a message naming the empty command. Either way, assert the user-visible signal — not just the exit code, which is what made the current test's name and body diverge without anything failing.

tickets.title: SC-01's hard exclusions are matched before the path is resolved — an ancestor symlink in write_scope reaches .git
acceptance: (C-2/C-3, SC-01) RAISED AS CRITICAL BY THE WAVE-11 SECURITY PASS and verified by reading the write path before filing. `writeTool` (fs-tools.ts:114-127) runs in this order: `refuseIfHardExcluded(relPath)` on the SURFACE path, then `resolveOrRefusal` (realpath containment), then `refuseIfOutsideScope(relPath, ...)` on the SURFACE path again — and finally `fs.writeFile(resolved.abs, ...)` on the RESOLVED path. `editTool` (:136-149) is identical. So both gates judge one path and the write lands on another.

THE ESCAPE THAT MAKES IT CRITICAL: a symlink whose surface path is inside the ticket's write_scope but which resolves into an excluded directory INSIDE the same worktree. `packages/foo/link -> ../../.git` makes `packages/foo/link/hooks/pre-commit` pass the exclusion check (it does not match `.git/**`), pass containment (`.git` IS inside the worktree root), and pass the scope check (the surface path is in scope) — then writes a git hook, which executes on the next commit. W11-02 closed the leaf-symlink hole in containment; this is the same class one gate to the left, and containment cannot catch it because the target is legitimately inside the worktree.

DELIVER the check on the path that is actually written: re-run `matchesAnyGlob(..., HARD_EXCLUSIONS)` against the RESOLVED path (relative to the worktree root) after `resolveOrRefusal`, not only against the surface path. Keep the surface check too — it gives a better refusal message for the ordinary case and costs nothing.

CONSIDER WHETHER write_scope NEEDS THE SAME TREATMENT and say what you concluded either way: `refuseIfOutsideScope` also matches the surface path, so a symlink inside scope pointing at another in-worktree path outside scope has the same shape. It is a lesser breach than reaching `.git`, but it is the same defect.

RED FIXTURE per gate: with `link -> ../../.git` planted inside the worktree and `link/**` inside write_scope, `write` and `edit` must both throw rather than create `.git/hooks/pre-commit`. Failing today. Plant the symlink with `fs.symlink`, not by shelling out.

tickets.title: agentRunner.command chooses the binary the host spawns and the settings PUT validates nothing about it
acceptance: (C-2/C-3, FR-S2) RAISED AS CRITICAL + HIGH BY THE WAVE-11 SECURITY PASS, verified at the source: `resolveAgentRunner` uses `agentRunner.command` verbatim as the binary spawned on every subsequent build run, and that setting is written through the generic `PUT /projects/{id}/settings` and `PUT /settings/global` handlers, which validate nothing per key except `CONSENT_GATED_KEYS` — a set containing exactly `['copilotEnabled']` (scope-routes.ts:44). `parseAgentRunnerSetting` checks only that `command` is a string: no allowlist, no length cap, no shape constraint.

THE ASYMMETRY IS THE ARGUMENT: this codebase already has a mechanism for exactly this problem, and it is applied to a LOWER-stakes key. `refuseConsentGatedKey` exists because, in its own comment, 'a caller could PUT straight through it' — and it guards whether Copilot is enabled. Choosing which executable the host runs is a strictly larger decision and has no equivalent gate.

DELIVER a per-key gate on `agentRunner` in the same shape as the consent gate rather than a new mechanism: the PUT path refuses or requires explicit confirmation for a change to the spawned command, and `parseAgentRunnerSetting` constrains it (at minimum a length cap and a refusal of shell metacharacters; an operator allowlist is better if one can be expressed). Say which you chose and why.

DO NOT BREAK THE FEATURE WHILE SECURING IT: W11-04 makes the external CLI a legitimate, supported choice, and W11-18 makes a misconfigured one refuse. A gate that blocks a deliberate operator choice is wrong; one that lets an unattended writer silently repoint the binary is also wrong. The distinction to encode is who is asking, not whether the value is unusual.

RED FIXTURE: a PUT that changes `agentRunner.command` without whatever confirmation is chosen is refused with a named error, asserted through the real route rather than the parser alone; and a value carrying shell metacharacters is rejected by `parseAgentRunnerSetting`.
SCOPE PRE-CHECKED: `scope-routes.ts` has no test sibling of its own; `settings-routes.test.ts` is the suite that drives those PUTs and is in scope, so this cannot self-block for want of a test file.

tickets.title: The search ReDoS guard cannot see backreferences — (a+)\1+ walks straight past it
acceptance: (SC-18) RAISED AS HIGH BY THE WAVE-11 SECURITY PASS and verified: `isUnsafeSearchPattern` counts quantifiers that directly follow a closing `)` or appear as raw `*`/`+`/`{` outside a character class. It has no notion of a backreference — `grep -c backref fs-search.ts` returns 0. `(a+)\1+` is a textbook catastrophic-backtracking pattern and matches none of the existing shapes: `\1` is not a raw quantifier and does not follow `)`.

THIS IS THE THIRD PASS OVER THE SAME GUARD, which is the reason to fix the category rather than the instance. W11-02 bounded the obvious nested quantifier, then immediately shipped a second commit for the adjacent-quantifier gap the first fix missed. A third hand-rolled shape would be the same bet a third time.

PREFER A CATEGORICAL FIX over another heuristic clause if one is available in-scope: refuse backreferences outright (the search tool has no need of them), or bound execution rather than shape — a time or step budget on the match, which is immune to whatever the next unanticipated pattern is. If a heuristic is kept, say why the categorical option was rejected.

RED FIXTURE: `(a+)\1+` is refused (or bounded and reported) rather than accepted, plus at least one other backreference shape, and the existing accepted-pattern tests still pass — a guard that starts refusing ordinary searches is a worse outcome than the bug.
REPORT WHETHER THE SAME GUARD PROTECTS ANY OTHER ENTRY POINT, so the fix is not silently partial: if another tool or route compiles a user-supplied regex, say so; if this is the only one, say that.
notes: Filed 2026-08-06 from the windowed wave-11 security pass (segment W11b). Third finding of the session on this one guard, after W11-02's original bound and its own same-session follow-up for adjacent quantifiers — which is the argument for changing the approach rather than adding a clause.

tickets.title: resolveVault degrades to an EMPTY_VAULT on every non-macOS host, so the redaction layer four tickets built runs with nothing to redact while a cloud provider is live
acceptance: RAISED [MEDIUM] BY THE WAVE-11 SECURITY PASS (docs/work/SECURITY_W11f.md) AND NEVER CARRIED ONTO THE BOARD — re-verified live 2026-08-13 and the severity is wrong. `resolveAgentRunner`'s sibling `resolveVault` (apps/server/src/cli/run-build.ts:96-107) catches `NoKeychainAdapterError` and returns `EMPTY_VAULT` (line 83), whose `listValues()` is `async () => []`. `collectSecretValues(resolveVault(io.cwd), io.cwd)` at line 183 therefore hands the redaction layer an EMPTY list, and every downstream redaction pass runs correctly against nothing.

THE COEXISTENCE THAT MAKES IT HIGH, MEASURED NOT ASSUMED: `NoKeychainAdapterError` (packages/shared/src/config/credential-store.ts:223-229) is thrown for any platform with no adapter — its own message says 'no OS keychain adapter for platform X yet', and the file's header comment says the adapter set is macOS-only today. So this fires on EVERY Linux and Windows host that has not set `DOKIMA_NO_KEYCHAIN`. Meanwhile a cloud provider does NOT need the vault to work: Vertex resolves credentials through `GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS` ADC discovery (packages/gateway/src/providers/vertex.ts:83, and docs/DEPLOYMENT.md lists it as an environment variable). Linux host + Vertex configured by env = a fully live cloud provider with redaction silently inert. That is the exact reach-a-cloud-provider-unredacted failure W11-11, W11-14, W11-16 and W11-17 were four consecutive tickets spent closing, defeated by a fallback rather than by any of the paths they hardened.

IT IS A SILENT DEGRADATION, WHICH IS THE DEFECT: `return EMPTY_VAULT` emits nothing — no stderr line, no receipt, no event. An operator on Linux gets a run that looks identical to a redacted one. Compare the sibling failure two dozen lines above at line 175-180, where an unset `DOKIMA_SIGNING_KEY` REFUSES TO START with a named reason and `return 2` rather than minting unverifiable receipts. That is the precedent this path should follow, and the same file already contains it.

FIX (Law 8 / FR-S2): the degraded path must refuse or announce, never proceed quietly. Preferred shape, matching the signing-key precedent: refuse the run with a named error naming `DOKIMA_NO_KEYCHAIN`/`DOKIMA_VAULT_KEY` as the supported fallback (`credential-store.ts:191` already writes that exact guidance for the half-configured case). If a refusal is judged too strict for a project with no registered secrets at all, then distinguish the two cases — an empty vault because nothing was ever registered is fine; an empty vault because the platform HAS NO ADAPTER while entries may exist is not — and say which was chosen in the ticket notes with the reasoning. DO NOT "fix" this by widening the redaction layer or adding a second secret source: the redaction layer is correct and tested, it was handed an empty list. The defect is the fallback, and it lives in eleven lines of one file.

RED FIXTURE: a run on a simulated no-adapter platform (inject the throwing store, do not depend on the host OS) must be refused or must emit the named warning — proven failing against the current `return EMPTY_VAULT` before the fix, captured verbatim. A second fixture pins the benign case (macOS adapter present, vault genuinely empty) still starting normally, so the fix does not turn a fresh project into a refusal.
Full gate per CLAUDE.md Law 3 on Node 22, including `pnpm --filter @dokima/web e2e`.
notes: Filed 2026-08-13 during a board audit, not by a security run. Source: docs/work/SECURITY_W11f.md's `medium[]` array, whose CRITICAL became W11-20 and whose HIGH became part of the same ticket — the two mediums were never ticketed and no process step would have caught that, since the security docs are written per-wave and nothing re-reads them. Re-severitied from MEDIUM to HIGH on the coexistence evidence in acceptance 2; the original finding did not establish that a cloud provider stays live while the vault is empty, which is what makes it more than a hygiene issue. Worth noting as a process gap in its own right: a wave's security findings need a filing step, or the ones below the fold expire quietly.

I filed this citing Linux + Vertex-by-env as the reachable case; on reading the code the existing doc comment made a counter-argument I had not addressed — that on a no-adapter platform vault.register would refuse identically, so no vault secret could ever have been stored to redact. The finding survives by a DIFFERENT path, which is the one now in the code comment: resolveCredentialStore also accepts the encrypted-file backend behind DOKIMA_NO_KEYCHAIN + DOKIMA_VAULT_KEY (P-003), so an operator on Linux CAN register secrets and ~/.dokima/vault.json plus the project name index persist on disk; a later run not carrying those two variables degrades to an empty list while the secrets are still registered. The discriminator is the name index under <DOKIMA_HOME>/secrets/<projectId>/, but computeProjectId and INDEX_FILENAME are private to packages/shared/src/secrets/vault.ts — reaching them needs either a write_scope widening or a re-derived project-id hash here, which is the exact declared-twice defect W12-01 exists to fix. tickets.title: the external agent command is tokenized with .split(' '), so any agent binary on a path containing a space is silently mis-spawned
acceptance: RAISED [MEDIUM] BY THE WAVE-11 SECURITY PASS (docs/work/SECURITY_W11f.md), never carried onto the board; re-verified live 2026-08-13 at apps/server/src/cli/run-build.ts:188-189. `resolveAgentRunner`'s external branch does `(agentRunner.command ?? '').split(' ').filter(Boolean)` and feeds `[agentBin, ...agentArgs]` straight to `createChildProcessSpawn`. A command like `/Applications/My Agent/bin/agent --flag` tokenizes to `/Applications/My` plus four bogus args.

THE FAILURE MODE IS A CONFUSING REFUSAL, NOT AN INJECTION — state this correctly rather than inheriting the security framing. W11-20 already constrained `parseAgentRunnerSetting` to reject shell metacharacters (`;&|$()<>` and friends) and cap length at 4096, and `createChildProcessSpawn` does not go through a shell, so a split token cannot become a second command. What actually happens is a spawn of a path that does not exist, on macOS where `/Applications` paths with spaces are ordinary — the operator sees a failure that names a truncated path and nothing explains why.

FIX: store the runner as structured `command` + `args[]` rather than re-deriving argv from a string, OR tokenize with a real argv splitter that honours quoting. Prefer the structured shape — it removes the parse entirely — but that touches the settings type and its persisted value, so check the migration cost before choosing, and if the structured shape is taken, an existing string-valued setting must keep working (read-time compatibility, not a breaking change to a stored setting).
The W11-20 metacharacter constraint in `parseAgentRunnerSetting` stays regardless of which shape is chosen — do not treat quoting support as license to relax it.

RED FIXTURE: an external runner whose command is a quoted or space-containing path spawns the intended binary with the intended args — proven failing against the current `.split(' ')` first. Plus the W11-04 regression guard: an ordinary multi-arg command with no spaces in the path still round-trips unchanged.
Full gate per CLAUDE.md Law 3 on Node 22, including `pnpm --filter @dokima/web e2e`.
notes: Filed 2026-08-13 alongside W12-02 from the same unfiled SECURITY_W11f.md `medium[]` array. Kept at MEDIUM after re-checking: the security pass's own fix note suggested an argv-splitting library, but the exploitability it implies is not there post-W11-20 — this is a correctness and operator-experience defect on a path an operator deliberately configured, so it is filed as one. Recording that re-assessment rather than inheriting the label is the point; a finding carried forward at a severity nobody re-derived is how a backlog stops meaning anything.

tickets.title: the ticket HANDOFF carries only the ticket title as context — the Context Packer exists, is unexported, and has never had a caller
acceptance: FOUND 2026-08-13 BY A STEP-BACK REVIEW OF THE PRODUCT THESIS, not by a failing test — nothing in the gate can see it. `packages/harbormaster/src/loop-handoff.ts`'s `defaultHandoffBuilder` sets `context: ticket.interface ?? ticket.title`, and `apps/server/src/cli/run-build.ts` passes `defaultHandoffBuilder()` with no override. Every ticket session the built-in agent has ever run received one line of context. FR-L5 (BLUEPRINT §7.2) describes a Context Packer; `loop-handoff.ts`'s own doc comment says packing 'is FR-L5's own concern, not the claim loop's' and nothing ever supplied it.

ROOT CAUSE IS AN UNEXPORTED MODULE, NOT MISSING CODE. `packages/memory/src/packer/pack.ts#assemblePacket` is fully built and tested (core block + repo-map skeleton + ticket block + relevance-ranked slices + prior findings, stable-prefix ordered, whole-slice trimming, never naive truncation). It has zero non-test callers because `packages/memory/src/index.ts` exports ONLY `lessons/*` — the packer is unreachable across the package boundary, and TECH_STACK repository conventions forbid deep imports. Export `assemblePacket` and its types from the package's public surface as part of this ticket.

BUILD THE PACKED CONTEXT IN `apps/server`, NOT IN HARBORMASTER — this is the load-bearing design decision and it is already settled, do not re-open it. The §4 declared-dependency matrix has a BLANK in the harbormaster x memory cell and harbormaster's package.json does not declare `@dokima/memory`; `apps/server` declares BOTH `@dokima/memory` and harbormaster. `HandoffBuilder` is already a fully overridable seam (`loop-handoff.ts`: 'fully overridable by passing a custom builder'). So the fix is a new `apps/server/src/cli/handoff-context.ts` that composes `assemblePacket` into a `HandoffBuilder`, passed at `run-build.ts`'s existing `buildHandoff:` call site. NO architecture amendment and NO founder decision is required — adding a harbormaster -> memory edge would be the W11-02 shape (matrix ✅ + declaration as one deliberate chore) and is explicitly NOT what this ticket does.

DEGRADE HONESTLY WHEN THERE IS NOTHING TO PACK (C-1, FR-G5). `assemblePacket` takes `codeIndexHandle` and `factsHandle` as OPTIONAL — verified 2026-08-13 by reading the body: with neither handle it still returns core block + repo map + ticket block under the resolved token envelope, and the slice/findings sections render empty rather than throwing. A project with no code index and no memory store must therefore get a real packet that is strictly better than today's one-line context, never a refusal and never a fabricated slice. `modelWindowTokens` must come from the resolved model target, not a hardcoded constant. Relatedly, `assemblePacket` throws `PackerError` when the core block exceeds its 1k-token ceiling — that must surface as a named refusal at run start, not an unhandled rejection mid-session.

RED FIXTURE, PROVEN RED FIRST: a ticket whose `interface` field is absent produces a HANDOFF whose `context` is exactly its title today — assert that against the CURRENT `defaultHandoffBuilder()` path before changing anything, then assert the wired builder produces a packet containing the core block and the ticket's acceptance criteria. A second fixture covers the degraded path (no handles) and asserts the packet is still well-formed and the slice section is absent rather than empty-but-labelled.
Full gate per CLAUDE.md Law 3 on Node 22, including `pnpm --filter @dokima/web e2e`.
notes: Filed 2026-08-13 from a step-back architectural review asking whether Dokima actually implements its own product thesis ('the product manages the context'). It does not, on the build path. This is the single largest gap between what the product claims and what the ticket loop does, and it ranks ABOVE the attest content-parity gap (W12-07) that the same review found first. Sized 8 rather than 13 because the packer is built and tested — this is an export plus a call site plus honest degradation, which is exactly the build-then-wire seam shape that has recurred on this board (W11-04's `RunSessionInput.secretValues`, W11-16's wrap-`spawn`): a mechanism lands with no production caller and stays green forever because nothing tests for a caller.

Same-lane (`core`) as W12-03 deliberately: both edit `apps/server/src/cli/run-build.ts`, and P8 permits same-lane write_scope overlap while forbidding it cross-lane. They must never run in parallel; whichever claims second rebases.

HANDOFF 2026-08-13, BLOCKED mid-implementation on a defect in this ticket's own premise, found by doing the work. Acceptance criterion 3 says to compose `assemblePacket` into a `HandoffBuilder` and hand it to the existing `buildHandoff:` seam, on the strength of `loop-handoff.ts`'s claim that the builder is 'fully overridable'. It is not overridable by anything asynchronous: `HandoffBuilder` is `(ticket: Ticket) => Handoff` and `loop-land.ts:218` calls it synchronously, while `assemblePacket` is `async`. So the seam cannot accept a real packer, and that — not neglect — is why FR-L5 never had a caller. WHAT WAS VERIFIED BEFORE BLOCKING, so this is not a guess: the call site is `const handoff = options.buildHandoff(ticket)` with no `await`, and `loop-claim.ts:63` declares a second `buildHandoff: HandoffBuilder` that may need the same treatment. WHY NOT JUST WIDEN THIS TICKET'S SCOPE: `loop-handoff.ts` belongs to W12-06 (`orchestrator`) and this ticket is `core`, so adding it would trip P8 cross-lane overlap and fail the board — exactly the schema-bug case law 1 says to report rather than work around. UNBLOCKED BY W12-08 (filed with this note, `orchestrator`, 2pts), which widens the type to `Handoff | Promise<Handoff>` and awaits it. Nothing was written to `packages/memory/src/index.ts` or `handoff-context.ts` — this ticket starts clean once W12-08 lands, and its acceptance needs no change beyond the seam now actually existing.

UNBLOCKED 2026-08-13: W12-08 landed, widening `HandoffBuilder` to `Handoff | Promise<Handoff>` and awaiting it at both `loop-land.ts` and `loop-claim.ts`. The async seam this ticket needs now exists; acceptance is unchanged.

tickets.title: validator output is never re-injected into the agent session — the tool anchor exists and fires nowhere
acceptance: FOUND 2026-08-13 alongside W12-04. `packages/loop/src/anchors.ts` implements the Anchor framework (BLUEPRINT §3.5, FR-L2) — 'external ground truth composed onto the micro-loop as facts the model must reconcile with, rather than raw self-confidence' — and exports `gatherAnchorFacts` / `formatAnchorFactsForPrompt`. SCOPE IS THE TOOL ANCHOR ONLY. `anchors.ts`'s own header states the memory and challenger anchors are stubs that 'never fabricate a fact', pending W5 (challenger) and W7 (memory). Wire the TOOL anchor — validator/scanner output turned into facts via `toolFact` — and leave the other two unwired. Do NOT attempt to make three anchors real; that is a separate ticket and blocks on the same recall-population question W12-04 documents.
The import edge is already legal: harbormaster -> loop carries its ✅ in the §4 matrix and `@dokima/loop` is declared in harbormaster/package.json. No matrix change.

RED FIXTURE: a session whose validator run reports a failure, driven past enough turns that the failure would otherwise have left the window, still carries the failing fact in the prompt on the later turn — proven absent against the current `gateway-session.ts` first.

Anchor facts must be redacted on the same path everything else in the prompt is (`renderHandoff` already redacts `context` unconditionally) — a validator that echoes a secret value must not reintroduce it.
Full gate per CLAUDE.md Law 3 on Node 22, including `pnpm --filter @dokima/web e2e`.

tickets.title: wire per-ticket expert selection: add an explicit `role` field, set at decomposition (D-025)
acceptance: UN-HELD 2026-08-13 — FOUNDER DECISION D-025 (Brad, presented with three options): a ticket names its expert in an explicit `role` field, set at DECOMPOSITION time by the planner that already knows what kind of work it is. Rejected: inferring from lane/module (collapses 93 experts onto ~11 lanes, so security-auditor and db-architect could never both serve `core`), and a model reading the roster to pick (a model decision inside the trust boundary, needing its own receipt under Law 4 and a call per ticket before work starts).

THE DEFECT THIS FIXES: `defaultHandoffBuilder(role = ROLE_CODING_AGENT)` is called with no argument at every production call site, so every ticket the built-in agent has ever run was dispatched as `coding-agent` while `content/` ships 93 experts. The mechanism half already exists — `apps/server/src/api/roster-resolve.ts` documents that an expert file stem doubles as its `AgentRole`, and the gateway matrix already routes per role.

SCHEMA: add `role` to `plan.json`'s ticket contract as an OPTIONAL key (`OPTIONAL_KEYS` in scripts/validate-plan.mjs, beside `scaffold`), validated against the roster when present. Optional, not required: 208 existing tickets are `done` and must not be rewritten, and a ticket with no `role` keeps resolving to `coding-agent` exactly as today. Adding a REQUIRED field would fail the board on every historical row.

VALIDATE THE VALUE, or the field is decoration: an unknown role must fail `validate-plan.mjs` by name, not silently route to the default — an expert typo that quietly falls back to coding-agent is the same silent-degradation class this wave keeps finding. Read the valid set from `content/` rather than hardcoding a list that drifts from the pack.

C-4 STILL BINDS: naming a maker role must never let the maker also verify. The reviewer identity/model separation is mechanical (CLAUDE.md law 5) and this field does not get to soften it — prove it with a red fixture where a ticket names a role and the verifier still resolves to a distinct identity.

RED FIXTURE: a ticket carrying `role` produces a HANDOFF dispatched as THAT expert (proven to dispatch as `coding-agent` against the current builder first); a ticket with no `role` still dispatches as `coding-agent`; an unknown role fails the board validator.
notes: Filed HELD 2026-08-13. The board has no field for 'waiting on a human', which $holdNote4 already records as a recurring gap — holdTickets in conductor.config.json is the only place it can be said, so it is said there and here. Related open design question from the same review, NOT ticketed and belonging in docs/DECISIONS.md rather than on the board: attest v3.5.0's gauntlet loop (builders never grade their own work; a critic that saw a prior draft never grades the retry) may be the missing quality layer for this same loop, and C-4 already supplies the identity separation it needs. That may be one design with this ticket rather than two.

UN-HELD 2026-08-13 by founder decision D-025 (explicit `role` field at decomposition). Repointed and resized 5 -> 8: the original ticket was scoped only to `loop-handoff.ts` on the assumption the answer would be a code-local one, but the chosen direction adds a board-schema field, so `scripts/validate-plan.mjs` and its test come into scope too. Removed from conductor.config.json holdTickets in the same commit. NOTE the decomposer half (making the planner actually SET the field) is deliberately NOT in this ticket's scope — this ticket makes the field exist, be validated, and be honoured; a follow-up teaches decomposition to emit it, and until then a human sets it by hand.

write_scope widened at claim, deliberately and before writing anything — the same build-then-wire seam this wave keeps finding, caught at claim this time instead of at close. The filed scope was loop-handoff.ts + validate-plan.mjs, but `Ticket` (packages/tickets/src/types.ts) has NO `role` field, so a builder reading `ticket.role` would compile against a widened local type and read undefined forever: the field would be validated on the board and never reach the maker. Tickets are event-sourced, not columnar, so there is no migration — the change is three small files (type, create, reducer) carrying one optional string through the projection. Same lane (orchestrator), no P8 overlap: the only other open tickets are W12-37 (harbormaster+cli) and W12-27 (gateway). The one call-site fact that keeps this inside scope: createPackedHandoffBuilder composes defaultHandoffBuilder(options.role) at handoff-context.ts:185, so fixing the default builder fixes BOTH production paths without touching apps/server.

Closed 2026-08-18. One design question the acceptance did not anticipate, found by its own C-4 fixture: making the TICKET win over the builder argument is required for the field to be reachable at all (the only production path, createPackedHandoffBuilder, always passes a role), but ticket-wins is exactly what lets a board row name code-reviewer or challenger as the expert that DOES the work — the maker declaring itself the verifier. guardMakerVerifierDistinct cannot catch that: it fires on the verifier side and compares MODELS, by which point the collapse has already happened. So both layers refuse a verifier role by name — validate-plan P11 on the board, TicketRoleRefusedError at dispatch — rather than the ticket relying on a promise in a doc comment. Roster read from content/experts/** stems (84 roles) with ALL-CAPS stems excluded, because the pack also holds METHODOLOGY/FINDINGS_SCHEMA/PARALLEL_WAVE_PROTOCOL reference docs that are not experts and would otherwise validate as roles. The four still-open tickets each carry a real role now, so the field is exercised on the real board rather than only in fixtures.

tickets.title: HandoffBuilder is synchronous, so the "fully overridable" context seam can never accept the async Context Packer
acceptance: FOUND 2026-08-13 BY W12-04 SELF-BLOCKING ON IT, which is the only way it could have been found — no gate can see it. `HandoffBuilder` is typed `(ticket: Ticket) => Handoff` (`loop-handoff.ts`) and `loop-land.ts:218` calls it synchronously: `const handoff = options.buildHandoff(ticket);`. FR-L5's Context Packer (`assemblePacket`) is `async`. A custom builder that packs real context therefore returns `Promise<Handoff>`, which does not satisfy `HandoffBuilder` and cannot be awaited at the call site.

THIS REWRITES WHY THE PACKER WAS NEVER WIRED. `loop-handoff.ts`'s doc comment says context assembly is 'fully overridable by passing a custom builder' — that claim is false for any real packer, and the seam has been structurally incapable of accepting one since it was written. The explanation is not that nobody got to it; it is that the only documented way in does not fit. Fix the comment along with the type so the next reader is not told the same wrong thing.

CHANGE: widen `HandoffBuilder` to `(ticket: Ticket) => Handoff | Promise<Handoff>` and `await` it at `loop-land.ts:218`. `defaultHandoffBuilder` stays synchronous and every existing caller keeps compiling — a sync function already satisfies the widened type, so this is additive, not a breaking change to the built-in path.

Check `loop-claim.ts`, which declares its own `buildHandoff: HandoffBuilder` (line 63) — if it calls the builder too, that call site needs the same `await`, and the ticket is not done until both are found and fixed. Grep for every invocation rather than assuming there are two.

RED FIXTURE: an async `HandoffBuilder` returning a packet after a resolved microtask reaches the session with its `context` intact — proven to fail (a `Promise` arriving where a `Handoff` is expected) against the current synchronous type first.
Full gate per CLAUDE.md Law 3 on Node 22, including `pnpm --filter @dokima/web e2e`.
notes: Filed 2026-08-13 mid-W12-04 rather than worked around, per CLAUDE.md law 1 and MASTER_PROMPT's scope rule. W12-04 could not simply widen its own `write_scope` to cover this: `loop-handoff.ts` is owned by W12-06 (lane `orchestrator`) and W12-04 is lane `core`, so adding it would have produced a P8 cross-lane overlap — a hard board failure. Filing a same-lane (`orchestrator`) predecessor is the only shape that is legal on this board, and same-lane overlap with the HELD W12-06 is permitted precisely because the two can never be `in_progress` at once. Sized 2: a type widening, an `await`, and a corrected doc comment.

WRITE_SCOPE WIDENED 2026-08-13 mid-work, named rather than silently taken (the W10-77 precedent). Acceptance criterion 4 told this ticket to grep for every invocation instead of assuming two; doing so found the second at `loop-claim.ts:193`, inside the retry loop that re-renders a HANDOFF per attempt — a path where an unawaited Promise would reach `runSession` on EVERY attempt, not just the first. `loop-claim.ts`/`loop-claim.test.ts` are owned by no open ticket and are the same `orchestrator` lane, so this widening creates no P8 overlap and needed no board restructuring — unlike W12-04, which correctly self-blocked rather than widen across lanes.

tickets.title: the packed context has no ranked code slices — nothing in apps/server ever opens a W7-06 code-index handle
acceptance: DISCLOSED BY W12-04 AT CLOSE, not found later. `assemblePacket` takes optional `codeIndexHandle` and `factsHandle`; W12-04 omits both, so the packet it ships carries the pinned core block, the repo-map skeleton and the ticket block, but NO relevance-ranked file slices (BLUEPRINT §7.2 item 1, FR-M4) and NO prior confirmed findings. That is the packer's documented degraded path and it is honest, but it is not the whole feature.

ROOT CAUSE, verified by grep rather than assumed: no caller anywhere in `apps/server/src` references `codeSearch`, `indexProject`, `code-index` or `codeIndexHandle`. `packages/memory`'s own `store/handle.ts` documents that the package never opens a writable connection — a caller must supply an already-open handle, and the sanctioned opener is `@dokima/events`' `openEventLog(...).db`, which `apps/server` already calls extensively. So the handle is reachable; nothing hands it over.

ALSO STILL UNEXPORTED: `packages/memory/src/code-index/` has its own local barrel that `packages/memory/src/index.ts` does not re-export — the identical defect W12-04 fixed for `packer/`, left in place there deliberately because nothing needed it yet. This ticket needs it, so it closes that too, and should be the ticket that finally makes the pattern impossible rather than fixing a third instance by hand.

DECIDE AND RECORD WHEN THE INDEX IS BUILT: `indexProject` has to run before `codeSearch` returns anything, and a build-run that indexes the whole repo on every ticket would be a large per-ticket cost against Law 9's local-model reality. State the chosen trigger (once per run / mtime-gated / explicit command) and why, in the code, rather than leaving it implicit.

RED FIXTURE: a ticket whose `write_scope` names a file containing a distinctive symbol produces a packet whose RELEVANT CODE section contains that file — proven absent against the current handle-less path first. Plus a guard that the degraded path still works unchanged when no index exists, so this never becomes "Dokima requires an index to run".
Full gate per CLAUDE.md Law 3 on Node 22, including `pnpm --filter @dokima/web e2e`.
notes: Filed 2026-08-13 at W12-04's close, in the same session that disclosed it, because this wave's founding lesson is that a finding recorded only in prose expires — W12-02/03 sat in SECURITY_W11f.md for six days for exactly that reason. depends_on W12-04 (done), and it inherits the `handoff-context.ts` territory W12-04 released.

tickets.title: no gate can see an exported interface that nothing calls — six instances have shipped, three in one chain
acceptance: THE DEFECT CLASS, with its instance list, because the count is the argument: a mechanism lands complete, tested, with a documented contract and NO production caller, and stays green forever. Known instances — W11-04 `RunSessionInput.secretValues` (removed at review rather than left dead), W11-16 wrap-`spawn` (no caller until W11-04 supplied one), W12-08 `HandoffBuilder`'s override (advertised as "fully overridable", structurally unusable), W12-04 `packer/index.ts` (a complete barrel never re-exported), W12-05 `anchors.ts` (framework, no caller), and the roster (93 experts, one dispatched). TWO OF THESE WERE SELF-DOCUMENTED — the source said a future ticket would wire it up and no such ticket existed, which is why prose intent is not a control.

BUILD `scripts/validate-exports.mjs`, NOT a `content/validators/*.sh`. `content/` is imported upstream data (CLAUDE.md law 6, provenance-headed, re-imported wholesale by W12-07) — a Dokima-specific check added there would be destroyed by the next import and does not belong to upstream. Repo-local validators live in `scripts/` beside `validate-plan.mjs`/`validate-traceability.mjs`, which `conductor.config.json`'s `gates` array already runs.

MEASURE BEFORE GATING — this is the acceptance criterion most likely to be skipped, and the one that decides whether the validator is worth anything. Enumerate exports from each package public barrel, count references outside the declaring package excluding tests, and REPORT THE REAL NUMBER before choosing where it lands. attest v3.5.1's file-size pass is the precedent: an honest denominator took its violation count from 71 to 8 by excluding worktrees, benchmark output and generated samples. A validator that fires on 200 legitimate public-API exports is noise and will be waived into irrelevance.

PLACE IT HONESTLY BY WHAT THE NUMBER SHOWS: `gate[]` only if the repo-wide count is at or near zero after calibration (the same rule `conductor.config.json`'s `` already states for `repoWide`: only honest while it reports ZERO, because otherwise every ticket fails for debt it did not create). Otherwise `advisory[]`, where findings anchor the review instead of blocking. Record which was chosen and the count that justified it.

RED FIXTURE: an export with zero non-test references is reported, and one referenced only from a `.test.ts` is ALSO reported (test-only usage is the exact disguise `RunSessionInput.secretValues` wore — it had tests and no callers). A guard proves a genuinely-referenced export is not reported.
Full gate per CLAUDE.md Law 3 on Node 22, including `pnpm --filter @dokima/web e2e`.
notes: Filed 2026-08-13 after the third instance in a single dependency chain landed in one session (W12-08, W12-04, W12-05). Claimed immediately rather than left on the board: every prior instance of this class was recorded in prose somewhere and none of that prose stopped the next one.

tickets.title: no cloud provider kind is constructible — half of "local or your cloud provider" refuses by design
acceptance: D-024 MAKES THIS A RELEASE BLOCKER, not an enhancement. `providerForConfig` throws `ModelResolutionError('kind-not-constructible')` for `anthropic`, `openai`, `vertex` and `copilot`. Its own comment gives the two honest reasons and they are still true: the registry stores a `credentialRef` (a NAME) where the adapter needs a resolved secret, and `AnthropicConfig.costTable` is REQUIRED with no $0 default ('no $0 default for a paid API'). Only `ollama`, `lm-studio` and bare oai-compat construct today, so a user who registers a cloud provider in the Providers panel gets a named refusal — which under D-024 option (b) is now a broken promise rather than honest caution.

RESOLVE THE CREDENTIAL AT CALL TIME THROUGH THE KEYCHAIN (Law 8, FR-S2). `targetToConfig` currently sets `apiKey: env.DOKIMA_MODEL_API_KEY` unconditionally with a comment saying the keychain 'resolves it at call time' — nothing does. The plumbing already exists and is proven: `resolveCredentialRef`/`resolveCredentialStore` (`packages/shared/src/secrets/`) and `collectSecretValues`, which `run-build.ts` already calls. The env key stays as the documented CI path, second in line behind a real ref.

SHIP REAL PRICE TABLES, and treat a missing one as a REFUSAL rather than $0. This is the load-bearing half: metering a paid API at $0 does not merely mis-report — it disables W2-07's budget breakers entirely, because a breaker that reads $0 can never trip. A provider whose model has no price entry must refuse by name, exactly as the current code refuses the whole kind.

THE oai-compat LOOPHOLE MUST CLOSE WITH IT, and it is how this was found: pointing `DOKIMA_MODEL_BASE_URL` at `https://api.openai.com/v1` with `DOKIMA_MODEL_API_KEY` routes a real paid OpenAI account through `createOaiCompatProvider`, which defaults to `LOCAL_COST_TABLE` — literally `{}`, so every priced call meters $0. That path bypasses the very guard the cloud-kind refusal exists to enforce. Detect a known cloud host on an oai-compat endpoint and require a price table for it too, or state explicitly why that is out of scope and file it.

RED FIXTURES: a registered cloud provider with a resolvable credentialRef and a price table CONSTRUCTS and reports non-zero cost for a fixture response (recorded fixture, never a live call — CLAUDE.md law 9a is untouched by D-024); the same provider with an unresolvable credentialRef refuses by name; a priced model missing from the table refuses rather than reporting $0.
Full gate per CLAUDE.md Law 3 on Node 22, including `pnpm --filter @dokima/web e2e`.
notes: Filed 2026-08-13 from the D-024 contract correction, found while answering whether the OpenAI plan could drive a supervised run. It can, through the oai-compat env path — but the spend ledger reads $0 and the budget breakers cannot fire, which is precisely the fabrication the cloud-kind refusal was written to prevent. The refusal was good engineering; what was missing was a ticket to remove the reason for it.

RELEASED 2026-08-13 before any code, on a sequencing conflict found while mapping the work rather than while writing it. Making a cloud kind constructible requires resolving `ProviderEntry.credentialRef` — a NAME, never resolved anywhere today — and `resolveCredentialRef` is async, so an async step lands upstream of provider construction and every production entry point adopts it. One of those is `apps/server/src/cli/run-build.ts:171`, which **W12-03 owns and is lane `core` against this ticket's `gateway`** — a cross-lane write_scope overlap is a hard P8 failure, the schema-bug case law 1 says to report rather than work around. Rejected the two workarounds explicitly: re-laning this ticket to `core` would hide a real file conflict behind a taxonomy edit, and adding a NEW async constructor beside the sync one would ship an exported function with no caller — the exact defect class W12-10 now gates. Correct order is W12-03 first (2pts), which releases run-build.ts at `done` under D-015; this ticket then widens cleanly.

WRITE_SCOPE SET AT CLAIM 2026-08-13, wider than filed and named rather than discovered later. `providerForConfig` must become async to resolve a credentialRef, so its three production callers come with it (`gateway-model-port.ts:151`, `onboard-dispatch-port.ts:205`, `run-build.ts:171`), plus the two tests that assert the refusal this ticket removes (`gateway-model-port.test.ts:276`, `providers-routes.test.ts:347`). `run-build.ts` was released by W12-03 at `done` (D-015), which is why this ticket waited for it. PRICING LOCATION VERIFIED BEFORE WRITING: `content/model-catalog/` is Dokima-owned, not listed in `scripts/import-content.mjs`, and ZERO of its files appear in the signed `content/manifest.json` — so W12-07's attest re-import cannot clobber it and no re-signing is required. Had it been part of the imported pack, this file would have belonged elsewhere entirely.
