tickets.title: a user cannot pin ONE model — `locked` pins a rung, so D-024 option (b) has no implementation
acceptance: D-024 OPTION (b): 'a specific model of their choosing, local or cloud, pinned, no escalation'. `EscalationPolicyMode = 'ladder' | 'locked' | 'token-gated'` and `locked` pins a RUNG of the R0–R4 ladder, then loops under a convergence budget. That is not the same promise: a user who says 'use gpt-5 and nothing else' is choosing a MODEL, and a rung can resolve to a different model as the matrix changes underneath them.

ADD THE MODE RATHER THAN OVERLOADING `locked` — `locked`'s D-018 semantics (pin a tier, loop until pass, park, never silently escalate) are real, tested and still wanted. The new mode pins an exact `(providerId, model)` and never escalates for any reason, including a failure that would normally trigger the ladder. Name it in `policy-types.ts` and resolve it through the SAME three-scope (run > project > global) per-role path D-018 already built; do not add a second resolution mechanism.

PARK HONESTLY WHEN THE PINNED MODEL CANNOT DO THE WORK. The whole point of pinning is that nothing quietly substitutes a different model — so exhaustion parks the ticket with a named reason (the shape `locked` already uses), never a silent fallback to the ladder and never a swap to a neighbouring model in the same tier.

MAKER≠VERIFIER SURVIVES PINNING (C-4, and this is the trap): if a user pins one model for every role, maker and verifier would resolve to the same model, which C-4 forbids BY CONSTRUCTION. Decide and state the behaviour — refuse the configuration by name, or require a distinct verifier pin — and prove it with a red fixture. Do not let a convenience setting quietly dissolve a hard constraint.

RED FIXTURE: a pinned policy runs the named model and, on a failure that would advance the ladder, parks with a named reason instead of escalating — proven to escalate against the current `ladder`/`locked` modes first. Plus the C-4 fixture above.
Full gate per CLAUDE.md Law 3 on Node 22, including `pnpm --filter @dokima/web e2e`.
notes: Filed 2026-08-13 from D-024. Deliberately separate from W12-11: this is the POLICY half (can a user express 'this model only'), that is the CAPABILITY half (can a cloud model be constructed at all). Both are needed before option (b) works end to end, and neither is sufficient alone.

write_scope gained `policy-pinned.ts` mid-work, named: appending the pinned mode took `policy.ts` to 461 lines and the repo-wide file-size gate went red — the FIRST time that gate has caught this session, and it caught accretion exactly as designed (the cap is on the FILE, not the diff, because several individually-reasonable appends become a monolith and no single one looks wrong). Split per CODE_BOOK_PROTOCOL into a chapter module; policy.ts is 383. The chapter deliberately does NOT import policy.ts — the C-4 guard needs to resolve other roles' policies, so the resolver is INJECTED as a parameter rather than imported back, which would have made the two modules mutually dependent and tripped validate-circular-deps.

tickets.title: the setup wizard never asks how work should be modelled, so the policy is chosen silently
acceptance: D-024: 'There is no silent default. A fresh install asks in the setup wizard and nothing spends money, or contacts a network, until the user has chosen.' Today `resolveLandEscalationPolicy` returns `ladder` when nothing is set, so a fresh install silently adopts cheapest-first escalation across whatever is configured — a policy the user never picked.

THE WIZARD PRESENTS THE FOUR D-024 OPTIONS IN THE USER'S OWN TERMS, not the internal mode names: local-only (never contacts a cloud provider) · one model I pick · start cheap and escalate when it has to · escalate only when I approve it. Map each to the resolved policy (`ladder`/`token-gated`/the W12-12 pinned mode) and write it at the scope the user chose, reusing the existing three-scope settings path — no new persistence mechanism.

LOCAL-ONLY MUST BE HONESTLY SELECTABLE WITH NO PROVIDER CONFIGURED AND NO NETWORK (C-1 as amended): choosing it completes the wizard, and the product then works. This is the guarantee D-024 kept as hard, so it gets a fixture, not just a menu entry.

NOTHING SPENDS OR CONNECTS BEFORE THE CHOICE. State plainly what the wizard itself does before a policy exists — a model list fetched from a cloud provider to populate a picker is itself a network call, so either it happens only after the user picks a cloud option, or the picker degrades to free text and says why.

RED FIXTURE: a fresh project with no settings does NOT resolve to `ladder` by default — a run started before a policy is chosen refuses by name, or the wizard blocks completion, whichever the implementation chooses; proven against the current silent-`ladder` behaviour first.
Full gate per CLAUDE.md Law 3 on Node 22, including `pnpm --filter @dokima/web e2e`.
notes: Filed 2026-08-13 from D-024, founder-chosen ('Ask in the setup wizard — no silent default'). The first-run wizard already exists (acceptance check A-18), so this is a step inside a built flow rather than a new surface. Note the interaction with W12-11: until cloud kinds construct, the 'one model I pick' and 'start cheap and escalate' options can only offer local models honestly — decide whether the wizard hides them or shows them as requiring provider setup, and say which in the close notes.

WRITE_SCOPE CORRECTED at claim: the filed scope said `apps/web/src/onboarding/**`, but the wizard COMPONENT lives at `apps/web/src/settings/FirstRunWizard.tsx` — only its test sits under onboarding/, and that test's own header explains why (a prior ticket's write_scope covered the settings component but not a sibling test file there). Owned by no open ticket, no P8 issue. ALSO FOUND AT CLAIM: the wizard's existing step 1 picks a MODEL MATRIX preset (which models serve which roles, FR-S3) and never touches the ESCALATION POLICY, which is the thing that silently defaults to `ladder` at policy.ts:80. Two different dimensions; the wizard asked about one. D-024 needs both.

WRITE_SCOPE WIDENED to two e2e specs, named: both drove the wizard via `getByLabel(/Hybrid/)`, a label this ticket removes. CONFIRMED MINE RATHER THAN ASSUMED — stashing the change and re-running gave 69 passed, so both failures are caused by this ticket and neither is pre-existing flake. Updated to `/Start cheap, escalate/`, which maps to the same `hybrid` matrix preset the old label selected, so the flows test what they always tested. This is the value of e2e being in the Law 3 gate: the unit tests were green while two real user flows were broken.

tickets.title: the provider registry has no field for a GCP project or location, so Vertex still cannot be constructed
acceptance: DISCLOSED BY W12-11 AT CLOSE, and referenced by name in the refusal message that ships in `provider.ts` — so this ticket must exist or that message points at nothing. W12-11 made `anthropic`, `openai` and `copilot` constructible by solving credentials and pricing. Vertex is NOT blocked on either: `createVertexProvider` requires `project` and `location`, and `ProviderEntry` (`packages/gateway/src/registry/types.ts`) carries only `id`/`kind`/`baseUrl`/`credentialRef`/`requestTimeoutMs`/`enabled`. There is nowhere to put them.

DO NOT DERIVE THEM FROM `baseUrl` — that is the guess this refusal exists to avoid. A GCP project id decides WHICH ACCOUNT GETS BILLED; inferring it from a URL fragment would be the same class of fabrication as metering a paid call at $0. Add explicit optional registry fields and validate them for the `vertex` kind specifically.

`VertexConfig` also accepts `serviceAccountJson` (a pre-resolved service-account JSON) which takes precedence over ADC. Decide and state which auth path Dokima supports: a `credentialRef` resolving to service-account JSON through the keychain (consistent with W12-11's credential handling), ambient ADC (works on a GCP box, invisible elsewhere), or both with a documented precedence.

PRICING IS ALREADY DONE: `content/model-catalog/pricing.v1.json` ships `vertex` entries for gemini-2.5-pro and gemini-2.5-flash, and `costTableFor` already refuses an unpriced Vertex model. This ticket adds no pricing work.

RED FIXTURE: a registry entry with kind `vertex` plus project and location constructs; one missing either refuses BY NAME saying which field is absent — proven against the current schema, which cannot express them at all.
Full gate per CLAUDE.md Law 3 on Node 22, including `pnpm --filter @dokima/web e2e`.
notes: Filed 2026-08-13 at W12-11's close, in the same commit that ships a refusal message naming it — a code comment pointing at an unfiled ticket is exactly the "prose intent is not a control" failure this wave keeps finding. Vertex is the one cloud kind D-024 option (b) still cannot serve.

WRITE_SCOPE CORRECTED at claim, named: the filed scope named `registry/types.ts` and a nonexistent `registry/types.test.ts`, but the VALIDATOR lives in `registry/validate.ts` (tested by `validate.test.ts`), and the fields have to survive three more hops to reach the adapter — `ProviderEntry` -> `ResolvedModelTarget` (model-resolution.ts) -> `GatewayConfig` (config.ts) -> `createVertexProvider`. A field that validates and then dies at any hop is the "settable and inert" defect W10-57 documented in this very file; `validate.ts`'s own construction is an explicit ALLOWLIST with a comment saying so.

tickets.title: the Providers panel still tells users cloud kinds are "not yet constructible" — a second copy of a message that is now false
acceptance: FOUND BY W12-11 AND DELIBERATELY NOT ABSORBED INTO IT. `providers-routes.ts:105`'s `buildCatalogProvider` carries an INDEPENDENT HARDCODED COPY of the refusal W12-11 removed: "provider kind X is registered but not yet constructible from the pipeline". The pipeline now constructs anthropic, openai and copilot — so the Providers panel tells a user a feature does not work while it does. A contract held in two places where the copy nobody edited keeps being served: the same defect class as W12-01's duplicated `DEFAULT_PORT`.

THIS IS THE MODEL-LISTING SURFACE, NOT INFERENCE — which is why it is its own ticket rather than a W12-11 scope widening (that ticket already widened twice, deliberately and on the record). `buildCatalogProvider` exists to populate the model picker via `listModels()`, a different call path from the chat path W12-11 fixed. It needs the same async credential resolution before a cloud kind can list anything.

REUSE `providerForConfig`, DO NOT REIMPLEMENT IT. A third independent copy of "which adapter does this kind mean" is how the second one happened. `buildCatalogProvider` should delegate, or the shared construction should move somewhere both call. The route returns `Pick<Provider, 'listModels'>` today, so check whether the narrowed type is load-bearing before widening it.

DEGRADE HONESTLY WHEN THERE IS NO CREDENTIAL: a registered cloud provider with no resolvable credential cannot list models, and the panel must say THAT rather than "not yet constructible". The picker degrading to free-text entry is acceptable and should say why; silently showing an empty model list is not.

RED FIXTURE: a registered `openai` entry with a resolvable credential lists models through a recorded fixture (never a live call, CLAUDE.md law 9a); one with no credential produces a named, accurate refusal that does NOT claim the kind is unconstructible. `apps/web/src/settings/ProvidersPanel.test.tsx` asserts the old string and must be updated with it.
Full gate per CLAUDE.md Law 3 on Node 22, including `pnpm --filter @dokima/web e2e`.
notes: Filed 2026-08-13 at W12-11's close. W12-11's full test suite passed WITH this stale message still asserted, because the assertion lives against a duplicate string on a path that ticket never touched — a green suite proving nothing about a claim the UI makes. That is the argument for W12-01's fix generalising: two copies of a contract, and the gate can only see the one under test.

RE-LANED core -> gateway and write_scope widened at claim, named. Listing models needs a CREDENTIAL but not a PRICE TABLE, and `providerForConfig` demands a model id to look a price up — which is circular, because listing is what tells you the models. So the catalog path needs a listing mode in `provider.ts`, and that file is owned by W12-14 (lane `gateway`); a `core`-laned ticket touching it is a P8 cross-lane failure. Re-laning is the correct fix rather than a workaround: the lane is a PARALLELISM CONTRACT, and two tickets that genuinely share a file should share a lane so they can never run at once. Same reasoning W12-04 used to sit in `core` beside W12-03.

tickets.title: the wizard offers four model-policy choices, not five — D-024 option (b) has an implementation now but no way to pick it
acceptance: W12-13 shipped the wizard with FOUR choices and stated in its own close notes that D-024 option (b) — "one model I pick" — would arrive with W12-12. W12-12 has landed: `EscalationPolicyMode` now includes `pinned`, which names an exact model and never substitutes. The wizard still offers four. This ticket is that promise, filed rather than left in prose.

ADD THE FIFTH CHOICE with the input it actually needs: a pinned policy carries a `model` and an optional `providerId`, so the wizard needs a model identifier from the user — unlike the other four, which map to fixed presets. Decide honestly whether that is free text (works with no provider configured and no network, but typo-prone) or a list fetched from the chosen provider (better UX, but a network call, and W12-15 must land first because model LISTING for cloud kinds is still broken).

DO NOT OFFER IT WHERE IT CANNOT WORK. Pinning a cloud model requires a constructible provider: anthropic/openai/copilot construct as of W12-11, vertex does not (W12-14). Either constrain the choice to what is reachable or say plainly what setup it needs — an option that silently fails at first run is worse than one that is absent.

C-4 IS ENFORCED AT RUN TIME AND MUST BE SURFACED AT PICK TIME: `PinnedPolicyMakerVerifierError` refuses a configuration that pins one model for both maker and verifier. A user who picks a single model in the wizard must not discover that at their first run — either the wizard pins only the maker role and leaves verifiers on the ladder (stating so), or it asks for a second, distinct model.

RED FIXTURE: choosing the pinned option persists `escalationPolicy: { mode: 'pinned', model: <chosen> }` at the scope the user selected, proven against the current four-choice wizard first; and the C-4 collision above is prevented or explained before the wizard completes.
Full gate per CLAUDE.md Law 3 on Node 22, including `pnpm --filter @dokima/web e2e`.
notes: Filed 2026-08-13 at W12-12's close. W12-13's STATUS entry says option (b) "arrives with W12-12" — that was true of the ENGINE and not of the UI, and the distinction is exactly the kind that evaporates if it lives only in a close note. The engine half is done and tested; this is the pick-time half.

RELEASED 2026-08-13 before any code, on a discovery that changes what this ticket MEANS. The escalation policy the wizard writes is READ BY NOTHING: `run-build.ts` never passes `policyScope` to `runLandLoop`, so `loop-land.ts:299` resolves `options.policyScope ?? {}` and every run gets `ladder` regardless of what the user chose. Adding a FIFTH inert control to a wizard whose other four are already inert would be worse than leaving it at four. Now depends on W12-18 (wire the setting into the run) and W12-12 (which shipped `pinned` in the GATEWAY policy type — `LandEscalationPolicy` in harbormaster is a separate union of ladder/locked/token-gated and does not model it, so honouring a pinned choice end to end is its own step).

BLOCKED 2026-08-18 at claim, on its own acceptance. The ticket assumes W12-12 made `pinned` runnable; it did not. W12-12 added the mode to packages/gateway/src/escalation, whose runEscalationPolicy has NO production caller — the live path is runLandLoop, whose LandEscalationMode is ladder|locked|token-gated, and resolvePolicyScope refuses `pinned` by name. Adding the fifth choice now would offer an option that refuses at first run, which this ticket's third acceptance criterion forbids in capitals. Also ruled out: mapping option (b) onto `locked` plus a one-entry matrix — D-024's cost note and the wizard's own doc comment already considered and rejected it, because `locked` pins a RUNG, not a model. The fix is core-lane and outside this ticket's apps/web write_scope, which under Law 1 is reported rather than worked around: filed as W12-37, now a dependency. Second thing to carry into the eventual claim: FirstRunWizard.tsx sits at EXACTLY 400 lines, so the fifth choice needs a file split planned at claim, not discovered mid-ticket.

UNBLOCKED 2026-08-18: W12-37 landed on D-027, so `pinned` is now a real run-time behaviour and offering the fifth choice no longer hands a user a first-run refusal. Two things this ticket now OWNS that it did not when filed: (1) the stored setting must carry `providerKind` alongside `model` — `tierKindFor` reads it to infer the 8-vs-12 convergence ceiling, and with nothing writing it every pin conservatively reads as `metered`; (2) the C-4 question in the original acceptance is already answered by construction — the pin lands on the maker role only and the verifier resolves from its own row, proven by a W12-37 fixture — so the wizard states that rather than asking for a second model. The 400-line FirstRunWizard.tsx split still needs planning at claim.

write_scope gained modelPolicyChoices.ts, planned at claim as this ticket's own note demanded rather than discovered mid-work: FirstRunWizard.tsx sits at EXACTLY 400 lines, so a fifth choice plus the model input it needs cannot land in it. The choice table is the natural extraction — it is data, the wizard is the surface that renders it. DESIGN DECIDED AT CLAIM on the ticket's free-text-vs-fetched-list question: FREE TEXT, and asked on the PROVIDER step rather than the policy step. The provider step is where the kind is already chosen, so the pin gets its `providerKind` for free (which W12-37 needs for the 8-vs-12 ceiling and which nothing writes today), and a fetched list is not available at first run anyway — W12-15 lists models for a CONFIGURED provider, and at step 1 there is not one yet. Offering a dropdown that is empty on the only run this wizard ever has would be worse than a field.

Closed 2026-08-18. D-024's four user choices are all pickable now; the wizard offers five options because 'cheapest-first' and 'approval-gated' are two of them. THE FREE-TEXT-VS-LIST QUESTION was answered by the wizard's own position in the flow rather than by preference: W12-15 lists models for a CONFIGURED provider, and at first run there is not one, so a dropdown would be empty on the only run this surface ever has. The field says so in place rather than leaving a user wondering why there is no list. ASKED ON THE PROVIDER STEP, not the policy step — that is where the kind is already chosen, so the stored pin carries providerKind and W12-37's ceiling inference stops silently reading metered for everything. C-4 IS STATED, NOT ASKED: W12-37 makes the maker-only pin true by construction, so the wizard says reviews use a different model instead of asking for a second one. The sentence moved to the shared hint after a fixture caught it appearing twice on one screen — it is true of all five choices, not just this one, so the choice detail was the wrong home. apps/web's own EscalationPolicyMode still read ladder|locked|token-gated (it redeclares rather than imports, being a browser bundle), so `pinned` had to be added there too — without it the choice could not be typed at all.

tickets.title: a THIRD copy of the adapter dispatch lives in cli/ops/providers-core.ts and nothing has updated it since W12-11
acceptance: FOUND BY W12-15, WHICH REMOVED THE SECOND COPY. `buildProvider` (`apps/server/src/cli/ops/providers-core.ts:54`) switches on `entry.kind` and constructs adapters itself — the ORIGINAL of the duplicate W12-15 just deleted, and the one whose existence that duplicate's own comment cited as the reason it was copied ('duplicated here rather than imported, since that module lives under cli/ops and this ticket's write_scope doesn't cover it'). Verify what it does with cloud kinds before assuming: if it still refuses them, the CLI and the API now disagree about whether a registered OpenAI provider works.

DELEGATE TO `providerForConfig`, do not re-fix in place. Three independent copies of 'which adapter does this kind mean' is how the second one happened and the third survived; the point of this ticket is that ONE dispatch exists afterwards, not that all three are individually correct.

CHECK THE PURPOSE FLAG CAREFULLY. `providerForConfig` takes `purpose: 'inference' | 'listing'` (W12-15); a listing provider carries NO cost table and must never serve a chat. notes: Filed 2026-08-13 at W12-15's close. WRITE_SCOPE WIDENED at claim, named: `buildProvider` becomes async (it now delegates to the async `providerForConfig`), so its two callers — `doctor.ts` and `providers-refresh.ts` — come with it. tickets.title: the escalation policy setting is written by two UI surfaces and read by nothing — every run silently gets
acceptance: FOUND 2026-08-13 BY W12-16, WHICH RELEASED ITSELF RATHER THAN ADD A FIFTH INERT CONTROL. `EscalationPolicyPanel` and (since W12-13) the first-run wizard both persist an `escalationPolicy` setting. `run-build.ts` never passes `policyScope` to `runLandLoop`, so `loop-land.ts:299` evaluates `resolveLandEscalationPolicy(options.policyScope ?? {}, role)` against an empty scope and returns `LADDER_LAND_POLICY` every time. Verified by grep: NO reader of that settings key exists in non-test code.

THIS INVALIDATES A CLAIM ALREADY IN STATUS.md, corrected in the same commit rather than left standing: W12-13's entry says the policy is "now CHOSEN, not inherited from `resolveLandEscalationPolicy's fallback". True of what is PERSISTED, false of what RUNS. D-024's promise is inert until this ticket lands.

READ THE EFFECTIVE SETTING and map it to `ScopedLandEscalationPolicy`, which is keyed by ROLE across run > project > global. The stored setting is a single flat object, so decide and state which role it applies to — **the maker role only** is the right answer: it makes the setting mean what a user thinks it means, and it keeps verifiers on the ladder, which satisfies C-4 by construction rather than by a later refusal.

`pinned` HAS NO LAND-POLICY EQUIVALENT and must not be silently dropped. W12-12 added `pinned` to the GATEWAY policy union; `LandEscalationPolicy` (harbormaster) is a separate union of ladder/locked/token-gated. A stored `pinned` policy must refuse BY NAME at run start — naming that the land loop does not yet honour it — rather than falling through to `ladder`, which would be the same silent substitution W12-12 exists to prevent.

RED FIXTURE: a project with a stored `token-gated` policy produces a run whose resolved policy is token-gated, not ladder — proven to resolve as ladder against the current code first. Plus: a stored `pinned` policy refuses by name rather than running as ladder.
Full gate per CLAUDE.md Law 3 on Node 22, including `pnpm --filter @dokima/web e2e`.
notes: Filed and claimed 2026-08-13, mid-W12-16. This is the EIGHTH instance of the wave's recurring class — a complete, tested mechanism with no production caller — and the most consequential, because the thing left unwired is the product promise D-024 was written to make. The four choices the wizard offers are all currently decorative.

That is part of the causal story, not an incidental blocker — a type you cannot name is a parameter you do not pass, and this is the same unexported-mechanism shape as W12-04 packer barrel and W12-11 openai adapter. write_scope gained run-build-policy.ts: adding the resolver took run-build.ts to 468 lines and the repo-wide file-size gate went red. tickets.title: the setup wizard offers three provider kinds while the Providers panel offers seven — you cannot finish first-run setup on a cloud provider
acceptance: FOUND 2026-08-14 while writing supervised-run instructions, after the founder asked why the instructions used env vars instead of the GUI. The wizard step 2 select offers exactly three options — LM Studio, OpenAI-compatible endpoint, Vertex AI — while PROVIDER_KINDS (providers-api.ts) carries seven, and the Providers panel renders all of them with a credential field. So a user whose plan is OpenAI or Anthropic cannot complete FIRST-RUN setup on it; they finish the wizard on something else and then go find Settings.

THE WIZARD IS THE FIRST THING A NEW USER SEES, which is why this is not cosmetic: it is the surface that decides whether the product feels like it supports cloud providers at all. W12-11 made anthropic/openai/copilot constructible and W12-15 made them listable; the wizard never learned.

REUSE `PROVIDER_KINDS` AND `KIND_LABEL` from providers-api.ts rather than hand-listing options a fourth time — the option list here IS a fourth copy of the kind table, and this wave has now fixed three copies of the adapter dispatch for exactly that reason (W12-11/15/17).

RESPECT THE ENDPOINT/CREDENTIAL SHAPE PER KIND: `hasFixedEndpoint` already says which kinds take a base URL and which take a credential only. A fixed-endpoint kind must not show a base-URL box, and a cloud kind must take the API key through the same POST credentials route the panel uses (Law 8 — the secret is exchanged for a ref, never stored in settings).
RED FIXTURE: the wizard renders an option for every kind in `PROVIDER_KINDS` (proven to render only three first), and selecting `openai` submits a credentialRef rather than a raw key.
Full gate per CLAUDE.md Law 3 on Node 22, including `pnpm --filter @dokima/web e2e`.
notes: Filed 2026-08-14. Sibling of W12-20: together they are the difference between "configure connectivity in a GUI and go" being true and being half-true.

tickets.title: no UI or API path starts a build run — the GUI can configure everything and then cannot run anything
acceptance: FOUND 2026-08-14, same trigger as W12-19. Grep for a route driving `runLandLoop`/`executeBuildRun` across `apps/server/src/api` returns NOTHING: `runs-routes.ts` serves `GET /tickets/:id/runs` and `GET /runs/:id/trace`, both read-only. A user can register providers, choose a model policy in the wizard, watch the board and replay a trace — and has no way to START the work from the product. `dokima run start` is the only entry point.

THIS IS THE GAP BETWEEN THE PRODUCT AND ITS OWN PITCH: the README says you describe what you want and Dokima works the board. Every configuration surface is a GUI and the one action that matters is a terminal command.

START A RUN AS A BACKGROUND JOB, not a held HTTP request — W10-58 already moved the creation pipeline off a held request onto a background job for exactly this reason, and a build run is far longer. Reuse that machinery rather than inventing a second job mechanism.

THE REFUSALS MUST REACH THE UI, not just a server log. `executeBuildRun` refuses by name for an unset signing key, an unreadable vault, an unconstructible provider kind and (since W12-18) a pinned policy the land loop cannot honour. Each of those is something a user can act on, and each currently only reaches stderr.

RED FIXTURE: starting a run from the API moves a claimable ticket off `ready` and the trace becomes visible — proven impossible against the current read-only routes first. Plus: a run started with no signing key surfaces the named refusal in the response rather than failing silently.
Full gate per CLAUDE.md Law 3 on Node 22, including `pnpm --filter @dokima/web e2e`.
notes: Filed 2026-08-14 after the founder asked why supervised-run instructions used env vars and a CLI rather than the GUI. The instructions were correct about what works TODAY, and that is the finding: the product configures in a GUI and runs from a terminal. Note the supervised run itself does NOT need this — it can be started from the CLI against GUI-registered providers, which is the path docs/work/SUPERVISED_RUN.md now documents.

write_scope NARROWED at close, named rather than left overstated: the filed scope included `apps/web/src/board/**` and this pass never touched it. The server gap was the hard half — there was no route at all — and the button is a small follow-up filed as W12-28. A scope that claims territory the ticket did not write is the same overstatement W12-07 was corrected for.

tickets.title: the Providers panel offers one auth method (an API key box) — "use my subscription" has nowhere to live
acceptance: FOUNDER DIRECTION 2026-08-17: settings should present every way a person can connect — an API key, or a subscription they already pay for — the way opencode does, and the wizard must never be the only road. The panel today has exactly one input: `draft.apiKey`, POSTed to the credentials route and exchanged for a keychain ref. There is no concept of an auth METHOD, so a subscription sign-in has nowhere to appear.

THE WIZARD IS ALREADY SKIPPABLE — verified, do not 'fix' it. `MainView.tsx` only enters the wizard on explicit action (`onOpenWizard` from Settings, or the guided-sample link) and it has a Cancel. Nothing auto-opens it. The complaint that prompted this ticket came from INSTRUCTIONS that framed it as a required step, not from the product. This ticket is about the Settings surface only.

MODEL AUTH AS AN EXPLICIT PER-KIND CHOICE, AND DO NOT MAKE IT BINARY. There are at least THREE shapes, not two: an api key (openai/anthropic), a subscription OAuth flow (copilot device code), and GOOGLE ADC (vertex — `TECH_STACK.md`: "Vertex auth = ADC, not API keys (D-007)"), whose inputs are a service-account JSON credential ref, a credentials file path, or ambient credentials the user established with `gcloud auth application-default login`. Local kinds need none at all. Each kind declares which methods it supports and the panel renders only that method's fields — `hasFixedEndpoint`/`needsBaseUrl` already establish the per-kind-shape pattern in `providers-api.ts`; extend that rather than adding a parallel one. An api-key-vs-oauth toggle would have to be torn up the moment Vertex is added, which is why this says so now.

WIRE THE COPILOT DEVICE FLOW, WHICH IS ALREADY BUILT AND HAS NEVER HAD A UI: `requestDeviceCode` and `pollDeviceAuthorization` (`packages/gateway/src/providers/copilot-device-auth.ts`) are complete and tested, `createCopilotProvider` takes a credential STORE rather than an api key, and `DEFAULT_COPILOT_CREDENTIAL_REF` names where the token lands. This is the ninth instance of the wave's unwired-mechanism class and the cheapest genuine 'use my subscription' win. Copilot stays default-off behind its explicit consent gate (D-019) — this ticket gives that gate a real sign-in, it does not remove it.

SUBSCRIPTION AUTH MEANS FLAT FEE, WHICH THE PRICING LAYER ALREADY MODELS HONESTLY: `pricing.v1.json`'s `notes.copilot` says a flat-fee subscription has no public per-token price, so it meters $0 and that is TRUE rather than a gap. Any subscription-authed provider added here inherits that reasoning; do not invent per-token rates to make a spend ledger look populated.

RED FIXTURE: a kind whose only method is subscription renders NO api-key field and completes through the device flow to a stored credential ref; a kind supporting both lets the user pick and submits only the fields that method needs. Proven against the current single-box panel first.
notes: Filed 2026-08-17 from founder direction. Split from the two subscription integrations (W12-22, W12-23) deliberately: this ticket is the SURFACE — auth method as a first-class per-kind concept plus the one flow that is already built — and it delivers value without depending on any external API being verified first.

AMENDED 2026-08-17 after the founder asked about Vertex: the first draft of criterion 3 implied a two-option model. Vertex is a third shape (ADC), so the method concept has to be extensible from the start rather than a boolean that gets rewritten. Vertex's own wiring is W12-25 and depends on W12-14 (the registry cannot express project/location yet, so Vertex is the one cloud kind that still refuses at construction).

write_scope gained ProviderAuthFields.tsx: the auth-method fields took ProvidersPanel.tsx to 439 lines and the file-size gate went red — third accretion catch of the wave (policy.ts, run-build.ts were the others), all three several reasonable appends rather than one oversized write.

tickets.title: Anthropic subscription sign-in — BLOCKED: Anthropic banned third-party subscription OAuth in Feb 2026
acceptance: FOUNDER DIRECTION 2026-08-17: a user paying for Claude Pro/Max should be able to sign in with it rather than register a separate API key.

VERIFY THE FLOW AGAINST REAL DOCS BEFORE WRITING A LINE (CLAUDE.md Law 2, non-negotiable and the reason this is its own ticket). Do NOT reconstruct an OAuth flow from memory or from how another tool appears to behave: confirm the authorization endpoint, client registration requirements, scopes, token refresh and — critically — whether subscription credentials are PERMITTED to serve API traffic under Anthropic's current terms. Record what was checked and when, the way `docs/TECH_STACK.md` records other verified API traps.

MODEL IT ON THE COPILOT ADAPTER, which is this repo's proven subscription shape: a credential STORE rather than an api key, a device/browser flow that mints a token, refresh handled inside the adapter, and `LOCAL_COST_TABLE` because a flat-fee subscription has no public per-token price.

IF VERIFICATION SHOWS THERE IS NO SUPPORTED PATH, CLOSE THIS TICKET WITH THAT FINDING rather than building something that works by accident. A sign-in button that depends on undocumented behaviour is worse than an API key field, because it breaks silently for users who trusted it.
RED FIXTURE: the flow mints and stores a credential ref against a RECORDED fixture (law 9a — never a live call in tests), and an expired token refreshes rather than failing the run.
Full gate per CLAUDE.md Law 3 on Node 22, including `pnpm --filter @dokima/web e2e`.
notes: Filed 2026-08-17. Depends on W12-21 because the panel needs the auth-method concept before a second subscription flow has anywhere to render.

VERIFIED AGAINST LIVE SOURCES 2026-08-17 (Law 2), and the answer inverts this ticket. Anthropic updated its Legal-and-compliance guidance in FEBRUARY 2026 to prohibit OAuth tokens from Claude Free/Pro/Max in ANY third-party product, tool or service outside Claude Code and Claude.ai. Routing user requests through subscription credentials is banned outright, and OPENCODE IS NAMED as a tool no longer permitted to do it — which matters, because "like opencode does" was the premise of this request. Developers must use API-key auth issued through Claude Console or a supported cloud provider. This is not a technical gap that a better OAuth flow would close; it is a permission that has been withdrawn. Building it would put a DISTRIBUTED product in direct violation of Anthropic terms and expose users to the account-suspension risk D-019 already gates Copilot for. Recommendation: close as WILL-NOT-BUILD and keep API keys as the Anthropic path. Left blocked rather than closed because that is a founder call.

CLOSED AS WILL-NOT-BUILD-IN-CORE 2026-08-17 under D-026, with the finding rather than the feature as the deliverable — which is what a spike is for and, for Anthropic, what the evidence supports. Core ships auth only where the vendor documents a third-party integration path; subscription sign-in moves behind the plugin seam (W12-27), so a user who wants it installs it deliberately and carries the exposure themselves. Nothing here is blocked on a better OAuth implementation: the endpoints work and the permission is the missing part. Recorded in docs/TECH_STACK.md so the next person asking "why not just add a login button" gets the answer without re-deriving it.

tickets.title: SPIKE: determine whether an OpenAI ChatGPT subscription can authenticate API calls at all
acceptance: FOUNDER ASKED FOR IT; I FLAGGED A DOUBT AND THE FOUNDER CHOSE TO INCLUDE IT ANYWAY — so this is filed as a SPIKE rather than an implementation, which is the honest shape for 'build it if it exists'. The doubt, stated so it can be checked rather than trusted: OpenAI has historically billed API usage SEPARATELY from ChatGPT Plus/Pro subscriptions, and a ChatGPT subscription has not been a supported way to authenticate API requests.

ANSWER ONE QUESTION AGAINST CURRENT OFFICIAL DOCS: can a ChatGPT Plus/Pro/Team subscription authenticate calls to an API endpoint Dokima could drive? Cite what was read and the date. This is a documentation question, not a reverse-engineering exercise: a path that works by imitating a first-party client is not a path this product can ship on, because it breaks silently and may violate terms.
IF YES: close this spike and file the implementation ticket, modelled on the Copilot adapter (credential store, no api key, LOCAL_COST_TABLE for a flat fee).

IF NO: record the finding in `docs/TECH_STACK.md` beside the other verified API traps, and make the Providers panel SAY SO where a user would look for it — "OpenAI API keys are billed separately from ChatGPT subscriptions" is a one-line label that prevents a support question and a wrong assumption. Then close.
DO NOT SHIP A SIGN-IN BUTTON THAT CANNOT WORK. That is the whole point of spiking this before W12-21 renders a method list.
notes: Filed 2026-08-17. Sized 2 because the deliverable is an answer plus a documented finding, not code. Deliberately has no depends_on — it should be answered EARLY, since its result decides whether W12-21's method list shows an OpenAI subscription option at all.

SPIKE PARTIALLY ANSWERED 2026-08-17 against live sources, ahead of anyone claiming it. The technical answer is YES-BUT: OpenAI genuinely ships "Sign in with ChatGPT" for Plus/Pro/Team, but it is for OPENAI'S OWN Codex CLI, using OpenAI's own client. There is NO explicit statement permitting a third-party product to use that flow — unlike Copilot, where the device flow is a documented integration path. OpenAI's Terms prohibit using the Services "automatically or programmatically", an open question on the openai/codex repo asks whether even FORKING Codex CLI affects ToS under ChatGPT sign-in, and the community plugins that do this self-describe as personal-use-only, explicitly not for powering a product. So my original doubt was right about OpenAI for a subtly different reason than I gave: the endpoint exists, the PERMISSION does not. For a product intended for distribution that is the same answer as no. Recommendation: record the finding in TECH_STACK.md, label it in the panel where a user would look, and keep API keys as the OpenAI path.

CLOSED AS WILL-NOT-BUILD-IN-CORE 2026-08-17 under D-026, with the finding rather than the feature as the deliverable — which is what a spike is for and, for OpenAI, what the evidence supports. Core ships auth only where the vendor documents a third-party integration path; subscription sign-in moves behind the plugin seam (W12-27), so a user who wants it installs it deliberately and carries the exposure themselves. Nothing here is blocked on a better OAuth implementation: the endpoints work and the permission is the missing part. Recorded in docs/TECH_STACK.md so the next person asking "why not just add a login button" gets the answer without re-deriving it.

tickets.title: a Node-version mismatch kills the CLI with a raw C++ stack trace before doctor can say anything useful
acceptance: HIT LIVE BY THE FOUNDER 2026-08-17 on the first command of the supervised run: `NODE_MODULE_VERSION 127 ... requires 137`, a raw `better-sqlite3` load error with no mention of Dokima, Node 22, or `.nvmrc`. CLAUDE.md Law 3 documents this exact trap and `fnm`'s default is Node 24 — so the single most likely first-run failure on a developer machine produces the least actionable message the product can emit.

`doctor` CANNOT HELP HERE, which is the crux: it dies on the same native import before any check runs. The guard therefore belongs in `cli-entry.mjs` BEFORE anything native is imported — a version check is the one thing that must not depend on the thing it is checking.

REFUSE BY NAME: compare `process.versions.modules` against what the bundled binary needs and print a message naming the product, the required Node line (`.nvmrc` says 22), the version actually running, and the fix (`fnm use 22` / `nvm use 22`). Exit non-zero. Same posture as every other named refusal this wave added — a control that fails unreadably is barely a control.

DO NOT HARDCODE 137-VERSUS-127. Read the expectation from `.nvmrc`/`engines.node` and the ABI from `process.versions.modules`, so the guard survives the next Node major rather than becoming a second constant that drifts from the first (W12-01 is on this board for exactly that failure).
RED FIXTURE: a simulated ABI mismatch produces the named refusal and a non-zero exit, proven to produce the raw `better_sqlite3.node` stack trace first.
Full gate per CLAUDE.md Law 3 on Node 22, including `pnpm --filter @dokima/web e2e`.
notes: Filed 2026-08-17. Highest leverage-per-point item on the board: it is the FIRST thing a new user can hit, it is already documented as a known trap, and the current behaviour is a C++ error message that mentions neither the product nor the fix.

write_scope: the pure translation lives in its own module rather than inside cli-entry.mjs, because importing that file to test it would EXECUTE it — it boots the CLI at module scope. `cli.test.ts` was dropped from scope and never edited; the guard is tested directly.

tickets.title: Vertex sign-in: detect ambient ADC, accept a service-account ref, and say which one is in play
acceptance: FOUNDER ASKED FOR A "login with Vertex" OPTION 2026-08-17. State the shape honestly before building it: Vertex does not take an API key and has no device flow. `packages/gateway/src/providers/vertex.ts` authenticates through google-auth-library's ADC chain (`vertex-auth.ts`), and `VertexConfig` accepts `serviceAccountJson` (a pre-resolved key JSON, FR-S2 credential ref, which TAKES PRECEDENCE), `credentialsFilePath`, or nothing at all — in which case ambient ADC is used.

DOKIMA CANNOT OWN THE GOOGLE LOGIN ITSELF, and pretending otherwise is the trap. The browser flow that produces ambient credentials is `gcloud auth application-default login`, run by the user against Google's own client. Implementing a lookalike OAuth flow to make a "Sign in with Google" button appear in-app would be reimplementing a first-party client — the same class of mistake W12-23 spikes for ChatGPT. What Dokima CAN do is the useful part: DETECT, GUIDE, and offer the service-account alternative.

DETECT AND REPORT: the panel shows whether ADC is currently resolvable and, when it is, which account/project it resolves to — `health()`/`warmUp()` already verify ADC token acquisition, so the check exists and needs surfacing rather than inventing. When ADC is absent, show the exact command (`gcloud auth application-default login`) instead of a generic failure.

OFFER THE SERVICE-ACCOUNT PATH as a stored credential ref through the same POST credentials route every other secret uses (Law 8 — the JSON is exchanged for a keychain ref and never lands in settings.json or the event log). This is the path that works on a machine with no gcloud installed, and it must be selectable rather than implied.

RED FIXTURE: a Vertex entry with a service-account ref constructs and reports which auth path it used; one with neither a ref nor resolvable ADC refuses BY NAME and names the gcloud command, proven against the current behaviour first. No live Google calls in tests (law 9a) — use the `authClientFactory` seam `vertex.ts` already exposes for exactly this.
Full gate per CLAUDE.md Law 3 on Node 22, including `pnpm --filter @dokima/web e2e`.
notes: Filed 2026-08-17. Depends on W12-14 because the provider registry still has no field for a GCP project or location, so Vertex is the ONE cloud kind that refuses at construction even after W12-11 — no auth work matters until an entry can express which project gets billed. Depends on W12-21 because the panel needs the auth-method concept (and W12-21 was amended in the same commit to stop treating that concept as api-key-vs-oauth, precisely because Vertex is a third shape).

Lane set to `ui` rather than `gateway`: the bulk of this ticket is the Providers panel, which W12-21 also owns, and P8 rejected the cross-lane overlap on filing. Two tickets that genuinely share a file share a lane so they can never run at once — the same correction W12-15 and W12-04 each made.

write_scope widened at work: the project/location fields had to cross FOUR allowlist mappers (browser WireProvider/toWireEntry/fromWireEntry, server fromWire/toWire), every one of which drops an unlisted field silently. Plus providers-auth-methods.ts, extracted when providers-api.ts hit 421 lines — fourth accretion catch of the wave.

tickets.title: the Copilot device flow has no server route — the adapter and the UI both exist, nothing connects them
acceptance: DISCLOSED BY W12-21 AT CLAIM, and it resized that ticket's assumption. W12-21 was filed saying the Copilot device flow "is already built and has never had a UI" — half right. `requestDeviceCode` and `pollDeviceAuthorization` (`copilot-device-auth.ts`) ARE complete and tested, and W12-21 added the panel affordance. What does not exist is anything in between: grep `apps/server/src/api` for a device-auth route and it returns nothing. The UI has a button-shaped hole and the gateway has a function nobody can call over HTTP.

TWO ROUTES, because a device flow is inherently two-step: one to REQUEST a device code (returns the user code and verification URL for display), one to POLL for authorization. Poll on the SERVER against the gateway function rather than proxying a loop from the browser — the token must land in the keychain via the credential path (Law 8) and never transit the web client.

THE POLL MUST TERMINATE HONESTLY: device codes expire and users abandon flows. Respect the interval and expiry the device-code response carries, and surface `authorization_pending`, `slow_down`, `expired_token` and `access_denied` as distinct, named outcomes rather than one generic failure — `CopilotDeviceAuthError` already exists for this.

D-019 CONSENT IS NOT WEAKENED BY THIS. Copilot ships default-off behind an explicit ledgered consent acknowledgement because using it against a personal account can get that account banned. This ticket gives the consent gate a working sign-in; it does not remove or bypass the gate, and a red fixture must prove an unconsented kind still refuses to enable.

RED FIXTURE: the two routes complete a device flow against a RECORDED fixture (law 9a — never a live GitHub call) and leave a credential ref the provider entry can carry; an expired code produces the named expiry outcome, not a hang.
Full gate per CLAUDE.md Law 3 on Node 22, including `pnpm --filter @dokima/web e2e`.
notes: Filed 2026-08-17 at W12-21's close. Recording the estimate error rather than hiding it: W12-21 assumed "already built, just needs a UI" and the missing middle was a whole HTTP surface. The panel now says so where a user would look, rather than showing a button that does nothing.

Lane `ui`, not `core`: it shares `providers-routes.ts` with W12-25, and P8 rejected the cross-lane overlap on filing. Fourth time this wave that two tickets sharing a file had to share a lane — the rule is doing real work.

write_scope gained providers-copilot-routes.ts. Adding the two routes took providers-routes.ts from 394 to 499 lines and the 400-line CODE_BOOK_PROTOCOL cap failed the repo-wide validator — caught by the full gate, not by the ticket-level tests. Extracting is the fix the cap was asking for rather than a workaround: the device flow is a self-contained protocol against one external endpoint, so it is a real seam. Also corrected on the way: the first implementation collapsed expired_token / access_denied / transport faults into one 502, which the ticket explicitly forbids — CopilotDeviceAuthError.code now surfaces as a 400 with the code in evidence, and only a genuine transport failure is a 502.

tickets.title: a provider/auth plugin seam — so subscription sign-in is possible without core shipping it
acceptance: D-026: core ships auth only where the vendor documents a third-party path. Everything else — Claude Pro/Max, ChatGPT Plus/Pro, any provider Dokima does not bundle — becomes reachable through a seam a user opts into, so the ToS exposure sits with whoever installed the plugin rather than with this product and every person handed it.

MOST OF THE INJECTION POINTS ALREADY EXIST, so this is a registry rather than a rewrite: every provider config takes `fetchImpl` (the same hook opencode's `loader` uses to swap an API key for an OAuth bearer), `CredentialStore` already abstracts secret storage behind keychain refs (stronger than opencode's 0600 JSON file), and Vertex already exposes an `authClientFactory`. What is missing is a way to REGISTER an auth provider Dokima does not ship.

DECIDE AND RECORD HOW A PLUGIN IS TRUSTED — this is the acceptance criterion most likely to be skipped and the one that decides whether the seam is worth having. A plugin is third-party code running in-process with access to credentials, inside a product whose thesis is C-2/C-3: sessions are untrusted and the platform holds the gates. "We hold the gates, except for plugins" is not a position this product can take silently. Choose among explicit install-time consent (the D-019 shape, ledgered), signature verification (the `content/` pack shape, already built and already verified by `doctor`), capability limits on what a plugin may reach, or a combination — and write down what was rejected and why. **Shipping the seam without this answer trades a legal risk for a security one.**

A PLUGIN MUST NOT BE ABLE TO EXFILTRATE CREDENTIALS IT WAS NOT GIVEN. Scope a plugin to the provider id it registers: it receives the credentials for that entry and no others, and it never sees the vault wholesale. `collectSecretValues` and the redaction path exist and should be checked against this, not assumed to cover it.

DESIGN FIRST, IMPLEMENTATION SECOND. The deliverable here is `docs/design/PLUGIN_SEAM.md` plus the type surface — the interface, the trust decision, the capability boundary, and the failure modes when a plugin throws, hangs, or returns a malformed credential. A loader that hangs must not hang a run. Do NOT ship a working Anthropic or OpenAI plugin from this ticket: that would put the thing D-026 declined back in the repo by another door.
Full gate per CLAUDE.md Law 3 on Node 22, including `pnpm --filter @dokima/web e2e`.
notes: Filed 2026-08-17 from D-026. The founder asked twice for Claude Max / ChatGPT Plus sign-in "like opencode does"; verifying how opencode actually does it is what produced this design — core ships an `AuthHook` + `loader` seam and the subscription flows live in separate plugin packages, which is precisely why opencode is structurally fine and a core implementation would not be. Sized 8 and deliberately design-heavy: the trust question is the hard part, and it is the part that cannot be retrofitted once a plugin API is public.

Closed 2026-08-19 as the design ticket it was scoped as: PLUGIN_SEAM.md plus the type surface, no loader. Two helpers were written, tested and withheld when validate-exports refused them for having no caller (buried 73->75); their behaviour is specified in the doc and they belong to W12-44.

tickets.title: the board has no Start-run affordance — W12-20 built the route and nothing calls it
acceptance: DISCLOSED BY W12-20 AT CLOSE. `POST /api/v1/projects/:id/build-runs` exists and returns 202 with a run id; nothing in `apps/web` calls it. Until something does, the GUI still cannot start work and the pitch is still only half true.
START FROM WHERE THE WORK IS VISIBLE — the board, next to the tickets a run would claim — rather than burying it in Settings. A user who can see a `ready` column should be able to act on it.

POLL THE STATUS ROUTE, THEN FALL BACK TO THE TRACE. W12-20's outcome map is IN-MEMORY and deliberately so: it is a convenience for the immediate poll, not a second source of truth, and a server restart forgets a finished run's stdout. Anything displayed after a reload must come from the event log the trace route already serves.

SURFACE THE REFUSALS AS TEXT A PERSON CAN ACT ON: unset signing key, unreadable vault, unconstructible provider kind, a pinned policy the land loop cannot honour. Each names its own fix; do not collapse them into "run failed".

RED FIXTURE: clicking Start moves a claimable ticket off `ready` and surfaces the run id; a refused run shows its named reason rather than a generic failure. Proven impossible against the current board first.
Full gate per CLAUDE.md Law 3 on Node 22, including `pnpm --filter @dokima/web e2e`.
notes: Filed 2026-08-17 at W12-20's close rather than folded into it. The server half was the hard half and is done; pretending the UI came with it would be the same overstatement this wave keeps catching in other people's tickets.

tickets.title: every control is the same outlined pill — there is no primary action anywhere in the product
acceptance: FOUNDER UX REVIEW 2026-08-17, judged against REAL CAPTURED FRAMES (docs/acceptance/runs/2026-08-17T20-11-14-317Z/) rather than from reading code. Fleet shows six identical outlined pills; the workspace shows eight. Nothing is primary, nothing recedes, so a new user's eye has nowhere to land and they read every control left-to-right and guess. "Start a run" — the most important action in the product — is visually identical to the theme toggle.

TOKENS ARE NOT DESIGN, and this is the precise gap. W10-06/28/30/32 landed 96 `--sw-*` tokens with zero raw hexes in feature stylesheets, and that work is real and stays. What is missing is the layer ABOVE tokens: button VARIANTS (primary · secondary · quiet/icon), a spacing rhythm, and a type scale. A palette without a hierarchy still renders a flat page.

ONE PRIMARY PER SCREEN, and name which one it is per surface: Fleet → New Product; workspace → Start a run; wizard → Next; Settings → the tab action. Everything else is secondary or quiet. A screen with two primaries has none.

APPLY IT WHERE IT IS MOST FELT FIRST rather than everywhere at once: the header, Fleet, the board run bar, and the wizard. A partial application that is CONSISTENT within those surfaces beats a complete one that drifts.

RE-CAPTURE AND COMPARE, do not assert improvement: `node apps/web/scripts/capture-acceptance.mjs` produces a frame per checklist item against a real build, and the pre-change run is at the path above. Put the before/after pair in the close notes so the judgement is visual and checkable rather than a claim.
Full gate per CLAUDE.md Law 3 on Node 22, including `pnpm --filter @dokima/web e2e`.
notes: Filed 2026-08-17 from a founder-requested UX review done against captured frames. This is first in the wave because every other visual fix looks better on top of it and worse without it — a board layout fix over flat chrome still reads flat.

tickets.title: the board gets a third of the window by default, so six lifecycle states cannot fit and the grid has to wrap them
acceptance: THE WORST SINGLE VISUAL DEFECT, visible in docs/acceptance/runs/2026-08-17T20-11-14-317Z/06-A-06.png: each lane renders Ready / Claimed / In Progress on one row and In Review / Blocked / Done beneath it. Kanban's entire value is ONE left-to-right pipeline; wrapping it into a grid destroys the metaphor, and a user cannot see flow at all.

ACCEPTANCE CORRECTED AT CLAIM — THE ORIGINAL WAS WRONG AND THE CODE SAID SO. It demanded "one horizontal pipeline per lane, scrolling rather than wrapping". `board.css` carries a long measured rationale for the opposite: the Board is the CENTRE OF THREE PANES and gets ~470px at a 1440px window, six 12rem columns need ~1200px, `flex-wrap` was tried and rejected (grow stretched the final row into double-width columns that read as a rendering bug), and `auto-fit`+`minmax` was chosen and re-measured by screenshot at 1440x900 and 1280x800 in both themes. W9-05's edge-fade scroll affordance already exists and is load-bearing down to a 120px pane. Unwrapping the grid would re-break what W10-06/W10-32 measured. THE ROOT CAUSE IS UPSTREAM: `defaultLayout()` allocates chat 34% / board 33% / artifacts 33%, so the pane the layout itself marks as `activeView: board` gets the smallest-equal share of the window.

GIVE THE BOARD THE ROOM ITS CONTENT NEEDS BY DEFAULT, rather than shrinking the content to fit a share nobody chose. The grid then fits more states per row on its own, with no change to the measured column minimum and no risk to the drop targets both e2e specs depend on. Any new split must stay inside MIN_PANE_PCT/MAX_PANE_PCT and remain user-draggable — this changes a DEFAULT, not a constraint.
EMPTY COLUMNS MUST NOT COST WHAT FULL ONES COST. Most of the captured board is empty boxes at full height, which is independent of the wrap and true at any pane width.
LANES NEED TO BE VISIBLE: `GATEWAY` and `UI` render as small grey uppercase with no separation, so a two-lane board reads as one grid.

LEAVE THE IN-CARD `Move to…` SELECT ALONE IN THIS TICKET, and say why rather than silently skipping it: it is part of the visible content the column minimum was MEASURED against (board.css W10-32), and the drag path it would be replaced by carries the refusal behaviour UX_SPEC requires ("drag-refusals explained", `RefusalPopover.tsx`). Swapping it is a real change to both, and bundling it here would put a measured layout and a refusal path at risk inside a ticket about pane allocation. File it separately if still wanted.
notes: Filed 2026-08-17. Depends on W12-29 so the card and column chrome lands on a real hierarchy rather than being restyled twice.

ACCEPTANCE CORRECTED 2026-08-17 at claim. The original was written from a screenshot reaction — "the board wraps 3x2, that is the worst single defect" — without reading the rationale beside the code. `board.css` documents that the wrap is a deliberate, screenshot-measured response to a 470px pane, that flex-wrap was tried and rejected, and that the scroll affordance already exists. The critique was right that the board is hard to read and wrong about why: the board is not laid out badly, it is allocated a third of the window while being the active view. Recording the correction because a ticket that tells a maker to undo measured work is worse than no ticket.

tickets.title: a user who comes to connect a provider finds a dead end — Settings without a project offers only the wizard
acceptance: THE QUESTION THAT PROMPTED THIS WAVE was "is there a way to configure without running the wizard". There is — Settings is always one click from the header — but docs/acceptance/runs/2026-08-17T20-11-14-317Z/17-A-17.png shows why it did not feel that way: with no project open, Settings renders one jargon sentence ("Open a project to configure its model matrix, autonomy dial, budgets, and scopes") and exactly one button, Run Setup Wizard. It does not link to CREATING a project, and says nothing about providers.

PROVIDERS GETS ITS OWN TAB, named "Providers". Today the panel is nested inside "Model Matrix" — the tab list reads Model Matrix · Agent · Autonomy·Budget·Berths · Cost Estimate · Effective Settings · MCP Servers · Validator Packs · Expert Overrides · Rule Lifecycle, and nothing in it says "this is where you connect an account". `ModelMatrixPanel` may keep composing the panel for its catalog; this is about the NAV, not about moving the component.

THE NO-PROJECT PAGE OFFERS REAL CHOICES rather than a single funnel: create or open a project, and connect a provider, with the wizard presented as ONE option among them instead of the only affordance on the page.

WRITE IT FOR A PERSON. "model matrix, autonomy dial, budgets, and scopes" is internal vocabulary. The first-run wizard's own copy ("Nothing spends money or contacts a network until you choose") is the standard — plain, specific, reassuring — and it is in this same codebase to copy from.

RED FIXTURE: Settings with no project renders an affordance that leads somewhere other than the wizard, and a project-scoped Settings renders a tab literally labelled Providers. Proven against the current single-button page first.
Full gate per CLAUDE.md Law 3 on Node 22, including e2e.
notes: Filed 2026-08-17. Independent of W12-29 — it is information architecture and copy, not visual hierarchy — so it can run in parallel with the board work.

WRITE_SCOPE WIDENED to two e2e specs, named. Four e2e tests failed the moment Settings opened on Providers instead of Model Matrix — three matrix flows timed out waiting for a form that is now a tab away, and the no-project spec asserted the old copy verbatim. All four are consequences of a deliberate change, not flake, and they are the SAME shape as W12-13/W12-19: change a default, break the callers that assumed the old one. The unit suite was green throughout; only e2e saw it.

tickets.title: the product uses four words for one concept — Fleet, programs, Product, project
acceptance: On ONE screen (docs/acceptance/runs/2026-08-17T20-11-14-317Z/01-A-01.png) a user sees the heading "Fleet", the empty state "No programs yet.", and a button "New Product" — for a thing the code calls a project. Elsewhere the nav offers "Describe · Plan · Decisions", and Settings mentions a "model matrix" and an "autonomy dial".

PICK ONE WORD PER CONCEPT AND WRITE THEM DOWN in `docs/design/VOCABULARY.md`, so the next surface built does not invent a fifth. This is a decision to record, not a preference to hold in someone's head — the same reason DECISIONS.md exists.
THE WIZARD IS THE STANDARD. Its copy is the best-written text in the product; whatever vocabulary is chosen should read the way that does.

INTERNAL TERMS THAT SURVIVE MUST EARN IT. "Lane", "receipt" and "manifest" are load-bearing product concepts with real meaning — keep them and define them. "Model matrix" and "autonomy dial" are internal names for user-facing settings and should be said plainly.

RENAME IN THE UI ONLY, not in the event log or the API. Wire shapes, event types and stored settings keep their names — a vocabulary pass that rewrites a durable contract is a migration, and that is not this ticket.
Full gate per CLAUDE.md Law 3 on Node 22, including e2e.
notes: Filed 2026-08-17 from the same review.

tickets.title: chrome reads as unfinished — emoji buttons, a full-width back bar, raw form controls
acceptance: Captured frames show 🔔 and ☀️ emoji sitting among text buttons in the header; `← Fleet` consuming a full-width bar for one link; native unstyled radios, selects and inputs throughout; and roughly 80% of every screen empty with content pinned to the top-left.
ICONS, NOT EMOJI. Emoji render differently per platform and font, and next to text buttons they read as a placeholder nobody replaced.
GIVE THE FORM CONTROLS THE SAME TREATMENT AS THE BUTTONS — inputs, selects and radios styled from the same tokens, so a form does not look like a different application than the page around it.
THE EMPTY SPACE IS A LAYOUT PROBLEM, not a content problem: give the page a max width and a vertical rhythm so content is composed rather than pinned to a corner.

ACCESSIBILITY IS NOT OPTIONAL HERE: whatever replaces an emoji button keeps an accessible name, and focus states survive the restyle. `docs/acceptance/CHECKLIST.md` A-19/A-20/A-21 already judge overlay and dark-theme behaviour — do not regress them.
Full gate per CLAUDE.md Law 3 on Node 22, including e2e.
notes: Filed 2026-08-17. Depends on W12-29 so chrome is restyled once, against a real hierarchy, rather than twice.

write_scope gained styles.test.ts: styling the form controls needs a focus ring, and the W10-06 raw-px guard refused `outline: 2px`. Exempting it is the honest fix rather than dodging into `box-shadow` (already exempt) purely to avoid touching the guard — a focus ring is geometry, and WCAG 2.2 treats its thickness as an accessibility property, so it should not be snapped to a spacing token that a later layout change could quietly thin. The allowlist entry carries that reason and is deliberately narrow: `outline-color` still has to come from a token. The file's own note warns that an exemption nothing needs is the first crack in an allowlist, which is why this one is justified in place.

tickets.title: board work has no focus mode — the pipeline still wraps because three panes share one window
acceptance: DISCLOSED BY W12-30 AT CLOSE. Widening the board default to 58% got 5 of 6 lifecycle states onto one row, up from 3. The sixth needs either a narrower `--sw-board-column-min` (measured at 8.5rem; W10-32's history is a warning against reducing it on a hunch) or a wider board still, which starves Chat — at 58% it is already ~300px. Neither is right: the real constraint is that three panes share one window.

THE MACHINERY EXISTS ALREADY. Panes collapse (`«` affordances, `collapsed` in `PaneLayout`) and the layout persists per project. What is missing is a one-click way to say "I am working the board now" rather than collapsing two panes by hand every session.

RESTORE, DO NOT DESTROY: entering and leaving focus must return the user to the layout they had, not to the default. The layout is already persisted, so the previous sizes are recoverable — do not overwrite them with the focused ones.

RED FIXTURE: focusing the board collapses the side panes and fits all six lifecycle states on one row at 1440px; leaving focus restores the exact prior sizes, including a layout the user had dragged themselves.
Full gate per CLAUDE.md Law 3 on Node 22, including e2e.
notes: Filed 2026-08-17 at W12-30's close instead of shrinking a measured constant to make a screenshot look better. W12-30 got the default allocation right; this is the affordance that makes the constraint stop mattering.

write_scope gained two e2e specs: both addressed the pane-header collapse toggle as `getByTestId(pane-x).getByRole(button)` — unnamed, and therefore unique only while the header had exactly ONE button. Adding Focus made it two and Playwright refused in strict mode, which is the right failure. Both now target the collapse control by accessible name, which is more precise regardless of how many buttons the header carries.

tickets.title: ProvidersPanel is mounted twice — the model catalog lives in one instance and the other cannot see it
acceptance: FOUND BY W12-31 AND IT BLOCKED THAT TICKET'S LAST STEP. `ModelMatrixPanel` composes its own `ProvidersPanel` to build the model catalog (`onCatalogsChange`), and W12-31 added a second mount on the new Providers tab. The discovered catalog lives in whichever instance did the discovering, so landing on the Providers tab and switching to Model Matrix leaves the Model picker empty — four e2e flows failed on exactly this.

LIFT THE CATALOG so one fetch serves both surfaces, rather than adding a third mount or duplicating the fetch. Where it lifts to is the design question: a shared hook, context, or the SettingsPage itself. Say which was chosen and why.

THE TWO SURFACES WANT DIFFERENT THINGS and the lift must serve both: the Providers tab is where entries are ADDED and tested; the matrix needs the resulting per-provider model lists plus `enabled` per entry (it distinguishes missing from unroutable, UX_SPEC §6a).

THEN MOVE THE LANDING TAB. W12-31 deliberately left Settings landing on Model Matrix because doing otherwise broke the picker. Once the catalog is shared, Settings should open on Providers — the reason most people open Settings — and the e2e flows should not need reordering to survive it.
RED FIXTURE: register a provider on the Providers tab, switch to Model Matrix, and the Model picker is populated — proven empty against the current double mount first.
Full gate per CLAUDE.md Law 3 on Node 22, including e2e.
notes: Filed 2026-08-17 at W12-31's close. W12-31 could have shipped the nicer landing by patching four e2e specs to work around the empty picker; it reverted instead, because a spec edited to tolerate a broken picker is worse than a landing tab that is merely not ideal.

tickets.title: the New Product -> New project rename — 41 occurrences across components, the palette and six e2e specs
acceptance: W12-32 decided the word (docs/design/VOCABULARY.md: "project", because the code, API, event log and registry already say it) and fixed the one term defined nowhere ("programs"). This is the mechanical sweep it deliberately did not start.

MEASURED, NOT ESTIMATED: 41 occurrences of "New Product" across `fleet/`, `palette/types.ts` and six e2e specs at filing time. Re-count before starting rather than trusting this number — the point of recording it is that the sweep is wide, not that 41 is still exact.

UI STRINGS AND TEST EXPECTATIONS ONLY. Wire shapes, event types, settings keys, API paths and the `mode: 'new'` request field keep their names — VOCABULARY.md says a rename that rewrites a durable contract is a migration and this is not one.
DO IT IN ONE PASS. A half-applied rename is worse than a consistently-old one, because then the product really does use two words for the thing this decision exists to give one name.

THE COMMAND PALETTE IS THE EASY MISS: `palette/types.ts` carries its own label, and a palette entry that still says "New Product" while the button says "New project" is exactly the drift VOCABULARY.md was written to stop.
Full gate per CLAUDE.md Law 3 on Node 22, including `pnpm --filter @dokima/web e2e`.
notes: Filed 2026-08-17 at W12-32's close. Split deliberately: the decision is durable and belongs in a doc, the sweep is mechanical and belongs in its own change where a broken spec is obviously attributable to it.

tickets.title: a pinned model, expressed as a run-scoped routing entry (D-027) — D-024 option (b) becomes usable
acceptance: UNBLOCKED BY D-027 (2026-08-18), which decided the layer question this ticket surfaced: a pin is a ROUTING fact, not an escalation mode. Translate `{ mode: 'pinned', model, providerId? }` at the composition root into (1) a run-scoped `RoleRouting` for the MAKER ROLE ONLY — `{ default: { model, fallbackChain: [] } }` — and (2) a `locked` land policy for the retry ceiling. Do NOT teach the land loop a pinned mode: its model-agnosticism is deliberate and D-027 preserves it deliberately.

THE RUN SCOPE IS THE MECHANISM AND IT IS UNUSED TODAY. `matrixFromRows` returns `{ project: ... }` only, while `ScopedRoleMatrix.run` exists and is honoured by `resolveScopedValue`'s per-role precedence. Add the run overlay there (or via a new `ResolveModelTargetInput` field that lands in `matrix.run`), so the pin goes THROUGH `route()` and never around it.

`route()` STAYING IN THE PATH IS THE ACCEPTANCE, NOT AN IMPLEMENTATION DETAIL. Prove all three still hold under a pin: `guardMakerVerifierDistinct` fires on a real collision (the verifier resolves the maker from the same matrix and therefore sees the pinned model); the fitness guard still fires, so a model unfit for the role still needs its ack; and `ResolvedRoute.scope` comes back `run`, so FR-S1's "why is this role on this model?" stays answerable.

`tierKind` IS INFERRED, NOT ASKED (D-027): `lm-studio`/`ollama` => `local` (12-attempt ceiling), everything else => `metered` (8). Read it from the resolved provider kind rather than guessing from the model string, and keep the Settings override path working.

RED FIXTURE: a stored `{ mode: 'pinned', model }` produces a run-scoped matrix entry that WINS over the project row, resolves the spawned session to exactly that model, parks under the locked ceiling instead of escalating, and leaves the verifier role resolving to something else. Proven against today's `resolvePolicyScope` refusal first.
Full gate per CLAUDE.md Law 3 on Node 22, including `pnpm --filter @dokima/web e2e`.
notes: Filed 2026-08-18 from W12-16. Eleventh instance of the defect class the W12-10 ratchet was built for, and the worst-shaped one so far: the engine is not merely uncalled, it is not exported from the gateway barrel at all — which is exactly why harbormaster reproduced its shape structurally instead of importing it. See W12-38 for the ratchet hole that let it through.

BLOCKED 2026-08-18 on a FOUNDER ARCHITECTURE DECISION, before writing code, and the ticket says why in its own third criterion: the hard half is making the pinned model be what the spawned session actually runs. Verified rather than assumed — resolveModelTarget (apps/server/src/api/pipeline/model-resolution.ts:260) takes ResolveModelTargetInput and has NO parameter through which a policy can pin anything, and it resolves through route(), whose module doc says route() is used deliberately BECAUSE it makes maker != verifier structural (C-4 / Law 5): routing a verifier role auto-resolves the maker role for the same task type and refuses a collision. So "the policy forces the model" is one of three things, and each is a contract change, not an implementation detail: (a) the land loop stops being model-agnostic, which its own module doc calls deliberate; (b) resolveModelTarget takes a policy override, which collides with the per-role matrix routing W12-06 just made meaningful — a ticket now names its expert, and the matrix routes that expert to a model, so a pinned model has to beat the expert the board chose, and someone has to decide that ordering; or (c) pinning bypasses route(), which trades D-024 option (b) for the structural C-4 guard and is the one option that should not be taken quietly. Deciding this in a commit body is exactly the move D-026 refuses to let W12-27 make, which is also why this ticket carries role architecture-designer. Needs a DECISIONS.md row first: WHICH LAYER OWNS MODEL SELECTION WHEN A POLICY PINS A MODEL.

Unblocked and re-scoped 2026-08-18 by D-027. The original acceptance said the hard half was "make the pinned model be what the spawned session runs" and left the how open; D-027 closes it. Scope changes with it: the land policy twin gains a `pinned` mode ONLY as far as the ceiling is concerned (which `locked` already provides, so possibly not at all), and the real work moves to model-resolution.ts where the run scope lives. Rewriting acceptance at claim rather than working to a superseded spec — same correction W12-30 needed.

write_scope gained run-build.ts and a new run-build-spawn.ts: wiring the pin through took run-build.ts from 397 to 406, past the 400-line cap. Second chapter split out of that file after run-build-policy.ts (W12-18), and the seam is real rather than convenient — executeBuildRun orchestrates a run, buildBuiltInSpawn constructs the session that run drives. Third time this wave the cap has caught accretion rather than one oversized write, which is the case it exists for.

Closed 2026-08-18 on D-027. The design held on contact: the pin is a run-scoped RoleRouting entry with fallbackChain: [], which makes 'never substitutes' a property of the DATA (resolveModelChain returns [model, ...fallbackChain], so a pinned chain has one rung) rather than a check someone has to remember downstream. Nothing was added to harbormaster's policy union and the land loop was not touched, so its model-agnosticism is intact. TWO FIXTURES OF W12-18's HAD TO BE INVERTED and that is the correct outcome, not collateral: they asserted the refusal that stood in for this feature, and one of them is the call-site fixture, which now proves executeBuildRun carries the pin into model resolution instead of proving it refuses. ONE FIXTURE OF MINE WAS WRONG AND THE CODE WAS RIGHT: I asserted that an unknown provider prefix (`no-such-box/model`) should refuse, but W10-60 established a slash can belong to the model id itself — 8 of the 23 models a real LM Studio serves carry one — so refusing would break them. The refusal now requires an EXPLICIT providerId that is not registered, and a vendor-namespaced pin binds normally, with its own fixture. run-build.ts hit 406 lines and buildBuiltInSpawn was split into run-build-spawn.ts. ONE HALF-WIRE, NAMED RATHER THAN LEFT: `providerKind` on the stored setting is what tierKindFor reads to infer the 8-vs-12 ceiling, and nothing writes it yet — absent reads as `metered`, the conservative direction. W12-16 is what writes it, and its acceptance now says so.

tickets.title: validate-exports cannot see an unexported dead engine — the ratchet has a blind spot in the shape of its own defect class
acceptance: W12-10 built `validate-exports.mjs` to catch "a mechanism lands complete, tested, with no production caller" — the defect found nine times and now eleven. It works by walking each package BARREL and flagging exports no non-test file outside the package calls. `runEscalationPolicy` is a complete, tested escalation engine with no production caller anywhere, and the ratchet reports 43 gaps and does not name it, because it is not in a barrel at all.

THAT IS THE WORSE CASE, NOT AN EXCLUDED ONE. An export with no caller is reachable and unused; a non-exported implementation with no caller is unreachable — it cannot be adopted without a separate barrel change, which is precisely how W12-04 (packer), W12-09 (code index) and W12-37 (pinned policy) each stayed dormant. The ratchet is blind to its own worst instance.

DECIDE THE SCOPE HONESTLY AND STATE IT. Flagging every unexported symbol with no in-package caller will surface enormous noise (private helpers are supposed to look like this). A defensible narrowing is exported-from-a-MODULE-but-not-the-barrel-and-uncalled-outside-its-file, or module-level `export`s in files nothing imports. Calibrate against this repo the way W12-10 did (529 -> 43) and record the number, including what the chosen rule still cannot see.
DO NOT RAISE THE 43 BASELINE TO MAKE THIS PASS. That rule is the ratchet's own; a new check gets its own calibrated count.

RED FIXTURE: the validator names `runEscalationPolicy` (or, if the scope decision excludes it, the fixture states which rule excludes it and why that is defensible — a documented blind spot is acceptable, an undocumented one is what this ticket is about).
Full gate per CLAUDE.md Law 3 on Node 22.
notes: Filed 2026-08-18 alongside W12-37, which is the instance that exposed it.

write_scope gained conductor.config.json at claim: a new count that nothing enforces is a report, not a ratchet, and the existing --max baseline is passed from there. If the calibrated number turns out not to be worth gating on, that decision gets recorded rather than silently skipped.

Closed 2026-08-18 at --max-buried 73. The number is the finding: the blind spot was LARGER than the debt the ratchet could see (73 buried vs 43 exported). Calibration was measured, not assumed — 90 raw, 108 once comment text stopped counting as a call, 73 once recorded fixtures and test-helper modules were excluded. The comment-stripping step is the one that mattered: runEscalationPolicy was hidden by exactly two prose mentions in loop-land-policy.ts explaining why that loop deliberately does NOT call it, so the first draft of this pass scored an explanation of why nothing calls a function as a call.
