Spot-checked three findings by hand before baselining rather than trusting the count — verifyBundleChain, runInContainerSandbox and codeSearchTool each have tests and zero production references. The barrel pass was left on its old counting on purpose and filed as W12-39: its 43 is a calibrated gate number, and sharpening the measurement underneath it is its own change with its own recalibration, not a side effect of this one.

tickets.title: the barrel export pass still counts prose as a call — its 43 is a floor, not a measurement
acceptance: W12-10's reference count is a word-boundary text match over raw file contents, and its own module doc says so plainly: it OVER-counts, because "a comment mentioning a name reads as a use". W12-38 proved that is not a theoretical bias — `runEscalationPolicy` was hidden from the new pass by exactly two prose mentions in a comment explaining why nothing calls it, until comment-stripping was added. The barrel pass still counts that way.

W12-38 DELIBERATELY DID NOT FIX IT, and that is the reason this ticket exists rather than a wider diff: the barrel pass's 43 is a calibrated baseline wired into the per-ticket gate, and sharpening the measurement underneath it would move that number for reasons unrelated to whatever ticket happened to be open. Changing a ratchet's meaning is its own change, with its own recalibration.

MEASURE FIRST, THEN DECIDE. Run the barrel pass with `stripComments` (already exported by the validator) and report the new count against 43 before changing anything. If it rises, the increase is pre-existing debt the old counting concealed and the baseline is re-set to the measured number WITH the delta recorded — which is not the forbidden "raise the baseline to make a ticket pass", and the note must say why it is not, in those terms.

RED FIXTURE: a symbol whose only non-test mention is inside a comment is reported by the barrel pass. Construct it, do not hunt for one — the fixture should still hold after whatever real instance exists today gets wired up.
Full gate per CLAUDE.md Law 3 on Node 22.
notes: Filed 2026-08-18 by W12-38, which found the bias and scoped it out on purpose rather than moving a calibrated baseline as a side effect.

Closed 2026-08-18. Measured before changing anything, as the acceptance demanded: 43 -> 62 under comment-stripped counting, so 19 already-dead symbols had been reading as used because a comment named them. Two hand-verified rather than trusted — every non-test reference to runClaimLoop and gateDecision is a comment, and loop-claim.ts:223 says in its own docstring that runClaimLoop's only callers are its own tests: the sentence admitting the defect was what concealed it. One design change the ticket did not ask for and the fixture forced: the strip now lives inside countReferences rather than in its caller. As a caller-side step the guarantee held only while every future caller remembered to pre-strip, and the constructed fixture passed against raw input while proving nothing — the exact weak-fixture shape this wave keeps finding. Cached so it is still one strip per file per run.

tickets.title: the Canvas can start a run only if the core was booted with a signing key it has no surface to set
acceptance: FOUND 2026-08-18 preparing the supervised run. W12-20 gave the Canvas a Start-run control, which posts to POST /build-runs, which calls executeBuildRunJob IN THE CORE PROCESS. That job reads process.env.DOKIMA_SIGNING_KEY and refuses without it. The signing key has no GUI surface — SUPERVISED_RUN.md says so in as many words — so the one action a user can now take from the Canvas works only if whoever started the server happened to export a variable first, in a terminal, before boot.

THIS IS THE W12-20 GAP HALF-CLOSED, NOT CLOSED. Before W12-20 the complaint was "every configuration surface is a GUI and the one action that matters is a terminal command". Today the action has a button, and the button silently depends on a terminal step taken before the process started — which is a worse failure than the old one, because it looks like it should work.

THE REFUSAL MUST REACH THE USER, AT MINIMUM. The route returns 202 and runs the job off-request, so a missing-signing-key refusal lands in the run status rather than the response. Check what the Canvas actually shows: a run that flips to `refused` with the reason visible is acceptable; a spinner that ends in silence is not. GET .../build-runs/:runId already exists to carry exactly this.

BETTER: REFUSE AT 202 TIME. The key is readable before any work starts, so the POST can decline with a named problem instead of accepting a run it knows cannot proceed. Decide between the two and record why — an honest 4xx at request time is cheaper for the caller than a status poll that reports a failure the server could have predicted.

DO NOT ADD A KEY-ENTRY UI IN THIS TICKET. Minting or storing a signing key is a credential path (Law 8) and belongs with the vault work, not with a route fix. Name the follow-up rather than growing this one.
RED FIXTURE: a POST to /build-runs with no signing key in the core environment produces an outcome the caller can read and act on, proven against the current silent-202 behaviour.
notes: Found by preparing the supervised run rather than by a test: the core had to be restarted with DOKIMA_SIGNING_KEY exported so the founder could use either path, and that is not something a first-time user would deduce. Filed rather than fixed in place because the supervised run itself is the higher-value act and this does not block it — the CLI path takes the env var from the invoking shell and works normally.

tickets.title: creating a new project asks for the absolute path of a directory the server is about to create anyway
acceptance: FOUND BY THE FOUNDER 2026-08-18, on the FIRST SCREEN of the first supervised run, which it blocked outright: "How do you know what folder directory it needs to be in? There should be a browse function... having them try to remember or type in what they need to do." The New project form is a bare required <input> labelled "Directory path" with no placeholder, no default, no example and no validation until the server rejects it.

THE SERVER ALREADY CREATES THE DIRECTORY, which makes this sharper than a missing picker. `registry-verbs.ts:41`: `if (input.mode === 'new') { await fs.mkdir(absPath, { recursive: true }); await ensureGitRepo(absPath); }`. The form asks the user to dictate the absolute path of a directory that does not exist yet and that the server is about to create. Line 66 completes the inversion: `name: input.name?.trim() || path.basename(absPath)` derives the NAME FROM THE PATH, when for a new project the name is the thing the user knows and the path is the thing they do not care about.

FOR `new`, REMOVE THE PATH INPUT ENTIRELY. Name (required) -> slug -> `<workspaceRoot>/<slug>`, with the resolved path shown read-only before the user commits so nothing happens at a location they cannot see. RESOLUTION BELONGS ON THE SERVER, not the client: the workspace root is server-side knowledge (the browser cannot know the home directory), and an API that requires a path its caller cannot compute is the same defect one layer down. `path` becomes optional on `mode: 'new'`.

A `workspaceRoot` SETTING WITH A REAL DEFAULT, and an escape. There is no concept today of where projects go — `DOKIMA_HOME` (~/.dokima) holds config, token and packs only, which is precisely why the form falls back to asking. Default it (e.g. `~/Dokima`), show the resolved path, and offer a quiet "change location" for people who keep everything under `~/Code`. A default nobody can override just relocates the annoyance.

TWO THINGS THAT WILL BITE: slug COLLISIONS (creating "My App" twice must not silently adopt the existing directory — `mkdir --recursive` succeeds on an existing dir and `registerProject` then REACTIVATES the existing record, so today the second create would quietly reopen the first project), and the `basename` name fallback, which inverts once the path is derived from the name.

RED FIXTURE: creating a project with a name and NO path succeeds, lands under the workspace root, and is refused by name rather than silently reopening when the slug already exists. Proven against the current required-path form first.
notes: Filed 2026-08-18 from the supervised run. The UX_SPEC is complicit and that is the finding worth keeping: §2 specifies the Fleet ACTIONS ("New Product / Onboard existing repo / Import") and never designs the step where the user says WHERE, so the implementation filled the hole with the laziest control that compiles and no review could catch it. Sibling ticket W12-42 covers onboard/import, which genuinely do need a path the system cannot guess.

write_scope widened twice mid-ticket, both for reasons visible only once the change existed. (1) apps/server/src/api/projects.test.ts: the route lives in projects/routes.ts but its tests live one directory up, and the route behaviour is the half worth proving — the workspace-root unit tests pass against a resolver nothing calls. (2) apps/web/e2e/**: nine specs opened New project and filled "Directory path", which is the field this ticket removes. They were rewritten to take the explicit-location escape rather than to Onboard, because they each seed state in a controlled tmpdir and genuinely need that path — which also leaves the escape hatch covered by real tests instead of only a unit fixture. Scripted in one pass rather than nine hand-edits; the Onboard call sites in the same files were left alone, verified individually.

Closed 2026-08-18. ONE ACCEPTANCE CRITERION WAS WRONG AS WRITTEN and the test suite proved it within a minute: I filed the collision guard against ANY existing directory, put it in registerProject, and it immediately reddened three unrelated tests that legitimately point `new` at a tmpdir they already created. Pointing New project at an empty folder you just made is fine, and reactivating an archived project by POSTing its path again is the DOCUMENTED un-archive route (UX_SPEC §2) — breaking either would have been a worse defect than the one being fixed. The guard moved to routes.ts and fires only on the DERIVED path, which is the case that actually matters: the user named a project, never chose a location, and would otherwise have silently adopted someone else's directory. The narrower rule is also the truer one — an explicitly chosen path that exists is the caller taking responsibility. Nine e2e specs drove the removed field and were rewritten in one scripted pass to take the explicit-location escape rather than switching to Onboard, because each seeds state in a controlled tmpdir and genuinely needs that path; the Onboard call sites in the same files were verified individually and left alone. The design-token guard also caught a raw `font-size: 0.875rem` in the new hint style — W10-06 doing its job on a two-line CSS addition.

tickets.title: onboard and import need a directory picker — the one case where the path is information only the user has
acceptance: W12-41 removes the path input from `new`, where the server creates the directory anyway. `onboard` and `import` are the opposite case: the directory already exists and its location is information ONLY the user has, so those two still need a way to say where — and typing an absolute path from memory is not it.

A BROWSER CANNOT DO THIS AND THE LOCAL ARCHITECTURE CAN. `<input type="file">` yields contents and a fake path; `webkitdirectory` yields relative paths. On a hosted web app "just add browse" is impossible. Dokima is not that: the core is a local, already-authenticated server on the same machine that already opens arbitrary project directories, so it can `readdir`. That is the local-first architecture paying for itself, and it should be stated in the design rather than discovered.

THE SECURITY QUESTION GETS AN ANSWER, NOT A WAVE-THROUGH. A listing endpoint is a filesystem-enumeration surface reachable by anything holding the bearer token. It is inside the trust boundary and the core already opens arbitrary paths, so the marginal exposure is real but bounded — say so explicitly in THREAT_MODEL.md, and decide whether roots are bounded (home + explicit additions) or unbounded. Record what was rejected.

DESIGN FOR THE COMMON CASE IN TWO CLICKS: start at sensible roots (home, the workspace root, the parents of already-registered projects) rather than at `/`. A picker that opens at the filesystem root and makes someone walk down is a worse version of typing.

FAILURE MODES ARE PART OF THIS: a path that does not exist, one that exists but is not readable, one that is a file rather than a directory, and one that is already registered. Each names what happened; `onboard`/`import` already refuse a missing directory server-side (`ProjectDirectoryError`) and that refusal should be reachable before the user commits, not after.
RED FIXTURE: onboard completes without the user typing a path, and an unreadable or non-existent selection is refused by name.
notes: Filed 2026-08-18 alongside W12-41, split deliberately rather than filed as one ticket: W12-41 is small, self-contained and unblocks a real user today, while this one carries a THREAT_MODEL decision and a new HTTP surface. Bundling them would have held the quick fix behind the security question.

write_scope WIDENED at claim time 2026-08-19. As filed it held the new picker and route but neither the call-site that renders the picker (FleetHome.tsx, where the path input actually lives) nor the registration that makes the route reachable (server.ts). Building only the listed files would have produced a route no client can call and a component nothing renders — the fourteenth instance of that defect class in this repo. The added files belong to W12-41 and W2-era tickets, all done, so nothing is claimed away from an open ticket.

write_scope widened a second time for docs/SECURITY_CONTROLS.md: the THREAT_MODEL entry this ticket requires cites a mitigating control, and SC-18 was the highest that existed. Citing SC-19 without writing it would have made the threat model reference a control that does not exist — the documentation form of the same defect as a code comment naming an unfiled ticket.

tickets.title: the signing key has no surface — a run cannot be started without a terminal
acceptance: W12-40 made the missing key an honest 409 that the Canvas already renders, so the failure is no longer silent. It is still not FIXABLE from the product: the refusal tells a user to set an environment variable and restart the core, which is the terminal step W12-20 existed to remove.

This is a CREDENTIAL path (Law 8, FR-S2): the signing key must never land in code, a settings file, a prompt or the event log. A credential REF resolved by the keychain is the shape; the raw key is not.
Blocked on the vault work rather than scoped here — W12-40 deliberately did not grow into it. Decide the storage seam first (keychain adapter vs vault), then the surface.
ALSO DECIDE: whether a first run can MINT a key rather than asking for one. A user who has never heard of receipt signing should not be asked to invent a secret.
RED FIXTURE: a user who has never opened a terminal can start a build run.
notes: Filed by W12-40, whose route comment names this ticket — an unfiled follow-up referenced from code is a comment that lies.

write_scope is PROVISIONAL — the storage seam (W12-43 acceptance) decides the real files, and whoever claims this should correct it before starting rather than force the work into a guess made before the decision.

write_scope replaced at claim: the provisional scope guessed at a SigningKeyPanel and a signing-key route, and the storage-seam decision made both unnecessary. resolveCredentialStore already exists for both platforms and the key is an HMAC secret, so the product can mint one and never has to ask — there is no panel to build.

write_scope widened for the two test-environment files. Minting means the code path now WRITES a credential, and DOKIMA_NO_KEYCHAIN was not pinned anywhere — so on darwin the suite would have written a real signing key into the developer login keychain. plan.json already records W10-04 declining to do exactly that from an automated test. The change creates the hazard, so the change owns the isolation.

Closed 2026-08-19. Proven live on a fresh DOKIMA_HOME with no key anywhere: run 1 minted, announced once and landed the ticket; run 2 minted nothing; a project holding a receipt with the key gone refused by name. No key-entry UI was built and none is needed — the provisional write_scope guessed at a SigningKeyPanel before the storage-seam decision made it unnecessary.

tickets.title: the plugin loader — build it only when there is a plugin to load
acceptance: BLOCKED BY DESIGN until a concrete plugin exists to load. W12-27 decided the trust model with zero plugins because that is cheap; the loader is the expensive, hard-to-reverse half (process boundaries, require semantics, a plugin depending on a different version of a package core already loaded) and none of it changes the trust decision.

Build createPluginContext and authorizeWithPlugin, whose behaviour is specified in docs/design/PLUGIN_SEAM.md §3.1 and §5. They were written and tested during W12-27 and withheld because validate-exports refused two exports with no caller — construct them from a real call site on the same commit.

THE CAPABILITY BOUNDARY IS STRUCTURAL, NOT PROMISED: a plugin receives PluginContext scoped to one provider entry, never CredentialStore. A refusal must be identical whether the ref exists or not, and must not consult the store.
NO FALLBACK TO THE UN-DECORATED FETCH on any plugin failure. An unauthenticated call to a subscription endpoint is the account-suspension risk D-019 gates Copilot for.
Consent is ledgered in the D-019 shape and default-off. No signature requirement — PLUGIN_SEAM.md §3.3 records why signing here would be an endorsement of the exact use the vendor prohibits.
notes: Filed by W12-27, which docs/design/PLUGIN_SEAM.md §7 names. Do not start this without a plugin in hand — the ticket exists to hold the decision, not to schedule the work.

Closed 2026-08-18, verified in the live browser rather than only in fixtures: scrolled to the bottom of the nine-question Describe form and the header is still there with every destination, Describe marked current. THE FIRST DRAFT INTRODUCED A NEW HOLE AND THE E2E SUITE CAUGHT IT: I made the main surface a project-only destination, which stranded anyone who opened the Roster with no project — the nav offered Roster, they were standing on Roster, and nothing led home. Three specs failed, all named 'toggles X and back to Fleet'. The fix is that `view: null` is ALWAYS offered and the label says which surface it currently is (Fleet with no project, Board with one). Three e2e call sites used '← Back', which no longer exists; two became a 'Fleet' click, and the third got SIMPLER — decisions-resume.spec.ts had to click Back before opening Decisions, purely because opening any view replaced the whole nav, and that detour was itself evidence of the defect. Deliberately did NOT invent tokens for the current-destination treatment: --sw-bg-subtle and --sw-border-strong do not exist, the real token set is W13-03's job, and half a system now means doing it twice — an accent border needs no new token and carries no text-contrast requirement.
tickets.title: the header scrolls away and the nav changes between views — you lose the way out mid-form
acceptance: FOUND IN A LIVE WALKTHROUGH 2026-08-18, and proven by accident: driving the browser, a click at the header coordinates landed in a textarea instead, because the header had scrolled off. On the Describe form — nine questions, well past one viewport — every navigation control disappears once you scroll. There is no way back to the board, to Settings, or anywhere, without scrolling to the top first.

THE NAV ALSO CHANGES SHAPE BETWEEN VIEWS. The workspace header offers Roster · Describe · Plan · Decisions; the Describe view offers only Back · Settings · theme. The map a user just learned disappears when they act on it, which is a large part of why the founder reported "stopping every second because it does not make sense".

STICK THE HEADER and keep the destination set STABLE across views: the same places are reachable from everywhere, with the current one marked rather than removed. Removing a destination to indicate you are in it is the thing that disorients.

THE HEADER IS ALSO UNGROUPED: seven controls at identical weight, so Describe (the primary action of a new project) looks exactly like the theme toggle. Group by kind — where you can go, what needs you, what you can set — and let weight say which is which.
RED FIXTURE: the header is reachable after scrolling a long view, and the destination set is identical in the workspace and in Describe, with the current view marked as current.
Full gate per CLAUDE.md Law 3 on Node 22, including `pnpm --filter @dokima/web e2e`.

notes: Closed 2026-08-18, each fix verified in the live browser. THE TITLE TRAP WAS WORSE THAN FILED, and reading the code is what showed it: `title` seeded from `projectName`, which is the literal string "Untitled" for an unnamed project, and `ready` only required `title.trim() !== ''` — which "Untitled" SATISFIES. So the button was disabled purely for want of an answer while the message said "Answer at least one question and give it a title", blaming a title the user had never been asked for and which the form had silently supplied. The message now names the ONE precondition actually unmet, proven by three fixtures across the three states. THE PRIMARY HAD NO CLASS AT ALL — a bare <button> inheriting the plain pill, so "Build the board" never read as the screen's action even when ENABLED; `btn-primary` at the existing 0.55 disabled opacity reads as the accent action waiting on something rather than as a disabled input. `Drafts:` captions removed from all eight fields, but the `drafts` FIELD stays: it is the section heading `buildInterviewSession` writes into the generated document, so it was always internal and correctly used there — only its doc comment ('Shown under the field') was stale, and it is now corrected in place. ONE FIXTURE OF MINE WAS WRONG: I asserted nine questions from counting a screenshot and there are eight; it now asserts against INTERVIEW_QUESTIONS.length so it cannot go stale when a question is added.
tickets.title: the Describe form has a title trap, an invisible primary, leaked internal names and no sense of length
acceptance: FOUR DEFECTS ON ONE SCREEN, all found live. (1) THE TITLE TRAP: "Working title" is pre-filled with the literal value "Untitled", so the field LOOKS answered while "Build the board" stays disabled telling you to "give it a title". A placeholder pretending to be a value is a trap, not a default.

(2) THE PRIMARY IS INVISIBLE WHEN DISABLED: "Build the board" renders grey-on-grey, indistinguishable from a disabled textarea, with the reason in 11px grey BELOW it. A disabled primary must still read as the primary, and must say what would enable it, next to itself.

(3) INTERNAL NAMES LEAK INTO THE FORM: every field is captioned `Drafts: Vision`, `Drafts: Scope`, `Drafts: User personas`. These are artifact filenames. VOCABULARY.md already forbids exactly this — internal terms are for wire shapes, not for the person answering the question. Either say what the answer is used for in the user's words, or say nothing.

(4) NO SENSE OF LENGTH OR PROGRESS: nine questions, no count, no grouping, no indication that everything is optional until you hit the disabled button at the bottom. Say up front how long this is and that blanks are skipped rather than guessed.

RED FIXTURE: the title field starts genuinely empty with "Untitled" as a placeholder; the disabled primary states its own precondition; no `Drafts:` string reaches the DOM; and the form declares its length before the first question.
Full gate per CLAUDE.md Law 3 on Node 22, including `pnpm --filter @dokima/web e2e`.

notes: Closed 2026-08-18. EVERY RATIO WAS COMPUTED, NOT ASSERTED, and doing so caught a real defect before it shipped: white on the new dark accent measures 2.46:1 and fails — so --sw-on-accent is the GROUND (7.56:1), which is the identical trap the previous dark accent had and a previous ticket fixed the same way. It now has its own guard so it cannot be reintroduced a third time. A second measurement changed a value: the hairline sits at 1.34:1 on the ground, fine as decoration and too weak for a divider that carries structure, so --sw-border-strong was added at 3.23:1 for WCAG 1.4.11 while --sw-border stays decorative. TWO THINGS THE OLD SYSTEM SIMPLY LACKED: a raised surface (there was no --sw-surface at all, so cards and panes had nothing to sit on and the app was one flat sheet with lines on it), and range in the type scale (0.65-1.25rem, so every text on a Fleet card lived inside four pixels). tokens.json is GENERATED from styles.css rather than hand-maintained, with a guard asserting it has not drifted — a generated file nothing re-checks is how a second copy starts lying. HONEST LIMIT, STATED RATHER THAN IMPLIED: the palette landed and the screens are NOT re-skinned, exactly as the acceptance required. `.readout` currently has no consumer, which is the no-caller shape this board has caught eleven times — deliberate here (W13-05/06 consume it) but worth naming, because the exports ratchet reads TypeScript and cannot see an unused CSS class at all.
tickets.title: no design system exists — styles.css is a guardrail, not a token set, and Phase 3.5 never ran
acceptance: THE ROOT CAUSE OF "IT LOOKS HORRIBLE", AND IT IS STRUCTURAL. apps/web has 42 passing style guards — no hex outside the token block, no raw px, no off-scale font-size, documented contrast per token. That system enforces CONSISTENCY and cannot express QUALITY: it can say "you used the correct grey", never "this screen has no composition". 42 green tests coexist with an unusable UI, and that is why nobody caught it.

PHASE 3.5 NEVER RAN. The SDLC this repo ships defines a Design Loop — ux-researcher flows, design-system-lead tokens and component inventory, ux-engineer mockups — and `docs/design/` contains UX_SPEC, VOCABULARY, contracts and policies but NO tokens.json and NO components.md. Those are exactly the design-system-lead outputs. The product went from architecture to implementation and skipped its own design phase.

DIRECTION CHOSEN BY THE FOUNDER 2026-08-18: INSTRUMENT PANEL. Dense, precise, high-signal — a tool for professionals. Deep slate ground, ONE signal accent, monospace for every number, and state encoded in FORM (a stripe, a chip, a bar) not only in text. Record it in VISUAL_DIRECTION.md with what was rejected (assay-office warmth; quiet-workshop calm) so the next surface does not re-litigate it.

A REAL TYPE SCALE IS THE FIRST DELIVERABLE. Today every text on the Fleet card lives inside a 4px range (11–15px), which is why nothing reads as more important than anything else. The scale must have enough range to carry hierarchy, and numbers get a tabular monospace face because this product is mostly numbers.

DO NOT RE-SKIN ANY SCREEN IN THIS TICKET. Tokens and direction only, so the surfaces that follow inherit one system rather than three interpretations. The guards stay and get extended to the new scale.
Full gate per CLAUDE.md Law 3 on Node 22, including `pnpm --filter @dokima/web e2e`.

notes: Closed 2026-08-18. THE INVENTORY IS THE DELIVERABLE AND IT WAS MEASURED, NOT ESTIMATED: 51 places re-declare the same card border across 14 stylesheets, 8 competing empty-state classes across 7 files, and all 15 files reach for semantic state tokens with no shared component (53 usages). MY FIRST COUNT WAS WRONG AND THE GUARD CAUGHT IT — a shell glob of `apps/web/src/*/*.css` returned 49 because it never reaches board/drawer/drawer.css two levels down; the test walks the tree and found 51. The baseline is the true number and the doc records why the first one differed, since the measurement IS the point of this ticket. THE SHARPEST FINDING is `.empty-state`: it already existed in styles.css and seven surfaces ignored it and wrote their own. That is the whole problem in miniature — a shared thing existing is not enough, it has to be the path of least resistance — and it is why the doc's rule says a primitive with three surviving competitors is not shared, it is a fourth option. Nothing is applied to any surface, deliberately: reviewing a system and its first three interpretations in one diff is how both get waved through. The 51 is now a ratchet that W13-05/06 must drive down and may not raise.
tickets.title: every card, pane, chip and empty state is bespoke CSS — there is no component inventory
acceptance: W13-03 gives the system its tokens; this gives it its parts. The same objects are re-implemented per surface today — a card is written one way in fleet.css and another in board.css, panes carry their own chrome, chips and empty states are improvised per screen.

INVENTORY WHAT ACTUALLY EXISTS FIRST, from the captured frames and the live app, rather than designing an idealised set: card, pane, lane column, ticket, chip/badge, stat, empty state, form field, primary/secondary/quiet button, tab. Name each one and say which surfaces use it.

EMPTY STATES ARE A COMPONENT, not an afterthought — UX_SPEC §2b already has a table of them and they are currently improvised per screen. A screen with nothing in it is the one most likely to be someone's first.

STATE IS A COMPONENT CONCERN: the direction says state is encoded in form. Decide once how "needs you", "running", "blocked" and "idle" look, so a Fleet card and a board lane say the same thing the same way.
RED FIXTURE: the shared components render from tokens only, and the guards prove no surface re-declares a component's colours locally.
Full gate per CLAUDE.md Law 3 on Node 22, including `pnpm --filter @dokima/web e2e`.

notes: Closed 2026-08-18, verified live: the one project with Ready 1 is now the thing the eye finds, and six idle cards recede to grey zeros. THREE LEVELS, NOT TWO, and that was a design decision the acceptance did not anticipate: 'a decision is waiting' and 'there is work to do' are different claims on a person, so only the first takes the attention stripe. A card with Ready 1 stops reading as idle without shouting. THE SORT WAS ALREADY BUILT AND ALREADY WIRED — sortByAttention exists, matches UX_SPEC §2 exactly, and FleetHome calls it. Checked because this board has found eleven mechanisms with no caller; this was not one. The gap was purely that nothing VISUAL expressed what the sort already knew. TWO FIXES THE INVENTORY MADE OBVIOUS: the decide count used --sw-danger, which says 'something is wrong' when the truth is 'a person is needed' — under W13-04's one-meaning-per-token rule that is now --sw-attention; and .project-card__board dt was set to 60% opacity against a dd at the same size, which is precisely why label and number read at equal weight and the card had no hierarchy. Dead CSS deleted rather than left: the heartbeat dot is drawn by .state::before now, and an orphaned rule is the same no-caller shape the style guards cannot see. Duplication ratchet 51 -> 50.
tickets.title: a Fleet card with work waiting looks identical to one with nothing to do
acceptance: SEEN LIVE: six project cards, every one reading "Not started · Ready 0 · Blocked 0 · Done 0 · No berths running · $0.00 today". The one project with Ready 1 was visually indistinguishable from five with nothing to do.

UX_SPEC §2 ALREADY SPECIFIES THE BEHAVIOUR AND IT WAS NOT BUILT: cards sort "needs you first" (pending Decide desc, then stalest heartbeat), and the pending-Decide count is "the only number rendered in the attention color". Implement the spec that exists before inventing new rules.

ENCODE STATE IN FORM, per the chosen direction — a card that needs you is a different SHAPE, not the same shape with a different digit. Labels shrink, numbers carry, and a project with nothing happening should recede rather than compete.
THE TWO ACTIONS ARE NOT EQUAL: Open is what you do every time and Archive is rare and semi-destructive, yet they render at identical weight. Fix the weighting.
RED FIXTURE: a card with pending work is distinguishable from an idle card by something other than the digit — asserted on a class or attribute, not a screenshot — and the sort puts it first.
Full gate per CLAUDE.md Law 3 on Node 22, including `pnpm --filter @dokima/web e2e`.

notes: Closed 2026-08-18, verified live at each step. THE FIX WAS THE LAYOUT MODEL, NOT THE CONSTANT: `auto-fit` + `1fr` splits a row evenly regardless of content, so five empty lanes took the same width as the one holding a card. Flex sizes to content — occupied columns grow, empty ones take only their header — and `--sw-board-column-min` is UNTOUCHED, which matters because W10-32 raised it on a hunch and W12-30 had to correct that. The empty case got its own separate value rather than re-litigating a constant two tickets already measured. board.css RECORDED A CONSTRAINT I HAD TO RESPECT and nearly broke: empty columns deliberately recede rather than vanish, because they are still drop targets and disappearing ones would move the remaining columns under the cursor mid-drag. This ticket changes their WIDTH, never their presence, and there is a fixture asserting that so a later 'tidy-up' cannot remove them. THE FIRST VALUE WAS HALF A REM SHORT: at 5.5rem 'In Progress' wrapped to two lines, making the empty columns taller than the thing they were receding behind; measured on screen and corrected to 6.25rem, with the reasoning recorded beside the constant in the same spirit as the note above it. The select had NO width constraint at all — it inherited the browser's intrinsic width and hung over the bottom edge of a card narrower than itself. Duplication ratchet 50 -> 49.
tickets.title: the board is six equal empty columns and the ticket card is narrower than its own title
acceptance: SEEN LIVE on a one-ticket board: six lane columns at equal width, five of them empty, filling ~85% of the pane; the single ticket in a ~130px box with its title wrapped over three lines; and a raw `Move to…` <select> overflowing the card's bottom edge.

LANE WIDTH SHOULD FOLLOW CONTENT, not a fixed six-way split. W10-32 and W12-30 both warn against shrinking `--sw-board-column-min` on a hunch — so measure, and do not re-litigate that constant without evidence.

AN EMPTY LANE IS NOT A BOX: five empty bordered columns are noise that outweighs the one real card. Decide how an empty lane reads at rest (collapsed, ghosted, or a single line) and let occupied lanes have the room.
THE TICKET CARD IS THE PRODUCT'S ATOM and currently cannot hold a normal-length title. Give it a real minimum, and replace the in-card raw select with something that fits the card it lives in.
RED FIXTURE: a board with one ticket in one lane does not render five equal empty columns, and the ticket card holds a realistic title without overflow.
Full gate per CLAUDE.md Law 3 on Node 22, including `pnpm --filter @dokima/web e2e`.

notes: Closed 2026-08-18. THE WALKER WAS ALREADY BROKEN AND NOBODY KNEW — the sharpest finding, and the ticket's own premise one layer deeper. It had not run since W12-36 renamed 'New Product', and W12-41's form change broke it again; a capture script nothing runs stops working and says nothing. Repairing it was the first act of this ticket. NO NEW DEPENDENCY, verified before deciding: Playwright emits 8-bit truecolour non-interlaced PNG (read from a real capture's IHDR), which node:zlib plus the five PNG filters decodes in ~60 lines. The decoder was checked against a known pixel before anything was built on it — the New Product button read [46,107,255], exactly the old #2e6bff accent token. pixelmatch + pngjs would have been a TECH_STACK decision for a repo that ships five runtime dependencies on purpose. THE THRESHOLD IS MEASURED: my first attempt used two existing runs and got 1-3.8% drift, which was real UI change, not noise — they were captured 16 minutes apart during active W12 work. Capturing twice on identical code gave the true floor: 16 of 21 frames pixel-identical, worst 0.21% (timestamps and generated ids). 0.5% is ~2.4x that and still fails on anything structural. The per-channel tolerance is deliberately small because measurement showed it barely matters (2.85% -> 2.70%); the ratio does the work. --out was added to the capture script because gating on every ticket would otherwise have added ~1MB of unread PNGs to the repo per ticket.
tickets.title: nothing compares the captured frames — the UI can rot silently between waves
acceptance: THE ACCEPTANCE WALKER ALREADY CAPTURES 21 FRAMES EVERY RUN AND NOTHING EVER LOOKS AT THEM. That is how a UI reaches "it looks horrible" with 42 style guards green: the guards check declarations, the frames check nothing, and no gate closes the loop between them.

COMPARE FRAMES ACROSS RUNS and fail on a material change that no ticket claimed. The point is not pixel equality — anti-aliasing and fonts drift — so pick a tolerance and justify it, the same way W12-38 and W12-39 calibrated their counts rather than assuming.

A DIFF IS NOT AUTOMATICALLY A DEFECT: a ticket that intends to change a screen must be able to accept the new baseline, and that acceptance must be explicit and recorded rather than a silent overwrite. Decide the shape of that and write it down.
DO NOT GATE ON THIS UNTIL W13-05 AND W13-06 HAVE LANDED — baselining a UI mid-redesign bakes in the thing being fixed.
RED FIXTURE: a deliberately altered frame fails the check by name, and an accepted baseline passes.
Full gate per CLAUDE.md Law 3 on Node 22.

tickets.title: the Node-version guard covers the CLI and not the test runner, which is where it actually bites
acceptance: REPORTED AS "tests failed" 2026-08-18 BY A STOP HOOK, and they had not. The full gate is green on Node 22 — 3633 tests, 69 e2e, lint and typecheck clean, all exit 0. The hook runs in its own shell, which does not inherit this session's `fnm use 22`: fnm's default here is v24.14.0 and a shell without fnm at all gets Homebrew's v26.7.0. Reproduced directly: `NODE_MODULE_VERSION 127 ... requires 147`, 17 of 27 failures in one file.

THE GUARD ALREADY EXISTS AND IS UNREACHABLE FROM HERE. W12-24 built `checkNodeSupported` in apps/server/src/bootstrap/node-abi-guard.mjs, and its message is exactly right — it names the product, the versions, and the fix. It runs on the CLI bootstrap path only. Tests, CI and hooks never touch that path, so the place the trap is actually sprung is the one place with no guard.

REUSE IT, DO NOT COPY IT. A second implementation of the same check is the duplication class this board has now caught four times (three copies of the adapter dispatch, four of the provider-kind table). `pretest` runs automatically before `test` under npm and pnpm, which makes it the natural seam.

REFUSE, DO NOT AUTO-SWITCH. Silently re-execing under a different Node would hide which version the suite actually ran on, and a test suite lying about its own runtime is worse than one that stops. Say what is wrong and what to type.
RED FIXTURE: the check refuses a mismatched version by name and passes the supported one, proven against `engines.node` rather than a hardcoded literal so it cannot drift when the engine moves.
Full gate per CLAUDE.md Law 3 on Node 22.
notes: Filed 2026-08-18 from a stop-hook report of failing tests. The tests were fine; the report was accurate about the exit code and wrong about the cause, which is exactly the confusion the guard exists to prevent.

Closed 2026-08-18. Verified both directions on real interpreters rather than by mocking: silent exit 0 on Node 22, and on Homebrew's Node 26 the named refusal naming the product, both versions and the exact command to type. ONE FIXTURE OF MINE FAILED ON MY OWN PROSE: the assertion that this file does not reimplement the ABI table tripped on the doc comment, which QUOTES the NODE_MODULE_VERSION error it exists to explain. Fixed by asserting against the comment-stripped source using W12-39's own stripComments — the same lesson that ticket learned, that prose about a thing is not the thing, and the third time this session a comment has been mistaken for code by a check.

tickets.title: the model is never told the Completion Manifest contract — asked in prose, validated as a schema
acceptance: FOUND BY THE FIRST SUPERVISED RUN, 2026-08-18 — the exact class of defect that run exists to catch, and one no fixture could have found. On a local model the agent did the work CORRECTLY: wrote subtract(a,b), ran verify to exit 0, and committed it on its own branch in its own worktree. The loop then auto-blocked with "ladder attempt cap (2) reached without a close · exitCode=0 no completion manifest returned" on both attempts, and released the ticket back to ready.

THE CONTRACT IS NEVER STATED. `parseCompletionManifest` requires strict JSON with `ticket: string`, `files: string[]`, `commits: string[]`, `evidence: string[]` and `verify: {command, exit}`. The only thing the model is ever told is one line of prose: "RETURN: Completion Manifest (files produced, verify result, evidence)". It is never told the output must be JSON, never given the field names, and never shown an example. The system asks in words and validates against a schema.

THERE IS ALSO NO SYSTEM MESSAGE AT ALL: `gateway-session.ts` builds `messages` as `[{ role: user, content: input.prompt }]`. Every instruction the model will ever receive is the rendered HANDOFF, which makes that render the ONLY place a contract can live — and it does not carry one.

THE PARSER IS NOT THE PROBLEM AND MUST NOT BE LOOSENED. It already tries three tiers (whole text, embedded balanced object, fenced block) and strips thinking blocks. Making it accept prose would mean accepting an unverifiable claim, which is the opposite of what a manifest is for. Fix the instruction, not the check.

STATE THE SHAPE AND SHOW ONE FILLED EXAMPLE. A schema a model has to infer is a schema it will get wrong; the example is what makes the difference for a smaller local model, which is precisely the configuration this product guarantees (D-024 option a, C-1). Keep the block compact — it is prepended to every session prompt and competes with the packed context for the window.

RED FIXTURE: the rendered handoff names every required field and carries a parseable example, proven by feeding that example straight into `parseCompletionManifest`; and a fake-model session that returns the documented shape closes, where the same session returning prose does not. Fixtures only, never a live call (law 9a).
notes: Filed 2026-08-18 from the first supervised run. Everything fixture-tested worked — worktree isolation, the MCP allowlist, the tool loop, SC-17/SC-01, the commit path — and the one thing no fixture could catch (that the model is never told the output contract) is what broke. The work from that run is still on branch sw/T-1-implement-subtract-a-b-in-src-math-mjs in /tmp/dokima-run, correct and verified.

write_scope gained packages/loop/src/index.ts: `parseCompletionManifest` — the function that decides whether a session closed a ticket — was not exported from the barrel, so nothing outside @dokima/loop could assert a session against the REAL contract without a deep import, which law 6 forbids across package boundaries. The harbormaster fixture that proves 'documented shape closes, prose does not' needs exactly that function; asserting against a re-implementation of it would prove nothing.

write_scope gained session-prompt.ts: adding the system message took gateway-session.ts from 394 to 429 lines, past the 400-line cap, caught by the repo-wide validator in the full gate. The seam is real rather than convenient — this is the standing instruction every session receives, while gateway-session.ts is the loop that runs one. Fourth time this wave the cap has caught accretion rather than a single oversized write.

Closed 2026-08-18. THE STRONGEST FIXTURE IS THAT THE EXAMPLE IN THE PROMPT IS FED TO THE REAL PARSER — a documented shape the parser rejects would be worse than no documentation, because it would look right and fail identically. Building it surfaced a second gap: `parseCompletionManifest`, the function that decides whether a session closed a ticket, was NOT exported from @dokima/loop's barrel, so nothing outside that package could assert a session against the real contract without a deep import (law 6). Asserting against a re-implementation would have proved nothing. TWO LEGACY FIXTURES CORRECTLY BROKE: they pinned the handoff byte-for-byte, which makes improving a prompt look like a regression — the field lines are still asserted exactly, and the RETURN section is now asserted by its CONTRACT (names every required field, carries a parseable example) rather than its literal text. The parser was deliberately not loosened: it already tries three tiers and strips thinking blocks, and making it accept prose would mean accepting an unverifiable claim, which is the opposite of what a manifest is for. The cap caught accretion a fourth time this wave (394 -> 429), so the system prompt became its own chapter.

tickets.title: a local endpoint cannot be sent the one option it needs — no per-provider request fields
acceptance: FOUND IN LIVE TESTING 2026-08-18 against a remote LM Studio. `prism-ml/bonsai-27b` is a REASONING model: it spends ~200 tokens thinking before answering, and the only thing that turns that off is the OpenAI-compatible `reasoning_effort` field — measured across four candidates, where `chat_template_kwargs.enable_thinking` and a `/no_think` suffix both did nothing and `reasoning_effort: "none"` took reasoning_tokens to 0.

THE ADAPTER CANNOT SEND IT. `OaiCompatProvider.chat` builds a fixed body — model, messages, temperature, max_tokens, stop, tools — with no passthrough. So a user who configures a local reasoning model through the GUI has no way to configure the one option that model needs, which cuts against D-024 option (a): local-only is a guaranteed-supported configuration, and local endpoints are exactly where per-model quirks live.

MERGE, NEVER CLOBBER. The passthrough must not be able to overwrite `model`, `messages` or `tools` — a config field that can rewrite the routed model would let a provider entry silently defeat the model matrix and, with it, the maker!=verifier separation that routing enforces. Spread the extras FIRST and let the derived fields win, and prove that with a fixture rather than a comment.

IT IS A PROVIDER-ENTRY FIELD, not a per-call one: it describes the endpoint, so it belongs beside baseUrl and headers in the registry, and it must survive validation the same way the other provider fields do.

RED FIXTURE: a configured extra reaches the request body; an extra that tries to override `model` or `messages` does NOT; and a provider without one sends exactly the body it sends today (no empty keys, no behaviour change for the 12 existing entries).
Full gate per CLAUDE.md Law 3 on Node 22.
notes: Filed 2026-08-18 from live testing. The founder asked what happens if thinking is disabled on bonsai-27b, and answering it honestly required the product to be able to send the field at all.

write_scope widened along the whole chain, and the widening IS the point: a provider field is only real if it survives every hop from the HTTP body to the adapter. validate.ts’s own comment names this — "validating project/location and then omitting them here would ship the exact settable-and-inert field the W10-57 note warns about" — so the same five hops were followed deliberately: wire (snake_case) -> registry entry -> ResolvedModelTarget -> GatewayConfig -> adapter constructor. Also gained providers-wire.ts: the field took providers-routes.ts from 397 to 405 lines, and the wire mapping is a real seam (published snake_case contract vs the registry’s internal shape) rather than a convenient one.

Closed 2026-08-18, and the feature was verified by USING it rather than only by fixtures: configured `{reasoning_effort: none}` on the live remote endpoint through the real HTTP route, then re-ran the same ticket on the same model. THE RESULT IS THE INTERESTING PART. With thinking ON, bonsai-27b used `write` and clobbered `add()` out of math.mjs — verify failed with 'add is not a function' and it burned nine verify calls flailing. With thinking OFF it produced CORRECT code (both functions present, `node src/check.mjs` prints OK) in 88s instead of 136s. It still parked, but for a completely different and much better reason: it used all twelve tool turns (DEFAULT_MAX_TOOL_ITERATIONS) before emitting a manifest, so the work is right and unclosed rather than wrong. SECOND FINDING, RECORDED NOT FIXED: `maxIterations` is a session option that nothing in apps/server ever sets, so the cap is effectively hard-coded at 12 — less severe than a no-caller mechanism because the default is sensible, but a chatty local model cannot be given more room without editing source. The merge order carries the real safety property and has its own fixture: extras are spread FIRST so `model`/`messages` always win, because a provider entry able to rewrite the routed model would silently defeat the model matrix and the maker!=verifier separation routing enforces.

tickets.title: the tool-turn cap is a session option nothing ever sets — hard-coded at 12 for every model
acceptance: FOUND IN LIVE TESTING 2026-08-18, immediately after W13-10. With thinking disabled, `prism-ml/bonsai-27b` produced CORRECT work — both functions present, `node src/check.mjs` printing OK — and still parked, because it used all twelve tool turns before emitting a manifest. The work was right and unclosed. `maxIterations` is a `GatewaySpawnSessionOptions` field and NOTHING in apps/server sets it, so `DEFAULT_MAX_TOOL_ITERATIONS = 12` is the value every model gets.

THE CAP MUST STAY. It exists for T-27 ("a session iterates tool calls indefinitely without producing a manifest") and this run is exactly why: an unbounded session on a chatty model would spend a budget going nowhere. This makes the cap CONFIGURABLE, never optional.

A CEILING, NOT A FREE NUMBER: a setting that accepts any value re-opens T-27 by configuration. Pick a maximum, refuse above it by name the way `resolvePolicyScope` refuses a malformed policy, and say in the refusal what the ceiling is.

THE DEFAULT DOES NOT MOVE. 12 is right for a capable model — the qwen run landed in four calls — and raising it for everyone would spend other people's budget to accommodate one weak model. This is a knob for the person who chose a chatty local model, which is precisely D-024 option (a) territory.

RED FIXTURE: a configured value reaches the session; an absent one still yields 12; a value over the ceiling is refused BY NAME rather than clamped silently, because silently running a different number than the one configured is the class of defect this board keeps finding.
Full gate per CLAUDE.md Law 3 on Node 22.
notes: Filed 2026-08-18 from the bonsai no-think run. Second finding of that experiment; the first was W13-10.

write_scope corrected: I filed run-build-policy.test.ts and it does not exist — the policy resolver's tests live in run-build.test.ts beside the call-site fixture that proves executeBuildRun actually reads the setting, which is the more valuable place for them anyway. Creating the file I had assumed produced a test suite vitest silently reported as 'no tests'.

Closed 2026-08-18, and THE EXPERIMENT THAT MOTIVATED IT FAILED — recorded because a negative result that changes the conclusion is worth more than a fix that looks good. The hypothesis was that bonsai-27b parked because twelve tool turns were too few: with thinking off it produced correct work and used exactly twelve. Given thirty it used twenty across two attempts, produced correct work again, and STILL returned no manifest. The cap was never the binding constraint; the model simply cannot emit the manifest, whatever budget it has. VERIFIED THE SETTING ACTUALLY TAKES EFFECT rather than assuming it from a null result — set it to 2 and the same run went from 226s to 15s. Without that check I could not have told 'the cap is not the problem' apart from 'my setting never reached the session', which are opposite conclusions with the same symptom. The fix stands on its own merits: maxIterations was a GatewaySpawnSessionOptions field nothing in apps/server ever set, so 12 was every model's value and unreachable without editing source. It refuses above a ceiling rather than clamping, because a setting that accepts any value re-opens T-27 by configuration, and silently running a different number than the one configured is the defect class this board keeps finding. One correction on the way: I filed run-build-policy.test.ts, which does not exist — the policy tests live in run-build.test.ts, and creating the file I had assumed produced a suite vitest reported as 'no tests'.

tickets.title: a killed run strands its ticket in in_progress forever — the watchdog that would recover it has no caller
acceptance: FOUND IN LIVE TESTING 2026-08-19. A run against a slow local 27b was killed at a ten-minute ceiling mid-session. T-1 was left in `in_progress` with its owner gone, and the NEXT run reported "0 landed, 0 parked" in zero seconds — the ticket was not claimable, not failed, not recoverable, and nothing said why. A crash, a laptop lid, or a Ctrl-C does the same thing.

THE RECOVERY MECHANISM IS BUILT AND HAS NO CALLER. `runWatchdogSession` (watchdog-session.ts) and `createFileStopSwitch` both sit in the buried-exports list from W12-38 — complete, tested, reachable from nothing. `watchdog-session.ts`'s own docstring says it: "`apps/*` or `loop-claim.ts`/`loop-land.ts` calls `runWatchdogSession`" is listed as what does NOT happen. Twelfth instance of the defect class, and the first one where the missing wire costs a user their work rather than a feature.

A STALE CLAIM IS A DERIVABLE FACT, NOT A GUESS: the events carry `ticket.claimed`/`ticket.started` with an actor and a timestamp, and the heartbeat freshness the Fleet card already renders is the same signal. Decide what makes a claim stale and say it in one place — do not spread the rule across the loop and the UI.

RECLAIM MUST GO THROUGH THE VERBS, NEVER AROUND THEM (Law 4, C-2/C-3). A stranded ticket returns to `ready` by an event with an actor and a reason, so the log explains what happened; a direct status write would be exactly the kind of path this product refuses to have.

DO NOT AUTO-KILL A LIVE SESSION. A slow model is not a dead one — the run this was found in was making real progress at five reads a minute when it was killed from outside. Whatever the staleness rule is, it must not reap a session that is still calling tools.
RED FIXTURE: a ticket claimed by an actor that never finished is recoverable on the next run, by name and with an event explaining it; and a ticket whose session is still active is NOT.
notes: Filed 2026-08-19 from live testing of qwen3.8-27b. The immediate cause was an external ten-minute kill, but the exposure is general: nothing in the product recovers a claim whose owner vanished. Worth noting the two mechanisms that would fix it were both already written — this is a wiring ticket, not a design one.

Closed 2026-08-19, verified against GENUINELY STRANDED STATE rather than a fixture: the ticket that had been stuck in in_progress since the qwen3.8 crash was reclaimed, explained in the log, and landed in six seconds on coder-next. THE EVENT LOG IS THE HEARTBEAT, and that is what makes this need no new bookkeeping: a live session emits an mcp.tool_call.completed per tool call, so recent events ARE proof of life. `claimedAt` alone could not do it — a legitimately long session and an abandoned one look identical by that measure, which is the trap the acceptance warned about ('do not auto-kill a live session'). There is a fixture for exactly that case: claimed an hour ago, active ten seconds ago, not reclaimed. THE BOUND IS DERIVED, NOT PICKED ROUND: the longest silence a healthy session can produce is one verify (10 min) plus one local model call (5 min), so 30 minutes clears it by a factor of two, and a fixture asserts the relationship rather than the number. I did NOT wire runWatchdogSession as the ticket speculated — it is a watchdog for a session that is still running, a different problem from a session that is gone, and adopting it here would have been reaching for a mechanism because it existed rather than because it fit.

tickets.title: a provider timeout crashes the whole run — ProviderTimeoutError is caught nowhere in the loop
acceptance: FOUND IN LIVE TESTING 2026-08-19 on `qwen3.8-27b`, a 27B dense model on local hardware. One model call exceeded the 300s provider timeout and `ProviderTimeoutError` propagated out of `runLandLoop` uncaught, killing the run with a stack trace. `grep` confirms it: nothing in packages/loop or packages/harbormaster catches it.

THE WORK WAS CORRECT AND WAS LOST TO THE OPERATOR. The first four tool calls were read -> edit -> verify -> commit, and the branch holds both functions with `node src/check.mjs` printing OK. The model then wandered for eight more read/list calls and one of them timed out. So a run can produce complete, verified, committed work and end in a stack trace with the ticket stranded in `in_progress` — the operator sees a crash, not a result.

A SLOW PROVIDER IS AN EXPECTED CONDITION, NOT AN EXCEPTION. This product guarantees local-only works (D-024 option a, C-1), and local hardware running a 27B model is exactly where a 300s call comes from. A timeout should end the ATTEMPT the way any other failed attempt ends — evidence, the ladder, a park — not the process.

PARK WITH THE TRUTH, and the truth here is specific: "the model did not respond within Ns" is a different fact from "the model produced no manifest", and a user choosing a smaller model needs to be able to tell them apart. Say which one happened.
PAIRS WITH W13-12 AND DOES NOT REPLACE IT: this stops the loop crashing, that recovers a claim whose owner vanished anyway. Both are needed — a laptop lid still strands a ticket even with this fixed.

RED FIXTURE: a provider that times out ends the attempt with evidence naming the timeout, the ladder continues or parks per policy, and the ticket does NOT remain in in_progress. Fake provider, never a live call (law 9a).
notes: Filed 2026-08-19 from the qwen3.8-27b run. Second orphaning cause found in one session — W13-12 came from an external kill, this one is the product crashing on its own timeout, which is the more common case since it needs no outside interference.

Closed 2026-08-19. THE PREDICATE IS AN EXPLICIT LIST, NOT A NAME PREFIX OR A CATCH-ALL, and that choice is the ticket: these five provider errors have no common ancestor, so matching on `name.startsWith('Provider')` would silently start swallowing any future class named that way — including one that means we have a bug — and a bare catch would turn a crash in the close gate into a quiet 'attempt failed', which is exactly the silence this product exists to refuse. There is a fixture asserting a TypeError still propagates. THE MESSAGE IS DELIBERATELY DISTINCT from 'no completion manifest returned': 'it did not answer in time' and 'it answered without a manifest' point at different fixes — a longer timeout versus a different model — and someone choosing a smaller model has to be able to tell them apart. loop-land.ts was sitting EXACTLY on the 400-line cap, so any addition broke it; `attemptOnce` moved out wholesale into loop-land-session.ts rather than shaving comments, which is the honest seam (one attempt, versus the ladder that decides what to do about it). Pairs with W13-12 and does not replace it: this stops the loop crashing, that recovers a claim whose owner vanished anyway — a closed laptop lid still strands a ticket with this fixed.

tickets.title: seven different limits can stop a run and nothing documents them together
acceptance: RAISED BY THE FOUNDER 2026-08-19 after three separate limits stopped runs in one session — a 12-turn tool cap, a 2-attempt ladder cap, and a 300s request timeout. The question "what is the limit and why" has no answer anywhere in the docs; grep finds the numbers only in source and in a STATUS entry written the same day.

THE INCONSISTENCY IS REAL AND UNDOCUMENTED: `oai-compat` carries a 300_000ms request timeout while `anthropic`, `openai`, `copilot` and `vertex` all carry 60_000ms. Five times longer for local endpoints is DEFENSIBLE — a 27B model on a laptop genuinely takes minutes where a hosted one takes seconds — but nothing says so, so it reads as an accident. State the reason next to the number.

ONE TABLE, EVERY LIMIT: request timeout (per provider kind), health timeout, verify timeout, validator timeout, tool-iteration cap, ladder attempt cap, convergence ceiling. For each: the value, WHY that value, what happens when it fires, and whether it is configurable.

THE TEST IS "CAN A USER TELL WHICH ONE STOPPED THEM": the refusals are already specific — "ladder attempt cap (2) reached without a close", "exceeded the per-session tool-iteration budget", "request timed out after 300000ms" — so the gap is discovery, not wording. The doc must make each message findable, keyed by the text a user will actually see.

DO NOT CHANGE ANY VALUE. Every one was chosen for a reason recorded somewhere in the source, and re-tuning them while documenting them would mean shipping an untested behaviour change under cover of a docs ticket.
Full gate per CLAUDE.md Law 3 on Node 22.
notes: Filed 2026-08-19. The founder's words: "we shouldn't have a wall clock that is confusing" — raised after I used "wall clock" as jargon, which is itself the VOCABULARY.md failure mode.

Closed 2026-08-19. THE ANSWER TO THE QUESTION AS ASKED IS THAT THERE IS NO CLOCK: nothing in Dokima counts a run's total elapsed time and kills it. What exists is seven specific bounds on specific things — one request, one command, one session's turns, one ticket's attempts — and the doc leads with that, because 'we shouldn't have a wall clock that is confusing' is answered better by 'there isn't one, here is what there is' than by a table alone. Indexed BY THE MESSAGE A USER ACTUALLY SEES rather than by internal constant name, since the gap was discovery and not wording — the refusals were already specific. The one genuine inconsistency is now stated where it lives: oai-compat's 300s request timeout against 60s for every hosted kind, annotated in the source with the measurement behind it (a 27B local model exceeding 300s in live testing, which is what W13-13 was filed for) so it reads as a decision rather than an accident. NO VALUE WAS CHANGED — re-tuning while documenting would have shipped an untested behaviour change under cover of a docs ticket.

tickets.title: the session waits blind and kills healthy generations — no streaming, and a total-duration timeout
acceptance: RAISED BY THE FOUNDER 2026-08-19: "shouldn't we have streaming with local models and shouldn't we be monitoring? as long as it's streaming responses we should be leaving it open, not having arbitrary timeouts." Correct on all three counts, and verified in source.

THE TIMEOUT IS TOTAL-DURATION, NOT IDLE. `fetchRaw` uses `AbortSignal.timeout(timeoutMs)`, which aborts the whole request at N ms REGARDLESS of whether tokens are arriving. A local 27B generating healthily for five minutes is killed exactly like a hung endpoint, and W13-13 was filed for a case that was very likely this — the model had produced correct work and was still going.

THE RIGHT CONTROL IS TIME SINCE THE LAST TOKEN. A stream that is producing is alive by definition; a stream silent for N seconds is hung whatever its total duration. Replace duration with idle on the streaming path, and say so in RUN_LIMITS.md, which currently documents the duration bound as if it were the right one.

FEASIBILITY WAS MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED: LM Studio streams `tool_calls` deltas AND emits a `stream_options.include_usage` chunk, so a streamed session can still meter spend and still drive the tool loop. Without the usage chunk this would not be possible without giving up the ledger, which is not a trade this product can make.

THE SESSION STAYS NON-STREAMING IN THIS TICKET. `gateway-session.ts` calls `chat()`, and moving the tool loop onto `chatStream` is a change to the one component every ticket runs through — it needs its own ticket, its own fixtures and its own supervised run. This ticket makes the idle timeout exist and be correct on the streaming path so that change has something safe to land on. Filed as the follow-up rather than smuggled in.

RED FIXTURE: a stream that keeps producing past the old duration bound is NOT aborted; a stream that goes silent longer than the idle bound IS, and says which. Fake SSE source, never a live call (law 9a).
notes: Filed 2026-08-19. `chatStream` is fully built — SSE parsing, usage metering, queue integration — and has no production caller outside anthropic's internal use. Thirteenth instance of the built-but-unwired class, and the first where wiring it fixes a defect a user actually hit.

Closed 2026-08-19. THE FOUNDER WAS RIGHT ON THE MECHANISM, not just the principle: `fetchRaw` used `AbortSignal.timeout(timeoutMs)`, which bounds the WHOLE request, so a model streaming healthily for six minutes was killed at exactly the same moment as one that had hung. The streaming path now bounds time since the last chunk (`streamIdleMs`, 60s), reset per chunk by `readSseDataLines`. Duration still bounds the non-streaming path, correctly — there a single response is the only signal that exists. FEASIBILITY WAS MEASURED FIRST: LM Studio streams `tool_calls` deltas AND emits the `include_usage` chunk, so a streamed session can still drive the tool loop and still meter spend; without the usage chunk this would have meant trading the ledger for responsiveness, which is not a trade this product can make. FOUND AND FIXED MY OWN W13-10 BUG ON THE WAY: `requestExtras` reached `chat()` and not `chatStream()`, so a provider configured to stop a model thinking would have started thinking again the moment the session streamed — the exact five-hop 'settable and inert' failure I had cited W12-14's comment about while writing it. It has its own fixture now. THE SESSION STILL DOES NOT STREAM, deliberately: moving the tool loop onto chatStream changes the one component every ticket runs through, and it needs its own fixtures and its own supervised run rather than riding along here.

tickets.title: the session is a black box while it runs — it does not stream, so there is nothing to monitor
acceptance: RAISED BY THE FOUNDER 2026-08-19 alongside W13-15: "shouldn't we be monitoring?" W13-15 made a producing stream un-interruptible; this is the other half — `gateway-session.ts` calls `chat()`, so a session produces NOTHING observable until the whole model call returns. On a local model that is minutes of silence with no way to tell work from a hang, which is exactly what made the first supervised runs so hard to read.

MOVE THE TOOL LOOP ONTO `chatStream`, which is fully built (SSE parsing, tool-call deltas, usage metering, queue integration) and has had no session caller since W2-09. Measured feasible during W13-15: LM Studio streams tool_calls deltas AND the include_usage chunk, so the loop still drives and the ledger still meters.

THE LEDGER IS NOT NEGOTIABLE. A streamed call must record the same spend a non-streamed one does; a session that runs faster and meters nothing is worse than the black box. If a provider cannot supply usage on a stream, that provider must fall back to `chat()` rather than lose the ledger — anthropic already models this with its `streamEnabled` switch.

EMIT PROGRESS AS EVENTS, not as console output. The event log is how this product explains itself and the Chat pane already renders agent activity, so a token or tool-call delta should arrive the same way everything else does. Decide the granularity deliberately: per-token events would flood an append-only hash-chained log, which is the wrong place for a keystroke stream.

THIS IS THE COMPONENT EVERY TICKET RUNS THROUGH. It needs its own supervised run before it is trusted, not just fixtures — the first supervised run passed every fixture and still failed on the one thing no fixture covered (W13-09). Do not close this on green tests alone.

RED FIXTURE: a streamed session drives the same tool loop, produces the same manifest, and records the same ledger spend as the non-streamed one against identical scripted input; and progress is observable before the call completes.
notes: Filed 2026-08-19. Pairs with W13-15: that made silence the only thing that ends a stream, this gives the session something to be silent OR noisy about. Sized 8 and explicitly gated on a supervised run rather than fixtures, because gateway-session.ts is the single component every ticket in the product passes through.

Closed 2026-08-19 after three supervised runs against a real local model (qwen/qwen3-coder-next via LM Studio). The mandatory run earned its place: every fixture passed while the FIRST run still spent 15 of 18.7 seconds with no observable signal, because the opening turn emitted only tool_calls and ChatStreamDelta carries only content. Fixed in scope by emitting session.turn_started before the first byte (longest dark gap 15s -> 1.5s, measured); the rest needs the gateway stream contract and is filed as W13-20.

tickets.title: a tool-calling turn streams nothing — ChatStreamEvent carries only content
acceptance: MEASURED, not theorised. W13-16 moved the session onto chatStream and its supervised run still spent 15 of 18.7 seconds with no observable signal: the model first turn emitted tool_calls and no text, and ChatStreamDelta carries only { content }, so a tool-calling turn streams nothing. That is the COMMON turn, and on a 27B reasoning model it is minutes rather than seconds.

ADD A TOOL-CALL DELTA to ChatStreamEvent and emit it from the adapters that already parse those deltas off the wire. W13-15 measured that LM Studio does send them; oai-compat already reads them to assemble the final response, so this surfaces something the adapter has in hand and currently discards.
THE LEDGER STAYS WHERE IT IS. The final event remains the only metering point; a tool-call delta is progress, never spend.
GRANULARITY, SAME RULE AS W13-16: the durable log gets at most one event per turn per kind. The firehose goes to the onDelta-style callback and stays in memory.
RED FIXTURE: a turn that emits ONLY tool calls produces an observable signal before the turn completes, measured against the W13-16 run where it produced none.
notes: Filed by W13-16 from its own supervised run, which is why that run was mandatory: every fixture passed and the feature still did not solve the stated problem for the dominant case. session-stream.ts names this ticket in a comment.

Closed 2026-08-19. Measured live on both models: coder-next went from 26/64 producing turns (41%) to 6/6 (100%), with 5 of them naming the tool — read, edit, commit, verify, verify. qwen3.6-35b-a3b was already 100% because it narrates on every turn; its producing events carry no tool name because text arrives before the tool call, which is correct rather than a gap.

tickets.title: the challenger never fires in an agent session — the anchor is still the stub W5 was meant to replace
acceptance: FOUND 2026-08-19 by a live three-ticket run, not by a test. The build-run loop works end to end against a real local model — claim, tool loop, close gate, receipt, in_review, dependency release on accept, park on an unsatisfiable gate — and the CHALLENGER never fires anywhere in it. createStubChallengerAnchor has no caller in source at all; it appears only in the bundled dist because the barrel exports it. Its own doc says it never invokes a second model and returns no facts.

THE COMMENT IS STALE AND THAT IS THE ROOT CAUSE. anchors.ts says real wiring lands in W5 for the challenger and W7 for memory. W5-05 and W5-06 are both done — but W5-06's write_scope was packages/pipeline/src/challenger/**, the RESEARCH challenger (claim citability, report verdicts, revision handoffs), which IS wired and works. The SESSION anchor was never inside any ticket's scope, so it was nobody's job, and the comment kept promising that someone else would do it.

createStubMemoryAnchor is in the same position for W7. Check both and fix or re-date both comments. A stub naming a wave that has already shipped is worse than a TODO, because it reads as scheduled work rather than as a gap.

DECIDE WHETHER THE SESSION CHALLENGER SHOULD FIRE AT ALL BEFORE BUILDING IT. BLUEPRINT section 3.5 says borderline confidence only (0.5-0.85) for cost reasons, and the session already has a close gate that re-runs verify out of process (SC-02) — a stronger check than a second opinion on the same output. If the close gate supersedes it, DELETE the stub and the comment rather than wiring a mechanism the product outgrew.
RED FIXTURE: either a session at borderline confidence produces a challenger verdict on the event log, or the stub and its interface are gone and no comment promises them.
notes: Filed from a live supervised run on 2026-08-19. Same build-then-wire seam this repo keeps hitting: the decomposition gave the challenger a package to live in and never gave anyone the call site.

Closed 2026-08-19 by DELETING the challenger stub, not wiring it — and the decision was taken from BLUEPRINT section 3.5 step 4 rather than from my first instinct. That step asks for an independent verifier model "only where no oracle exists"; a build-run session always has one, the ticket verify re-run out of process by the close gate, and where there genuinely is none — research claim and report citability — the challenger IS already wired in packages/pipeline/src/challenger. It was in the right place all along. The MEMORY stub was kept after checking: anti-jarvis-gap.test.ts uses it as the inert control condition proving the real anchor recalls something, so deleting it would delete the proof. Wiring the real memory anchor is W13-23. Ratchet lowered 62 -> 61.

tickets.title: the stream idle-abort was never attached to the fetch — a 300s wall clock still governs, and a slower model hits it
acceptance: FOUND 2026-08-19 by running the same three-ticket loop on a SECOND model. qwen/qwen3-coder-next passes everything; qwen3.6-35b-a3b died after 5m10s with a raw DOMException TimeoutError, leaving T-2 stuck at in_progress. The product claims to be model-agnostic and was agnostic only up to a speed threshold nobody had crossed.

DEFECT 1 — the idle signal is discarded. streamEvents builds createIdleAbort and passes idle.signal in the RequestInit, then fetchRaw spreads that init and writes `signal: AbortSignal.timeout(timeoutMs)` AFTER the spread, overwriting it. The idle abort is constructed and bumped on every SSE line and never reaches fetch. W13-15 replaced a duration cap with an idle cap and the duration cap never actually left: streams are still governed by DEFAULT_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS = 300_000.

DEFECT 2 — a mid-stream abort is not a provider error. fetchRaw translates TimeoutError into ProviderTimeoutError, but only around the initial fetch; once headers arrive fetchRaw has returned, and an abort during the body read escapes as a raw DOMException. isProviderError does not recognise it, so runSessionAbsorbingProviderFailure never absorbs it into a failed attempt: the run dies and the ticket is left claimed at in_progress rather than released or parked.
RED FIXTURE 1: a stream that keeps producing PAST requestTimeoutMs is not aborted. This is W13-15's stated intent and the assertion that would have caught this on the day it landed.
RED FIXTURE 2: a stream aborted mid-body surfaces as a ProviderTimeoutError, so a session absorbs it as a failed attempt and the ticket is released rather than stranded.
VERIFY ON BOTH MODELS, not one: the three-ticket loop must reach the same end state on qwen/qwen3-coder-next and qwen3.6-35b-a3b.
notes: Filed and fixed 2026-08-19 in response to Brad asking whether the loop works on both local models. It did not. The single-model testing that preceded it could not have found this: coder-next never runs a turn long enough to reach 300s.

write_scope widened: oai-compat.ts sat at 398 of the 400-line cap, so the fix could not carry its own explanation. The abort translation went to streaming.ts beside createIdleAbort it partners, and the two local-daemon presets were split into oai-compat-presets.ts. Shaving comments to fit is how a file stops saying why.

tickets.title: the real memory anchor exists and no session has ever used it
acceptance: FOUND 2026-08-19 while removing the challenger stub (W13-21). packages/memory/src/store/anchor.ts holds a REAL createMemoryAnchor, backed by assembleContext over the fact store, with its own tests. Nothing in production constructs it. gateway-session.ts composes only createToolAnchor, so every session runs with no prior findings and no calibration seed.

THIS IS THE CAUTIONARY TALE THE MODULE NAMES. anchor.ts's own header cites source-system-foreman-jarvis.md section 5 — an unwired memory engine recalls nothing and is worth nothing — and the engine is, in fact, unwired. anti-jarvis-gap.test.ts already proves the real anchor recalls something where loop's inert stub recalls nothing; that proof has simply never been applied to a running session.

WHAT IT NEEDS is a store handle the session does not currently have: createMemoryAnchor takes a SqliteHandle and an optional EmbeddingProvider. Decide where the session gets one, and what happens when there is no embedding provider configured (a local-only user may have none) — FR-G5 says degrade honestly, so a session with no memory must still run, and must not pretend it recalled anything.

BLUEPRINT section 3.5 makes this load-bearing rather than a nice-to-have: calibration applies ONLY when an external anchor is present, and today the tool anchor is the only one. Memory is the anchor that carries prior confirmed findings and the per-(model, phase) calibration seed.
RED FIXTURE: a session whose project has a confirmed prior finding relevant to its ticket receives it as an anchor fact, proven against the current behaviour where it receives nothing.
notes: Filed by W13-21. The loop-side stub is deliberately KEPT as anti-jarvis-gap.test.ts's control condition — this ticket is about constructing the real one in a session, not about replacing the stub.

write_scope widened at claim: run-build.ts is the composition root (harbormaster may not import memory, ARCHITECTURE section 4 — same constraint W12-04 solved by composing in apps/server), and session-anchors.ts is a new chapter module because gateway-session.ts was at 399 of the 400-line cap with the anchor block inline.

Closed 2026-08-19. Proven live, not by fixture alone: a planted VERIFIED fact reached the model 16 times in one run (use_count 0 -> 16) while a planted UNVERIFIED one stayed at 0. Also checked that wiring memory does not make runs worse — 4 controlled runs, 2 with memory and 2 without, all landed in 1 attempt. Buried ratchet 73 -> 72.

tickets.title: spend is metered in memory and thrown away — W11 exit criterion 3 cannot be shown for any provider
acceptance: FOUND 2026-08-19 verifying the W11 exit criteria. Criterion 3 reads: every call is metered — the run's spend ledger is non-zero and attributable per role.
