It cannot be demonstrated on ANY provider, and the reason is not that local models are free: CostLedger keeps a private in-memory array, nothing writes costUsd to the event log or any table, and the ledger dies with the process. There is no durable record to be non-zero or attributable.

THE FLEET ALREADY ADMITS THIS IN A COMMENT. projects/stats.ts returns spendTodayUsd as a hardcoded 0 and says so in prose, and cards.ts serves it as spend_today. A user reading the Fleet sees a spend column that is a constant.

ENFORCEMENT IS NOT BROKEN, and the ticket must not pretend otherwise: the budget breakers (W2-07) and the per-ticket cost cap read the live in-memory ledger DURING a run and work. What is missing is the record AFTER it. Fix the record, do not rewrite the enforcement.

GRANULARITY IS A DECISION, same rule as W13-16 and W13-20: the event log is append-only and hash-chained. One event per metered model call is the natural grain (a 24-turn run writes 24, comparable to session.turn_started) — but justify it rather than assume it, and carry role, model, ticket, run, prompt/completion tokens and costUsd so FR-S1's why is this role on this model stays answerable from the log alone.
SECRETS: a spend event carries a model id and numbers, never a prompt, a completion or a credential (law 8, FR-S2).
RED FIXTURE: after a run ends, its per-call spend is readable from the durable log and attributable per role — and the Fleet's spend column reflects it instead of a constant.
notes: Filed 2026-08-19 while verifying W11's exit criteria rather than by a failing test. Criterion 3 was the one still unproven at the W11 gate; this is why, and it is a bigger gap than the criterion suggests — token counts ARE non-zero on local models, so metering works; only the durability is missing.

write_scope adjusted at claim: CostLedger itself needs no change — enforcement already works off the live in-memory array and the ticket says not to rewrite it. The single choke point for a metered session call is takeMeteredTurn, which already holds both the ledger and the event log. gateway-session.ts is added only to thread  through, which LedgerEntry does not carry and FR-S1 needs.

write_scope adjusted at claim: CostLedger itself needs no change, because enforcement already works off the live in-memory array and the ticket says not to rewrite it. The single choke point for a metered session call is takeMeteredTurn, which already holds both the ledger and the event log. gateway-session.ts is added only to thread the role through, which LedgerEntry does not carry and FR-S1 needs.

Closed 2026-08-19. Proven live: 20 spend.recorded events survived a real run on qwen/qwen3-coder-next, attributable per role (43,921 prompt / 953 completion tokens, usd=0 because a local model is free). STATUS.md also refreshed for the whole day, and records the one gap this could not close: W11 exit criterion 3 says spend must be non-zero, which is unprovable on a local-only install by construction and sits against law 9b. Flagged for the founder rather than amended.

tickets.title: SC-07 is documented as landed and is not in force — the execution sandbox has no caller
acceptance: FOUND 2026-08-19 auditing the unwired-export list. packages/harbormaster/src/sandbox/ implements process and container isolation, complete and tested, and has ZERO production callers. Both verify paths — the in-session verify tool (git-tools.ts verifyTool) and the out-of-session close gate (SC-02) — go through reRunVerify, which is node:child_process exec with cwd and timeout ONLY: the parent environment is inherited whole and the network is open. runValidatorPack spawns the same way; RunValidatorOptions has no sandbox field at all.

SC-07 CLAIMS OTHERWISE AND NAMES THIS AS SHIPPED: verify commands, test suites and tool anchors run under a restricted child process, cleaned env (no vault handles, no tokens), network disabled by default, validator-pack executables under the same sandbox — Lands: W6-06. W6-06 is done. Its write_scope was packages/harbormaster/src/sandbox/** — the module and nothing else — so no ticket ever owned a call site. The same build-then-wire seam as the packer (W12-04), the code index (W12-09), the anchors (W12-05) and the memory anchor (W13-23), but this time on a security control.

TWO THREATS LOSE THEIR STATED MITIGATION: T-4 and T-21 (poisoned content pack executes with gate authority, rated M x H = H) both cite SC-07. A validator pack or a ticket verify command currently runs with the operator's full environment and unrestricted network.

THE DECISION THIS TICKET MUST TAKE AND RECORD: what happens when the host cannot isolate (SandboxUnavailableError). FR-G5 says degrade honestly, but a security control that degrades silently is worth nothing. Recommendation to weigh: refuse by default and require an explicit, ledgered acknowledgement to run unsandboxed — the D-019 consent shape — rather than a silent fallback.

DO NOT WEAKEN SC-02 WHILE WIRING THIS. The close gate re-runs the ticket's own verify out of session precisely so a manifest cannot substitute a no-op; the sandbox must wrap that execution, not replace or relax it.

RED FIXTURE: a verify command attempting an outbound connection and a read of a secret-bearing env var fails on both counts — which is W6-06's own acceptance criterion 2, never exercised against the real path.
notes: Filed 2026-08-19 from an unwired-export audit, not a failing test. Deliberately NOT fixed in place: wiring a sandbox into every verify changes execution semantics for every run and needs the unavailable-host decision made first. The docs are corrected in the same commit that files this, because a security document asserting a mitigation that is absent is worse than the gap.

Closed 2026-08-19 with the founder-chosen answer: fail closed, with an explicit ledgered waiver. Scoped honestly to the VERIFY path — runValidatorPack still has no sandbox parameter, so pack executables remain outside it and the docs say so rather than claiming the whole control. The refusal was placed AFTER the existing signing-key and vault checks so a new precondition never preempts an older refusal message; a test caught that ordering.

tickets.title: the autonomy dial is written and never read — a user sets a safety control that does nothing
acceptance: FOUND 2026-08-19, same audit as W13-25. The FirstRunWizard and Settings let a user choose Autonomy; the server persists it (PUT /projects/{id}/autonomy, project-scope settings key `autonomy`). NO RUN PATH EVER READS IT. `AutonomyMode` appears nowhere in loop-land, berths, loop-claim or apps/server/src/cli. `resolvePauseAction` — whose own doc calls it THE SINGLE ENFORCEMENT POINT for SC-10 — has zero production callers, as do `assertLedgerValidForNextClaim` and `assertExecutionAllowed`.

C-5 IS CURRENTLY VACUOUS, not merely unenforced. CONSTRAINTS C-5 says the dial cannot override a NEVER-AUTO pause site — but `isNeverAutoPauseSite` is referenced only inside the autonomy module, so nothing consults the dial OR the exemption. The constraint holds today only because the feature does nothing at all.

THIS IS WORSE THAN AN UNWIRED MECHANISM AND SHOULD BE RATED AS SUCH: a user makes an explicit choice about how much the product may do unattended, the product stores it, and the choice has no effect. `--breakpoint` (breakpoints.ts, wave boundaries) is a DIFFERENT control and is wired; it is not a substitute, and the two must not be conflated while fixing this.

DECIDE WHAT `auto` MAY ACTUALLY DO before wiring, and record it. `resolvePauseAction` returns take_default at a non-NEVER-AUTO site; confirm the documented default at each pause site is one a user would accept unattended, because wiring this turns those defaults on for the first time.

RED FIXTURE: a project set to `interactive` asks at a pause site where `auto` would take the default, proven against today's behaviour where the mode changes nothing; and a NEVER-AUTO site asks in BOTH modes (C-5).
notes: Filed 2026-08-19 alongside W13-25 from an unwired-export audit. Not fixed in place: wiring the dial turns documented auto-defaults on for the first time, which changes what an unattended run is permitted to do — a founder-facing decision, not an implementer's.

Scoped down at claim to the HONEST-SURFACE half, on the founder recommendation: do not wire auto yet. Today a pause site opens a clarification that blocks until someone resolves or dismisses it, so nothing auto-takes a default and the dial being inert is conservative rather than dangerous. Wiring auto would turn documented defaults on for the first time on projects whose owners set it believing it already applied. What ships now is the product no longer claiming otherwise. The wiring stays open as W13-32 with the defaults review as its first task.

e2e settings.spec.ts updated: it clicked the Auto radio and asserted it survived a reload. Auto is now disabled unless already selected, so the persistence assertion went with it — deliberately, since there is nothing left for a user to persist from that surface and the PUT is covered server-side. The spec catching this is the e2e gate doing its job.

tickets.title: an infrastructure failure consumes a ladder attempt, so two of them park a ticket a human then has to restart
acceptance: REPORTED FROM FIELD USE of a comparable multi-agent setup: a delegated session ends without a conforming terminal result — it degenerates into repeated malformed tool calls and never emits a final answer, or an endpoint stalls, or an acceptance gate times out on a large tree. The orchestrator records a blocked state and STOPS, and a human has to notice and tell it to continue. The automation should absorb this class without a person in the loop.

THE MECHANISM ALREADY EXISTS AND HAS NO CALLER. packages/loop/src/findings-infra.ts defines InfraFailureKind and createInfraFailureTracker, and its own header states the rule: a truncated review, an unparseable verdict, a limit pause, a watchdog kill or an output-buffer overflow RETRIES FOR FREE. Nothing constructs it. Eighth instance of the build-then-wire seam.

TODAY EVERY FAILURE COSTS AN ATTEMPT EQUALLY. loop-land.ts increments `attempt` per pass; runSessionAbsorbingProviderFailure (W13-13) correctly converts an endpoint failure into a failed attempt rather than a crash, but that attempt still burns the ladder. With the default cap of 2, two infrastructure hiccups park a ticket whose work was never judged — the park then needs a human, which is the reported symptom.

FREE RETRY MUST BE BOUNDED, and the bound is the point: a permanently unreachable endpoint must still park honestly rather than loop forever. Pick a separate free-retry ceiling, record every free retry on the event log so the run explains itself, and fall back to consuming an attempt once the ceiling is hit.

CLASSIFY DELIBERATELY, NOT BY CATCH-ALL. An endpoint failure, a watchdog kill and a verify/validator TIMEOUT are infrastructure — none is evidence the work is wrong. A session that returns without a Completion Manifest is NOT infrastructure: that is the model failing the contract, and it must keep costing an attempt. A catch-all here would turn a real defect into an infinite free retry, which is the silence this product exists to refuse.

RED FIXTURE: a ticket whose first two sessions fail for an infrastructure reason and whose third succeeds LANDS, where today it parks after two; and a ticket that returns no manifest three times still parks.
notes: Filed 2026-08-19 from a field report about a different multi-agent system exhibiting this class. Deliberately described in terms of Dokima's own mechanisms only — no third-party project detail is carried into this board.

Closed 2026-08-19. Scope covers only endpoint failures, which are the cleanly classifiable case today: a verify TIMEOUT is indistinguishable from a genuine non-zero exit in reRunVerify, so treating it as infrastructure needs that function to report a timeout first — deliberately left to a follow-up rather than guessed at. ceilingFor moved into the new chapter module because loop-land.ts was at 397 of the 400 cap.

tickets.title: a gate can pass on evidence from a scratch harness while the integrated product stays broken
acceptance: REPORTED FROM FIELD USE of a comparable multi-agent setup. A UI feature was rebuilt in an isolated harness, where it worked; inside the existing application it did not. Smaller models repeatedly reported the work finished while the user could still see it failing, and each round produced evidence from the isolated path rather than the integrated one. Nobody could say what differed between the two builds, so the loop had nothing to converge on and a larger model was eventually used instead.

THIS IS A GATE-SHAPE PROBLEM, NOT A MODEL-QUALITY PROBLEM, and that is the part worth fixing. Dokima re-runs a ticket's own verify command out of session (SC-02) so a manifest cannot substitute a no-op — but if the verify command exercises a harness rather than the product, the gate is satisfied while the user-visible behaviour is untouched. The oracle is only as good as what it drives.

FIRST DELIVERABLE IS A DIAGNOSIS STEP, not more retries. When a criterion passes in isolation and fails in the product, the loop should produce a structured DIFFERENCE between the two environments — dependency versions actually installed, initialisation order, configuration and feature flags, mount/container context, and styling or layering that only exists in the application shell — rather than letting a session guess. A repeated report of done against unchanged symptoms is the signal to run this, and it should be automatic.

SECOND: DECIDE WHETHER A TICKET CAN DECLARE THAT ITS VERIFY MUST DRIVE THE INTEGRATED PATH, and record the decision. A per-ticket flag is cheap and honest; inferring it is not. Whatever is chosen, a ticket whose acceptance is user-visible must not be closable on harness-only evidence.

DO NOT SOLVE THIS BY DISTRUSTING SMALL MODELS. Escalating to a larger model hides the defect at cost and leaves the gate wrong for every model, including the large one. The fitness bench (W2-08) already exists for model choice; this ticket is about what the gate demands.
RED FIXTURE: a ticket whose verify passes against an isolated harness while the integrated path is broken does NOT close, and the run emits a readable difference between the two environments.
notes: Filed 2026-08-19 from a field report about a different multi-agent system. Written entirely in terms of Dokima's own gate mechanisms; no third-party project, ticket, path or library detail is carried onto this board. write_scope intentionally EMPTY: the first deliverable is the diagnosis design, and guessing files before that decision is how a provisional scope becomes a wrong one.

Closed 2026-08-19 as the DESIGN ticket it was scoped as: docs/design/INTEGRATION_EVIDENCE.md, no gate change. It found the same defect in Dokima itself — TICKET_KEYS has no verify field, so 0 of 274 tickets carry one and every ticket falls through to a default that omits e2e, making the agent gate strictly weaker than law 3. Section 6 lists what must be decided before a gate can change.

tickets.title: attempt 2 gets the same handoff as attempt 1 — the gaps are never fed back, so a retry is a re-roll
acceptance: BLUEPRINT section 3.5 step 5 requires it in as many words: REVISE — re-ground, then fix, WITH THE SPECIFIC GAPS FED BACK; no-progress kill. The land loop does neither. attemptOnce calls buildHandoff(ticket) with the ticket alone, and HandoffBuilder has no parameter through which a prior failure could arrive, so every attempt renders an identical prompt. A retry is a re-roll of the same dice, not a correction.

THE DATA ALREADY EXISTS AND IS DISCARDED. CloseGateFailure carries reasons[]; SessionResult carries scopeViolations and output; a missing manifest is known. All of it is available at the moment the next handoff is built, and none of it is passed. The failure summary IS eventually written — by parkComment, after the ladder is exhausted, where only a human will read it.

WIDEN THE BUILDER, do not special-case the default one. A custom builder (the packed context builder, W12-04) must be able to see the same feedback, or the product's own context layer stays blind to why the last pass failed.

ADD THE NO-PROGRESS KILL the same step names. Two consecutive attempts that produce the identical gap set are not converging; burning the rest of the ladder on them costs tokens and delays the park. Stop early and park with that stated as the reason.

REDACTION IS NOT OPTIONAL HERE: gate reasons quote verify stdout/stderr, which can carry a secret. Feedback must go through the same redactDeep path the rendered handoff already applies (SC-06/FR-S2), and there must be a fixture planting a secret in a gate reason and asserting it does not reach the prompt.

RED FIXTURE: a ticket whose first attempt fails the close gate for a NAMED reason produces a second-attempt prompt containing that reason, proven against today's byte-identical prompts; and two identical failures stop the ladder early rather than running it out.
notes: Filed 2026-08-19 from a field report about a comparable multi-agent setup where work is lost between the orchestrator and its specialists and a human has to re-state what went wrong. Dokima has the same shape for a different reason: the feedback is computed, then dropped on the floor between attempts.

Closed 2026-08-19. The no-progress kill is LADDER MODE ONLY and only while an attempt remains: locked mode is defined as looping in place to its FR-L7 convergence ceiling and token-gated maps attempts onto rungs, so an early kill defeats those modes rather than serving them — three existing tests caught that and were right. Park reporting split into loop-land-report.ts because loop-land.ts was at the 400-line cap.

tickets.title: the close gate tells the maker that verify failed and never what it said
acceptance: W13-28's first recommendation, and the cheapest half of it. runCloseGate re-runs verify, captures stdout and stderr in a VerifyRunResult, and then reports only: verify re-run failed, command exited N. The output is discarded at the point of failure. W13-29 now feeds gate reasons to the next attempt, so the maker is told THAT it failed and never HOW — which is the position a person is in when an agent keeps reporting done against a symptom that has not changed.
SAME SHAPE AS EVERY OTHER FINDING THIS WAVE: the fact is computed and thrown away. It is not a new capability, it is a value already in scope at the line that builds the reason.

BOUND IT. Verify output can be a whole test run; a full dump would crowd the prompt it is meant to inform and can exceed a context window. Take a tail, state that it was truncated, and prefer stderr when both are present — a failing command puts its diagnosis there.

REDACTION IS ALREADY ON THE PATH and must stay that way: gaps ride the handoff context through renderHandoff's redactDeep (SC-06), so this must not introduce a second, parallel redaction step to keep correct.
RED FIXTURE: a ticket whose verify fails with a distinctive message produces a second-attempt prompt containing that message, proven against today's prompt which contains only the exit code.
notes: Filed and built 2026-08-19 as the concrete half of W13-28's diagnosis recommendation. The broader environment-difference packet needs the decisions in that document's section 6; this does not.
Closed 2026-08-19. The tail helper lives in loop-gates-verify.ts, which already owns running verify and the VerifyRunResult type — and loop-gates.ts was over the 400-line cap with it inline.

tickets.title: a plan-derived ticket can never close — its verify is a predicate and the close gate executes it as a shell command
acceptance: FOUND 2026-08-19. acceptItem mints a ticket draft with `verify: item.verifyCriterion` verbatim (lifecycle.ts:112). A verifyCriterion is a MACHINE-CHECKABLE PREDICATE over a PlanEvaluationSnapshot — same grammar as an item's condition, e.g. `receipts.staleCount == 0`. SC-02's reRunVerify EXECUTES ticket.verify as a shell command. Confirmed empirically rather than argued: `bash -c 'receipts.staleCount == 0'` exits 127, command not found.

CONSEQUENCE: every plan-derived ticket fails its close gate on every attempt, for a reason that has nothing to do with the work, and parks after the ladder. Two subsystems agreed on a field NAME and disagreed on its MEANING — a predicate to one, a command to the other.

FR-PLAN2 IS ALREADY SATISFIED WITHOUT THIS. The intent — the plan and the board never diverge on what done means — is carried by acceptance[0].text, which acceptItem already sets to the same criterion on the line above. The predicate also already has a proper evaluator: the plan lifecycle re-evaluates it against a fresh snapshot. Nothing is lost by not also handing it to a shell.

FIX: leave the draft's verify unset so the ticket falls back to the project's own gate, and keep the criterion in acceptance where it is read rather than executed. Do NOT teach reRunVerify to detect and evaluate predicates — that would couple the land loop to the pipeline's expression grammar and give one field two runtimes.
RED FIXTURE: a ticket minted from an accepted plan item carries a verify that is either absent or executable, and the criterion still appears in its acceptance.
notes: Found while checking my own W13-28 claim, after I had already got one thing wrong in the same session by reading a truncated config. Confirmed by running the predicate as a shell command rather than by reasoning about it.
Filed with role code-reviewer and validate-plan refused it: a verifier role may not be the maker (C-4, P11). The guard working on my own ticket, which is the point of it being mechanical.

tickets.title: wire the autonomy dial — after deciding which defaults are acceptable unattended
acceptance: DECIDE FIRST, AND RECORD IT: which documented default at each non-NEVER-AUTO pause site is acceptable to take unattended. Wiring the dial turns every one of them on for the first time, on projects whose owners selected auto believing it already applied. This is the whole risk and it is not a coding question.

askClarification opens a blocking card unconditionally and takes no pause-site kind. It needs one, plus the project mode, before resolvePauseAction can be consulted — the mode lives in project settings, which harbormaster cannot read, so it must be injected the way every other cross-package dependency in this loop is.
C-5 IS THE HALF THAT MUST NOT BE LOST: isNeverAutoPauseSite must be consulted on the same path, or wiring auto silently removes a constraint that is currently vacuous but intact.
RED FIXTURE: a project set to auto takes the documented default at a non-NEVER-AUTO site and ledgers it; the same project still ASKS at a NEVER-AUTO site.
notes: Filed by W13-26, which shipped the honest surface only. Today nothing reads the dial and every gated pause blocks, so the current state is conservative — there is no urgency here, and real risk in wiring it without the defaults review.

tickets.title: the shipped bundle boots a server on EVERY command — dokima --help hangs and opens a writable state.db
acceptance: FOUND 2026-08-19 by running the product as a customer would, against the BUILT artifact rather than the source. `node apps/server/dist/main.js --help` prints usage and then never exits: it binds 127.0.0.1:DOKIMA_PORT and opens a WRITABLE connection to ./.dokima/state.db (plus -wal and -shm) in whatever directory it was run from. The same happens for a mistyped command, and for every other subcommand.

ROOT CAUSE IS THE BUNDLE, NOT THE CODE. api/main.ts ends with the standard run-if-main guard: isMainModule compares pathToFileURL(process.argv[1]).href to import.meta.url. In source those differ, so it stays dormant. esbuild bundles every module into ONE file, so import.meta.url becomes dist/main.js — which IS process.argv[1] — and the guard fires on every invocation, before and regardless of what the CLI dispatch decides.

THIS DEFEATS W10-44 IN THE ONLY PLACE THAT MATTERS. That ticket exists because --help used to boot the core; it fixed the source, and every test in this repo runs against source. The artifact a customer installs was never covered, so the fix was true and the shipped behaviour was not.

FIX BY REMOVING THE LANDMINE, not by adding a flag: a module that is IMPORTED must not also be an ENTRY POINT. Move the self-boot into its own dev entry that nothing imports, and point playwright.config.ts at it — it is the only consumer that runs api/main.ts directly.
RED FIXTURE: an assertion that the built bundle contains no run-if-main self-boot, so this cannot return the next time a module grows one. A source-level test cannot catch this class by construction.
notes: Found only by executing the built artifact. Every prior verification this session ran source, including my own — the bundle is a different program and nothing tested it.

Closed 2026-08-19. Verified against the BUILT artifact: dokima --help exit 0, --version exit 0, a typo exit 2, none of them binding a port or opening a state.db. The red fixture asserts the bundle itself, because a source-level test cannot catch this class by construction — the bug only exists after bundling.

tickets.title: a fresh install cannot build a board — it guesses a model that does not exist and reports the failure unreadably
acceptance: FOUND 2026-08-19 by using the product as a customer: fresh DOKIMA_HOME, boot, New project, Describe your product, Build the board. It fails with: The run failed: env: request failed with 400 Bad Request (HTTP 500). That is the primary flow of the product, on a clean install, and it does not work.

THE CHAIN: nothing in the visible path ever asks for a model, so resolveModelTarget falls through to envTarget, whose defaults are baseUrl 127.0.0.1:1234 and model 'local-model'. A real LM Studio answers that with a perfectly clear error — Invalid model identifier 'local-model'. Please specify a valid downloaded model — and Dokima discards it, showing an internal provider id and two different status codes instead.

THIS IS A LAW 9(b) VIOLATION, not merely a UX gap. Which model does the work is the user's choice, asked at setup, NEVER DEFAULTED SILENTLY. A placeholder model id pointed at a guessed endpoint is a silent default, and the code comment calling it 'a normal first-run state, not an error (C-1)' is the assumption to correct: C-1 promises local-only WORKS, not that an unconfigured install guesses.
REFUSE, NAMED AND ACTIONABLE, when nothing is configured and no env override is set: say that no model is configured and where to choose one. FR-G5 degrades honestly; an unusable 500 is neither.

DO NOT BREAK THE CI SEAM (law 9a): DOKIMA_MODEL_BASE_URL / DOKIMA_MODEL_ID set explicitly must still resolve exactly as today. The refusal is only for the case where nothing anywhere says which model to use.
RED FIXTURE: resolving with no providers, no matrix rows and no env override refuses by name rather than returning a placeholder target; and the same call WITH the env vars set still returns them.
notes: Found by running the product end to end in a browser on a clean install, not by a test. Every existing test either configures a model or asserts the env fallback, so the unconfigured path was covered as a feature rather than as the dead end it is.

Closed 2026-08-19. Verified in a browser on a fresh install: the failure went from "env: request failed with 400 Bad Request (HTTP 500)" to "no model is configured for this project yet. Open Settings to choose one...".

tickets.title: the setup wizard registers nothing unless you also create the sample project
acceptance: FOUND 2026-08-19 by walking a fresh install as a customer. Step 2 is titled Register one provider. It registers nothing: savePresetAndProvider posts the entry inside a `providers` key on PUT /settings/global, which that route has never handled — the file's own comment says so. The only real putProviders call lives in step 4, inside Create sample project.

SO A USER WHO SKIPS THE SAMPLE ENDS WITH NOTHING REGISTERED, which is what happened here: complete steps 1 to 3, decline the sample, and the provider list is still empty and the matrix still has no rows. After W13-34 the product then correctly says no model is configured — honest, and still a dead end reached straight after a setup flow that claimed to configure it.

THE CONSTRAINT IN THE WAY IS REAL, not an oversight: the global-scope registry write is ADDRESSED THROUGH A PROJECT, and when the wizard is opened with no project in view there is nothing to address it through. That is why it was deferred to the step that creates one.

FIX: when a project IS in view — which is every path that reaches the wizard from Settings — register at step 2 through that project. Keep the deferral only for the genuinely projectless case, and say so in the step's copy rather than leaving the title claiming something it does not do.
RED FIXTURE: completing steps 1 to 3 with a project in view and declining the sample leaves a registered provider behind, proven against today's empty registry.
notes: The wizard itself is good — step 1 is the clearest copy in the product and is exactly what law 9(b) asks for. The defect is that its output does not survive the path most users take.

Closed 2026-08-19. Verified in a browser: completing steps 1-3 and declining the sample now leaves {"id":"first-run","kind":"lm-studio",...} registered, where the registry was empty before. The board still cannot be built because the preset is never expanded into matrix rows — filed as W13-36, not folded in here.

tickets.title: no shipped model names: a preset says WHICH ROLE gets the better model, never which model
acceptance: FOUND 2026-08-19 completing the customer walkthrough. After W13-35 the wizard registers a provider, and the board still cannot be built: resolveModelTarget needs providers AND matrix rows, and the rows are empty. The wizard records defaultModelMatrixPreset (all-local) in global settings; scope-routes validates that name against PRESET_NAMES and stores it; NOTHING ever expands it into rows. presetAsGlobalScope exists, is exported from the gateway barrel, and has no caller — the ninth instance of this seam.

AND EXPANDING IT AS-IS WOULD NOT FIX THE WALKTHROUGH, which is why this is not a one-line wiring ticket. PRESET_ALL_LOCAL hardcodes qwen2.5-coder-7b-instruct and qwen2.5-coder-32b-instruct. A user whose LM Studio holds different models — the machine this was found on holds 26, none of them those — would get the same Invalid model identifier failure, one step later and harder to explain.

THE REAL FIX IS TO PICK FROM WHAT THE PROVIDER REPORTS. Every adapter already implements listModels(); the wizard registers a provider and then never asks which of its models to use. Decide whether the preset becomes a SHAPE (which role gets the stronger model, which the cheaper) resolved against the live model list, rather than a literal set of model ids that can only be right by luck.

UNTIL THEN THE REFUSAL IS CORRECT AND SHOULD STAY: W13-34 makes an unconfigured project say so and point at Settings. That is a dead end a user can act on, which is strictly better than a guess that fails at the endpoint.
RED FIXTURE: a fresh install that completes the wizard against a provider holding arbitrary models can build a board — the walkthrough this ticket came from, run end to end.
notes: Filed rather than fixed on purpose: wiring presetAsGlobalScope alone would move the failure from 'no rows' to 'model not found' and look like progress. write_scope left empty because the first deliverable is the shape-vs-literal decision.

Closed 2026-08-19 for the hardcode half on the founder instruction that a customer must use the models they have. Zero model-name literals remain in shipped source (fixtures excepted — law 9a requires those). The remaining half, asking the user WHICH of their models to use and writing matrix rows from it, is W13-37.

tickets.title: the setup flow must ask which of the user's models to use, and write the matrix from it
acceptance: W13-36 removed every shipped model name: a preset is now a SHAPE (which role gets the stronger model) and buildPresetMatrix takes the two ids from its caller. Nothing calls it yet, so a fresh install still has no matrix rows and still cannot build a board.

THE WIZARD REGISTERS A PROVIDER AND NEVER ASKS WHICH OF ITS MODELS TO USE. fetchProviderModels already lists exactly what that provider reports; putModelMatrix already writes rows. Both exist and the wizard calls neither.

ASK FOR TWO: a model for the work and a model for review. C-4 requires them to differ, and route() refuses a collision — so a provider holding only ONE usable model must be told that plainly at setup rather than at the first review.
NEVER RANK THE MODELS FOR THE USER by parsing names for parameter counts. That is a hardcode wearing a heuristic: the names on a real machine are arbitrary. Offer the list and let them choose.
RED FIXTURE: a fresh install that completes the wizard against a provider holding arbitrary model names can build a board — the walkthrough W13-34/35/36 came from, run end to end.
notes: Filed by W13-36 rather than folded in: removing the hardcodes and adding a picker are separate changes, and shipping the second without the first would have kept the guessed ids alive underneath it.

tickets.title: the importer cannot tell a Dokima-native expert from one upstream deleted
acceptance: FOUND 2026-08-19 CHASING A FALSE ALARM. The v3.5.4 dry run reported "1 REMOVED: pm-interviewer.md", which blocked W12-07 as a founder decision about diverging from the pack. It was not a removal: `pm-interviewer` HAS NEVER EXISTED IN attest — `git log --diff-filter=D --all` finds nothing and the name appears nowhere in that repo. Our copy carries a header saying so, written when it was created: "Provenance: Dokima-native (authored for ticket W5-02)... per BLUEPRINT's Dokima-is-canonical-for-itself decision".

THE DEFECT IS THE COMPARISON MODEL. `dry-run.mjs` computes `removed` as "local agents upstream does not have", which is exactly right for a file that came FROM upstream and exactly wrong for one that never did. `LOCAL_OVERRIDES` does not cover this — it is for locally PATCHED upstream files (validate-mermaid.sh: "upstream version renders differently"). There is no way to say "upstream never had this and never will".

THIS WOULD HAVE COST THE PRODUCT THE FILE. Every future import reports it as a removal; eventually someone accepts one and deletes a load-bearing expert. It nearly happened here — the standing W12-07 note recommended keeping it as an override and "recording the permanent divergence", which frames a deliberate native file as drift. The tool's output was believable and wrong.

A NATIVE REGISTRY BESIDE LOCAL_OVERRIDES, keyed the same way and carrying the same kind of reason string. TWO FILES QUALIFY, not one — `content/samples/link-shortener.md` is also Dokima-native — so find them by their own provenance headers rather than hand-listing what this ticket happened to notice.

THE REPORT MUST SAY WHICH IS WHICH. A native file should not appear under "removed" at all; if a genuine upstream deletion ever happens it must still be reported, because that IS a decision someone has to make.

RED FIXTURE: a native file is not reported as removed and is not deleted by an import; a genuinely-removed upstream file still IS reported. Fixtures against a temp source tree, never the real upstream checkout.
notes: Filed 2026-08-19. Unblocks W12-07, which was blocked on a founder decision that turns out not to exist — nothing was lost upstream, so there is nothing to decide and nothing to fix in attest.

Closed 2026-08-19. The v3.5.4 dry run now reports `experts removed 0` and `Dokima-native 1 pm-interviewer.md (upstream never had these — not a removal)`. DETECTED FROM THE FILE'S OWN HEADER rather than a registry entry, because a second hand-kept list would drift from the files the first time someone added a native one — and the marker has been sitting in pm-interviewer.md since W5-02 wrote it, unread by anything. There is a fixture asserting the REAL file still carries it, so an innocent header edit cannot silently restore the false alarm. WHAT MAKES THIS WORTH THE TICKET: the false alarm had already done damage. It blocked W12-07 as a founder decision about diverging from the pack, and my own note on that ticket recommended keeping the file as a LOCAL_OVERRIDE and 'recording the permanent divergence' — framing a deliberately native file as drift, on the strength of one line of tool output that was believable and wrong.

tickets.title: there are two interviews — the built adaptive engine, and the static one users actually get
acceptance: AC-1 IS A COMMITTED ACCEPTANCE CRITERION, NOT A DOC'S ASPIRATION: docs/USER_STORIES.md says "Interview adapts question depth to my answers; I can skip and return". Neither half is delivered. The engine that does exactly this is BUILT and TESTED in packages/pipeline/src/interview — depth ceiling (MAX_FOLLOWUP_DEPTH = 4), skip, resume, NA-1 human-only enforcement — and all four verbs (beginTopic, submitAnswer, skipTopic, resumeTopic) sit in the W12-38 buried-exports list with no production caller.

THE SHORTCUT SHADOWS THE REAL THING. `apps/web/src/onboarding/InterviewPanel.tsx` is a SECOND interview: eight static questions, its own state, no follow-ups, no per-topic skip, no resume. It exists because a browser bundle cannot call a model directly (ARCHITECTURE §4 / law 6), so adaptive depth needs a server endpoint that was never built. Users get the shortcut.

THE ENDPOINT CAN BE STATELESS, which is what makes this tractable: the client ALREADY sends a whole `InterviewSession` to `POST .../pipeline/run` (`request-body.ts`), so the same shape can carry a follow-up request. No new persistence, no session store, no second source of truth about where an interview has got to.

THE CEILING STAYS AND IS THE POINT. MAX_FOLLOWUP_DEPTH is what keeps this an interview rather than an unbounded chatbot, and its own comment ties it to FR-L7 convergence discipline. A model-driven question also costs money per turn, so it needs the same metering and refusals as any other model call — and a local-only user (C-1, D-024 option a) must still get a working interview, which means the static questions remain the floor when no model is reachable rather than being deleted outright.

DELETE THE SHORTCUT ONCE THE ENGINE DRIVES THE PANEL, or the two drift and the simpler one keeps winning because it is already wired — the exact story of `.empty-state` in W13-04, where a shared thing existed and seven surfaces reinvented it anyway.

NEEDS A SUPERVISED RUN, NOT GREEN TESTS. This is the front door: the first thing a new user touches. The last built-but-unused mechanism wired into the session path passed every fixture and failed on what no fixture covered (W13-09).
notes: Filed 2026-08-19 after the founder asked how to close the gap between pm-interviewer.md and the implementation. The doc is NOT overclaiming — it accurately describes the engine that was built. Fourteenth instance of the built-but-unwired class and the largest: an entire subsystem shadowed by a simpler reimplementation of itself.

Closed 2026-08-19, VERIFIED AGAINST THE LOCAL MODEL, not only fixtures: the live endpoint returned 'Who are the primary users of this tool—developers, businesses, researchers, or another group?' in one second. That is AC-1 delivered for the first time since it was written. THE FIRST LIVE TEST FAILED AND MY OWN CATCH-ALL HID WHY — it returned reason 'unavailable' in 0.017s for what was actually a ROUTING failure: a real project's matrix carries coding-agent rows only (that is what the wizard writes), so asking for role 'pm-interviewer' was unresolvable. Fixed twice over: fall back to the configured role, and report 'no-model-configured' distinctly from 'unavailable' with the underlying message, because a single catch-all hiding four different causes is the silence this product exists to refuse. I HAD INTRODUCED A SECOND SILENT FAILURE IN THE SAME TICKET: buildInterviewSession read answers[deliverableId] only, so every follow-up answer was dropped — a person could answer three adaptive questions and none would reach the draft, and the feature would have looked like it worked. Follow-ups are now real questionsAsked at increasing depth, which is what the engine's ceiling counts. THE ON-BLUR DESIGN WAS WRONG AND THE E2E SUITE PROVED IT: fetching a follow-up whenever the cursor left a field meant a model call per tab, surprise layout shifts, and three failing specs plus a run that went from 30s to 1.2m. Made explicit ('Ask me more about this'); e2e returned to 69 passing at 29.7s. Two e2e specs also had to stop addressing textareas by positional index, which was a latent break the moment any form grew.

Story ref corrected 2026-08-19: filed as US-001, which does not exist. The adaptive-depth interview is US-101. validate-traceability caught it and had been failing on main since W13-18 merged, because it is not in the law 3 gate.

tickets.title: law 9(a) is a rule nothing checks — make it mechanical
acceptance: W13-18 route tests reached a real LM Studio on 127.0.0.1:1234 for a day via envTarget fallback, and passed or failed depending on which model was loaded. Law 9(a) forbids exactly this and nothing checked it.

Refuse any non-loopback host and loopback on the two local model daemon ports (1234, 11434). Allow loopback on ports a test itself started — refusing those enforces "no sockets", a different and wrong rule.
RED FIXTURE: disabling W13-18's stub is caught by the guard rather than by an unrelated assertion.
notes: Filed after the fact: built in response to the stop hook that surfaced the live calls, then back-filled here so the board matches reality. Merged as b949b10.

tickets.title: a paused creation run must be findable again — the UI knows no route back to it
acceptance: MEASURED, not theorised. Clean DOKIMA_HOME, live LM Studio, guided sample: the run paused on two founder decisions, both were answered on the standalone Decisions board, and the product then had no way to continue. Board: empty. Describe: a blank interview form. The paused run was on disk the whole time (.dokima/runs/<id>.json, status awaiting-decisions) and POSTing its resume route by hand built the whole board — so resume WORKS and honours decisions answered anywhere. The only missing piece is that nothing can discover the run id.

InterviewPanel.tsx says so in its own comment: "there is no route back to a paused run". awaiting.run_id lives in component state, so navigating away discards it. GuidedSample tells a first-run user to "answer it in Decisions to continue" — which is exactly the navigation that strands them. Two surfaces disagreeing, and the one a new user reads is the wrong one.

ADD THE DISCOVERY PRIMITIVE: GET /api/v1/projects/:id/pipeline/runs listing the project run records newest-first (wireRunRecord shape, startedAt ordering). loadPausedRun already needs a runId; nothing lists. Pick deterministically when several are awaiting — silently picking the wrong one is worse than the current honest dead end.
NO AUTO-RESUME. Do not watch for "last slate decided" and resume in the background: that is a durable state change with no human in the loop (Law 4). Continue stays an explicit button.
Fix the GuidedSample sentence too. Fixing the plumbing and leaving the instruction that walks people off it fixes nothing a user would notice.

RED FIXTURE: the walkthrough this came from, end to end — run the pipeline, pause, answer the slates on the standalone Decisions board, navigate away, come back, Continue, board built. Not a unit test on the new route.
tickets.notes: Resume is proven to work: POSTing /pipeline/<runId>/resume against the live paused run built the board, with decisions that had been answered on the standalone board. This ticket is discovery + navigation only — do not touch the resume contract.

tickets.title: Describe does not recognise a run that is still running — only one that has paused
tickets.notes: Found while verifying W13-38, not by W13-38 failing. Same class as the copy W13-38 fixed: a screen that does not know what state its project is in.
acceptance: W13-38 recovers a run whose status is awaiting-decisions. A run that is still RUNNING is discoverable by the same route and is ignored: fetchAwaitingRun filters for awaiting-decisions and returns null.

CONSEQUENCE: click Build the board, navigate to Board and back to Describe while the run is in flight (~4 minutes on a local model, so the window is wide), and the blank interview form is what you get — with a live run building. The only control offered is Build the board, and pressing it earns a 409 refusal for doing the one thing the screen suggested. Nothing corrupts; the server refuses a second concurrent run correctly. The screen is what is wrong.

Make it fetchActiveRun (running OR awaiting-decisions). The running case restores the Building the board... state and resumes the status poll against the recovered run id, rather than showing the form.
The mid-answer guard stays: recovery must not pull the screen out from under a founder who has started typing (InterviewPanel only recovers from an untouched form).
RED FIXTURE: start a run, navigate away and back before it finishes, and the describe screen must show the run in progress — not an empty form.

tickets.title: the land loop branches from a hardcoded main — a repo on any other branch cannot run a single ticket
tickets.notes: Found by running the product, not by a test. Same hardcode class the founder called out for model names in W13-36: a customer uses what they have, not what we assumed.
acceptance: MEASURED: a customer project created with plain git init (default branch master on this machine) built its board, then Start a run refused every ticket with: fatal: invalid reference: main. Zero tickets are workable on any repo whose trunk is not literally named main.

ROOT CAUSE, verified not guessed: loop-land.ts runLandLoop does options.baseRef ?? 'main', and nothing on the server/CLI path supplies baseRef. berths.ts already defaults the same concept to HEAD, so two defaults for one idea disagree inside one package — evidence for which one is right, not a tie.

Resolve the repo's ACTUAL branch instead of guessing a name. An explicit options.baseRef still wins; otherwise read the checkout. Add the helper to @dokima/git (mergeLocal already runs this exact rev-parse inline) rather than a fourth copy.
A detached HEAD must REFUSE with a message naming the problem, not silently fall back to a guessed branch. Guessing is what produced a failure that reads like a broken product.
Do NOT change berths.ts: HEAD is already correct there, and this ticket is about the loop agreeing with it.
RED FIXTURE: the land loop runs a ticket to completion in a repo whose trunk is named something other than main. That fixture is red today for exactly the reason above.

tickets.title: the park comment tells the operator THAT a ticket failed and never HOW
tickets.notes: The human-facing twin of W13-30, which fixed exactly this for the maker. Found by running a real ticket on a local model.
acceptance: MEASURED. A real ticket ran on a local model, exhausted its 12-iteration tool budget twice, and parked. The whole explanation the operator got was: attempt 1/2: exitCode=1 no completion manifest returned. The session had said precisely why — exceeded the per-session tool-iteration budget (12) without a Completion Manifest (T-27) — and attemptSummaryLine dropped it.

CONSEQUENCE: the remedy is a real setting (maxToolIterations) and it is undiscoverable. The operator cannot tell a model that ran out of turns from one that crashed, from one that answered nothing — all three print the same line. The agent had in fact written correct scaffolding into the worktree; the run read as a flat failure.
Carry the session's own stderr into the summary when there is no manifest. Bounded and with truncation ANNOUNCED, matching verifyFailureTail (W13-30) rather than inventing a second convention.

REDACTED, not raw: the park comment is appended to the event log, and Law 8 says secrets never reach it. Use redactString the way W13-29 does for fed-back gaps. A test must plant a secret-shaped string in stderr and assert it does not survive.
Say nothing extra when stderr is empty: the existing line is already right for a session that simply returned no manifest with no explanation.

tickets.title: a session can wait forever for a provider queue slot — the run never ends and nothing says why
tickets.notes: This is the founder-reported failure class: a session that never ends and has to be kickstarted by hand. Reproduced in our own product on a healthy endpoint.
acceptance: MEASURED. A ticket ran on a local model and the run sat at status running for 25+ minutes with ZERO events after a single session.turn_started. LM Studio was fully healthy throughout — /v1/models in 1ms, a chat completion on the same model in 0.36s. The product was hung, not the endpoint. This is the founder-reported failure class: a session that never ends and has to be kickstarted by hand.

WHY THE EXISTING GUARD DID NOT FIRE: the 60s idle abort (W13-15) is armed INSIDE the stream, and the stream had not started. runQueuedStream awaits a queue slot BEFORE calling source(), and that await has no bound at all.

THE LEAK: RequestQueue defaults to concurrency 1, and runQueuedStream only releases its slot from the generator finally. A consumer that abandons the stream without closing it never releases, so every later call to that provider blocks forever.

BOUND THE WAIT. Acquiring a slot gets a deadline; exceeding it raises the same ProviderTimeoutError shape the rest of the system already understands, so W13-27 retries it for free as infrastructure rather than spending a ladder rung. The bound must NOT punish honest queueing — several berths sharing one provider legitimately wait — so default generously and make it configurable next to streamIdleMs.
RED FIXTURE: a queue whose slot is never released must make the next call FAIL with a timeout naming the queue, not hang. Assert it against a fake clock, not by waiting.
Out of scope: finding the abandonment path that leaks the slot. That is worth its own ticket; this one makes the product recover instead of needing a person to kickstart it.

tickets.title: a runaway generation streams forever — nothing bounds one turn, so the run never ends
tickets.notes: This is the founder-reported failure (ISSUE12 issue 1) in its final form: the session never ends and a person has to restart it. W13-42 fixed a different cause of the same symptom; this is the remaining one.
acceptance: MEASURED, three separate live runs. The run sits at status running with no events after a single session.turn_started. Proven in flight, not stuck: lsof shows an ESTABLISHED connection to the endpoint, LM Studio sits at 160% CPU, and our node process at 0.7%. The model is generating and will not stop.

WHY NO GUARD FIRES, and this is by design rather than by omission: W13-15 replaced duration bounds with an IDLE bound on the founder's own instruction — as long as it is streaming we leave it open. That is right for a 27B generating slowly. It leaves a model that never stops generating completely unbounded, because every token bumps the idle timer.
The W13-42 queue bound does NOT cover this and was verified not to: the stall outlasted the 5-minute acquire timeout with no error, because the request had a slot and was streaming.

BOUND ONE TURN by output, not by duration. request.maxTokens already exists on the adapter and the agent session never sets one, so a turn may emit without limit. A ceiling on completion tokens per turn ends a runaway while leaving a slow model alone — which is the property W13-15 protects and this must not undo.

The failure must read as INFRASTRUCTURE (W13-27 retries it free), and the park comment must name it — W13-41 made that visible, so the operator should see the ceiling and its number rather than a bare no-manifest line.
RED FIXTURE: a fake provider that streams deltas forever must end the turn and the run, not hang the suite. Assert against a token count, never by waiting.

tickets.title: the watchdog is built, tested, and has never run — nothing wires it into the claim or land loop
tickets.notes: Found by the no-production-caller sweep, ranked first because this session was spent on sessions that hang while the guard for exactly that sat unused.
acceptance: runWatchdogSession is defined and tested in watchdog-session.ts and has ZERO non-test references in the repo. Its single mention outside its own test is a COMMENT in loop-claim.ts. It is not present in apps/server/dist/main.js, so it has never executed in the shipped product.

Its own module header says so: "Not yet wired into those loops — out of this ticket write-scope — this is the drop-in unit a future ticket composes into the claim/land loops." That future ticket was never filed. This is it.

WHY IT MATTERS NOW: W13-42 and W13-43 both exist because a session hung and nothing stopped it. A watchdog with dead-letter escalation was sitting in the package the whole time. Wiring it is defence in depth behind those two bounds, not a replacement for them.

DEVIATION, recorded because the ticket as filed is impossible: runWatchdogSession cannot wrap the built-in agent. It requires a  and builds its spawn from createWatchdogChildProcessSpawn; the built-in agent is createGatewaySpawnSession, an in-process async function with no command. Reuse the PURE checkWatchdogBreach inside the session turn loop instead, and give the external-CLI runner the real child-process watchdog it was written for.

COOPERATIVE, never a Promise.race. An in-process session cannot be cancelled from outside, so a race abandons a session that keeps taking turns, keeps spending against a ticket, and keeps writing into the worktree after the gate ran. Check the breach at a turn boundary and return. Also note deadLetterAndBlock RELEASES the ticket despite its name — calling it mid-session would fight the land loop that owns the claim, so the breach surfaces through the session result and the loop parks with evidence as it already does.

SCOPED TO THE BUILT-IN AGENT, which is the default and where every measured hang happened. The external-CLI runner needs the child-process watchdog it was actually written for — a real kill, not a cooperative check — and that touches apps/server/src/cli/run-build.ts, which W13-46 already claims. validate-plan refused the overlap (P8), correctly. Filed as W13-47 rather than worked around.

tickets.title: two superseded duplicates: the unused morning queue, and createChildProcessSpawn
tickets.notes: Not a missing feature — a duplicate one. The shipped morning queue works; this is the copy that will go stale. Deleting createChildProcessSpawn would have dropped the ONLY test of SC-03/SC-07 env hardening — and W13-47 had just moved external agents onto a spawn with no env coverage at all. Ported first.
acceptance: buildQueueProjection and buildReviewCard have zero non-test references and are absent from the shipped bundle. The morning queue a user actually sees is built by apps/server notifications-routes, which does not call either.

So the product has TWO implementations of one surface, one of them unreachable and unmaintained. This repo has already been bitten by a second copy drifting from the first (W10-55 provider kinds, W12-19 wizard kind list).
DECIDE, and record the decision: either the routes adopt these (one implementation, tested) or these are deleted (one implementation, shipped). Do not leave both.
If adopting: the route behaviour is the contract — its tests must still pass unchanged, since that is what users have.

SECOND CASE, same class: W13-47 replaced createChildProcessSpawn's only production caller with createWatchedExternalSpawn, so it is now an export with no caller — it consumed the export ratchet's last slot of headroom (60 -> 61 against a baseline of 61). It is superseded, not merely unused: the watched spawn does the same job with a bound. Remove it and LOWER the ratchet, rather than leaving a second way to spawn an unbounded child process for someone to reach for later.

tickets.title: a completed land was destroyed by the push that announces it
tickets.notes: Verify before fixing: this may be a deliberate local-first default rather than a gap. Either way the docs and the code should agree.
acceptance: createGiteaForgeAdapter, createGitHubForgeAdapter, flushMirrorQueue and checkMirrorPrerequisites all have zero non-test references. run-build.ts passes localFirstPushToRemotes, and land-push.ts says it "structurally mirrors @dokima/forge's real pushToRemotes" — two implementations of one idea, only one reachable.
ESTABLISH WHICH IS INTENDED. FR-I2 promises dual-remote push; the wizard offers a forge credential step. If a user fills that in today, determine by EXECUTION whether anything uses it.

If the forge path is meant to be reachable, wire it and say what selects between local-first and forge. If local-first is the only supported path today, the wizard step and FR-I2 must say so — an offered field that goes nowhere is the W13-35 defect again.
RED FIXTURE: complete the wizard with a forge credential and assert, by execution, that landing either reaches the forge or refuses honestly. Not that a function exists.

SCOPE NOTE: run-build.ts is deliberately NOT claimed here. Establish first, by execution, whether the forge path is reachable; if wiring is then required, re-scope this ticket to include it rather than holding a file on speculation — that speculation is what clashed with W13-44 and W13-47.

tickets.title: the external-CLI agent runner has no watchdog — and it is the path with no bounds at all
tickets.notes: Split out of W13-44 because both wanted run-build.ts and W13-46 already claims it — validate-plan P8 refused the overlap. Scope widened to the harbormaster barrel: it never published the watchdog at all, which is WHY nothing could call it — the same build-then-wire seam as W12-04 (packer), W12-09 (code index) and W13-23 (memory anchor), now a fourth time.
acceptance: W13-42 (queue wait), W13-43 (turn output) and W13-44 (session wall-clock) all bound the BUILT-IN agent. The external-CLI runner has none of them: run-build.ts hands it createChildProcessSpawn, which waits on a child process for as long as that process runs.

createWatchdogChildProcessSpawn is a drop-in SpawnSession with the same shape plus limits and onBreach, and it kills the process TREE with a force-kill grace. That is the right guard here precisely because a child CAN be killed, where an in-process session cannot — which is why W13-44 had to be cooperative instead.

THE BREACH REASON DOES NOT REACH THE CALLER TODAY: that spawn kills the tree and resolves from child close with whatever the process happened to emit, so onBreach is the only place the reason exists. Wrap it so the explanation lands in stderr, where W13-41 already puts session reasons into the park comment.

ONE setting for both runners, derived from measured sessions rather than a round number (attempts on this board ran ~3 minutes, and the ladder multiplies that by attempt count). W13-44 hardcoded the built-in default; exposing it here must feed the built-in session too, or the product carries two wall-clock ceilings that can disagree. Same settings-key mechanism as maxToolIterations and maxTurnTokens — a CEILING, refuse rather than clamp.
RED FIXTURE: an external command that never exits must be killed AND reported, asserted against a real short ceiling on a real child process rather than by waiting on the default.

tickets.title: the Roster is a debug dump — internal prompt text, three failure-toned lines per card, no action

tickets.title: capture-tour emits a text-first evidence pack — the audit's eyes, serialized for models without vision

acceptance: Beside each captured frame, an evidence.json: every visible text string; every interactive element as role + accessible name; per-element bounding geometry; summary stats (content-area occupancy fraction, per-column card class histograms on the board).

Deterministic and mock-free like the tour it extends: real server, throwaway home, zero model calls during capture.
The pack is data the trust boundary treats as evidence: stable ordering, so two captures of an unchanged UI byte-diff clean (the W13-07 rot-detection property extends to evidence).

tickets.title: the end-user-simulator judges the evidence pack through the gateway, citations re-verified before findings enter the funnel
tickets.notes: Layer 3 of DESIGN_REVIEW_LOOP.md. Dispatch shape per the onboard-mode precedent (code reads, model judges); Law 9a: tests use the fake gateway, never live calls. Scope narrowed from apps/server/src/api/pipeline/** after P8 flagged overlap with W13-51's model-resolution.ts — the dispatch lives in its own ux-audit/ directory; holding the whole tree was speculation, the third time this session P8 has caught exactly that. Scope widened to the route-registration point in server.ts and the pipeline barrel BEFORE building — a route module nothing registers and a mode no barrel exports are this board's defining defect, and this ticket exists because of it.
acceptance: A ux-audit run: harness hands evidence packs to the end-user-simulator expert via the gateway (matrix-routed — local qwen must work, C-1), model returns AuditFinding[] in the existing improve-mode shape.

EVERY finding carries a citation — an exact string that must appear in the evidence pack. The harness re-greps each citation; a finding whose citation is absent is DROPPED and logged (C-2/C-3: a model's claim is never trusted unverified). The drop is visible in the run, not silent.
Surviving findings enter the existing findings -> plan -> tickets funnel with receipts, where severity/leverage vocabulary is honest (closes the loop with W13-50).
C-4 by construction: the judging role is a verifier role, so route() refuses it sharing the maker's model.

RED FIXTURE (docs/TESTING.md planted-defect discipline): a scripted fake-gateway judge returns one finding with a real citation and one with a fabricated citation; the real one reaches the plan, the fabricated one is dropped and the drop is logged.
Vision degrades honestly (FR-G5): a vision-capable model may receive frames as enrichment; a text-only model gets the same run with no warning-free silent skip — the run records which mode judged.

tickets.title: idea to board: actions with unstated consequences and undefined verbs on the novice\u2019s critical path

[HIGH] The Improvement Plan card asks the novice to Accept or Dismiss PC-001 based on a machine expression ('receipts.staleCount == 0') and jargon-dense rationale ('stale receipt(s)', 'downstream phases', 'gating on invalidated evidence'), with no statement of what Accept actually does — an undecidable decision. [MEDIUM] The Ready ticket card exposes a 'Move to…' select offering 'claim', but nothing tells the novice what claiming means, that agents normally do this, or what happens to the ticket if they pick it — an invitation to mutate state with undefined verbs. CITATION (evidence) 05-board-seeded: "Move to…" FIX: Label the menu with the vocabulary word and consequence (e.g. 'claim — assign this ticket to be worked next') or hide manual verbs behind the ticket drawer where they can be explained.

[MEDIUM] The one hard dead end on the decide path — no token to load the inline decisions — is explained with 'slates' (defined nowhere a user can see) and 'workspace' (a word VOCABULARY.md explicitly bans in favor of 'project'), so the novice hits a wall described in words they have never met. CITATION (source) apps/web/src/onboarding/AwaitingDecisions.tsx: "The slates were kept, but this session has no API token to load them — reopen" FIX: Rewrite in vocabulary words: 'Your decisions were saved. Reopen this project to answer them.' — and use 'decisions', not 'slates', everywhere a user reads it.

[LOW] The very first workspace screen greets the novice with two undefined internal terms — the Chat empty state promises 'manifests' and the Board empty state promises the idea will be 'decomposed into tickets' — before they have done anything at all. CITATION (evidence) 04-workspace-empty: "Messages, questions, findings, and manifests appear here as agents work." FIX: Replace 'manifests' with plain language (or define Completion Manifest at first meeting, as VOCABULARY.md requires) and swap 'decomposed into' for 'broken into'.

tickets.title: run and recover: blocked is a dead end and the trace speaks wire ids to the person it exists to inform
tickets.notes: Novice-journey audit (orchestrated 2026-08-20, five parallel reviewers, every citation mechanically re-verified — 24/24 held). The persona: a novice with a building idea and no clue what to do, who must be walked through everything.
acceptance: [HIGH] A blocked ticket offers the novice nothing to do: no verb in the transitions graph lists 'blocked' as a source, so the card renders no Move menu and every drag off the Blocked column is an illegal drop that animates back — the state announces itself but has no exit affordance and no on-card explanation of how a ticket ever leaves Blocked. [HIGH] When a drag is refused, the popover's headline 'rule' line is an SRS/SC requirement id by design (e.g. 'FR-T2'), which is written for the builder — a novice reads an opaque code where the explanation of why the board said no should be. CITATION (source) apps/web/src/board/refusal.ts: " * name (SRS FR id or SC id, e.g. `FR-T2`) is shown alongside the human" FIX: Lead with the human-language rule ('Tickets need a passing gate before review') and demote the FR/SC id to a small provenance tag.

[MEDIUM] Every trace event carries a 'File field report' button, but nothing on the screen says what a field report is, who reads it, or what happens after filing — the term appears nowhere in VOCABULARY.md, so the novice has an unlabeled consequence attached to the trace's only per-event action. CITATION (evidence) 07-session-trace: "File field report" FIX: Add a tooltip/one-line explainer ('Flag this event so the improvement loop learns from it') and register the term in VOCABULARY.md or rename it to something self-describing.

[MEDIUM] The ticket drawer greets the novice with six consecutive empty states ('No acceptance criteria recorded.', 'No history yet.', 'No manifest yet.', 'No gates have run yet.', 'No spend recorded yet…') plus undefined jargon ('No active berth on this ticket right now.', 'Spend by rung') — each is honest but none says what will fill it or what the novice should do next, and 'berth' and 'rung' are absent from the vocabulary law. CITATION (evidence) 06-ticket-drawer: "No active berth on this ticket right now." FIX: Rewrite each empty state to name the trigger that fills it ('Gates run automatically when an agent closes this ticket'), and define or replace 'berth' and 'rung' per VOCABULARY.md.

[LOW] The card's Move menu offers bare lifecycle verbs like 'claim → claimed' without saying who claims — the novice cannot tell whether choosing it assigns the ticket to themselves or dispatches an agent, i.e. whether the action spends anything or starts work. CITATION (evidence) 05-board-seeded: "claim" FIX: Label the menu options with actor and consequence (e.g. 'Claim for an agent — moves to Claimed') at least on first use.

tickets.title: the run outcome is invisible: parked returns to Ready unmarked, the banner says finished, and Chat stays silent
tickets.notes: Live novice rerun, 2026-08-20 evening, fresh home, local model. Complements W13-60 (park comment written for the builder) — this is the layer ABOVE it: the novice never reaches the comment at all. Scope widened before building: the Chat pane is empty because the ROUTE serves a hardcoded empty stream to registered projects (chat-fixture.ts: "no chat or message producer exists anywhere in this repo yet" — stale premise, the producers landed weeks ago). The fix is the real projection that route's own HANDOFF asks for.
acceptance: MEASURED live: a run parked PLAN-auth-setup after 2 attempts. The ticket returned to READY with no visible mark, the banner read "run-mt1zfnvy — finished", and the Chat pane still said "No agent activity yet." after a full agent session. From the novice's chair: the run finished and nothing happened.

TWO SYSTEMS DISAGREE: the park comment's own header says "auto-blocked with evidence" while loop-land's park path calls releaseTicket — status ready. Either the park marks the ticket visibly (a parked state-in-form on the card, with the attempt evidence one click away) or the comment stops claiming blocked. The board must show WHICH ticket parked and WHY without opening a drawer.
The run banner surfaces the outcome line the CLI already prints ("0 landed, 1 parked") instead of the bare status word. "finished" with nothing landed reads as success-toned nothing.

The Chat pane either receives session events (turn started, producing, spend — they are all in the event log) or stops promising them. A pane that says "appear here as agents work" and stays empty through a real session is a broken promise on the novice's most-watched screen.
RED FIXTURE: drive a run that parks (fake gateway, no manifest) through the real routes and assert the board shows a parked mark on the ticket and the banner carries landed/parked counts.

tickets.title: the guided sample writes user data to /tmp — and the e2e suite deletes every such folder on the machine
tickets.notes: DATA LOSS, observed: a real novice walkthrough created its sample at /tmp/dokima-sample-<ts>; a later e2e run on the same machine deleted it (guided-sample.spec.ts afterEach rm -rf globs ALL /tmp/dokima-sample-*). The Fleet then honestly shows "Unavailable — folder is gone", but the work is gone with it. Scope widened for the systemic half: a DOKIMA_WORKSPACE_ROOT env override (the same mechanism DOKIMA_HOME is) so no test harness can ever write into a real home, plus a validator gating /tmp literals out of product code permanently.
acceptance: FirstRunWizard.handleCreateSample hardcodes path: /tmp/dokima-sample-<ts> — volatile (macOS clears /tmp on reboot), shared, and e2e-clobberable. The spec's own comment has flagged the hardcode since it was written. A REAL user's first project must not live somewhere the OS or a test run erases.
Create the sample the way W12-41 creates New projects: let the SERVER choose a durable location (the same default folder New project uses), or place it under DOKIMA_HOME. No /tmp.

guided-sample.spec.ts stops deleting folders it did not create: it must track exactly the paths its own run made (resolve them via the API it drove) and remove only those. A machine-wide glob delete of user-shaped folders in a test suite is the defect, independent of where the wizard writes.
RED FIXTURE: complete the wizard's sample step and assert the created project's path is NOT under /tmp; the spec's cleanup provably touches only paths recorded from its own session.

tickets.title: packages/mcp gets a real client: stdio transport implementing the injected ToolExecutor
notes: Filed 2026-08-20 from the integrations audit: the mcpServers settings key is stored and read by nothing; packages/mcp has the full allowlist/approval machinery with no transport, so FR-I3 is a promise with no wire. Transport was deliberately kept out and injected (tool-call.ts) — this ticket builds the injectable.
acceptance: ESTABLISHED, not assumed (verified 2026-08-20): requestToolCall takes an injected ToolExecutor and the only production executor is the closed agent-session set — no code can connect to an external MCP server. CITATION (source) packages/mcp/src/tool-call.ts: "Transport (stdio/HTTP/SSE spawn) is deliberately kept out of this package and injected instead".

Build a stdio JSON-RPC MCP client under packages/mcp/src/client/**: spawn -> initialize -> tools/list -> tools/call, implementing the ToolExecutor contract, with an explicit kill/dispose lifecycle. Every await on the child carries a deadline (the W13-47 lesson: a hung server is killed and reported, never awaited forever).
Law 9(a) is hard: tests speak to a LOCAL fake MCP server child process (a fixture script in-repo speaking the wire protocol) — no network, no live servers, in any test or CI path.

Discovered tools map to McpToolDefinition with ids namespaced <serverId>.<tool> so an external tool can never collide with the closed agent-session set (mcp-wiring.ts AGENT_SESSION_SERVER_ID namespace).

RED FIXTURE: a fixture server that never answers initialize is killed at the deadline with an error naming the server id; a tools/call that errors surfaces the server’s own message, never a bare exit code (the W13-41 lesson).

tickets.title: preload configured MCP servers at run start
notes: The mcpServers settings key is a passthrough nothing reads (verified 2026-08-20). Preloading = read settings, spawn clients, register servers+tools in the project log, route calls.
acceptance: Define the mcpServers settings schema (server id, command, args, env as credential REFS only — Law 8/FR-S2) in settings-types with validation; the untyped passthrough becomes typed. CITATION (source) apps/server/src/api/server/settings-routes.ts: "keys (`mcpServers`, `validatorPackSelection`".

At run start, read merged settings, start each configured server via the W14-01 client, registerServer + discovered tools into the project log (idempotent across runs, same tolerance as ensureAgentSessionToolsRegistered — CITATION packages/harbormaster/src/agent-session/mcp-wiring.ts), and compose a ToolExecutor routing <serverId>.<tool> to its client. All clients disposed when the run ends, breach or not.
A server that fails to start degrades honestly (FR-G5): the run continues, the failure is ledgered as an event and printed once — never a silent absence and never a crashed run.
Credential refs resolve through the keychain resolver at spawn time; the literal value never lands in settings, the event log, or any spawn record (Law 8) — asserted by a planted-ref fixture.
RED FIXTURE: a run configured with one healthy and one broken server registers and can call the healthy one through requestToolCall while the broken one is ledgered, and the run proceeds.

tickets.title: agent sessions see external MCP tools behind the allowlist, with approval cards
notes: FR-I3: tools surface through a per-role allowlist matrix; side-effectful tools carry requiresApproval; every call is an audited, costed event. The machinery (setRoleAllowlist, requestToolCall, decideToolCall, PendingApproval) is built and tested with no caller — this wires it.
acceptance: External tools join the session’s tool schemas ONLY behind the role allowlist (setRoleAllowlist): a role without an entry cannot see the tool at all (FR-I3 acceptance sketch). The closed built-in seven stay exactly as they are. CITATION (source) packages/harbormaster/src/agent-session/tools.ts.

External tools default requiresApproval: true. A call to one parks a Decide-tier notification (same store the morning queue reads) and returns a structured awaiting-approval tool result to the session — the session keeps its turn discipline and never blocks a queue slot on a human (the W13-42 lesson).

decideToolCall is the only path from pending to executed: approval executes through the run’s composed executor and the result reaches the ticket’s next session pass; rejection records and informs. Approver identity is the notification decider, mechanically distinct from the session actor (C-4).
Every external call — requested, approved, rejected, executed — is an audited event replayable from the log (FR-I3), with cost recorded.

RED FIXTURE: (a) role without allowlist entry cannot see the tool; (b) a requiresApproval call parks a card and does NOT execute; (c) deciding it executes on the injected fake executor and the result lands in the next pass.

tickets.title: MCP has a face: Settings panel and the approval card shows the work
notes: Novice north star: register a server once, see its tools, and decide approvals from the morning queue with the evidence on the card (the W13-61 discipline).
acceptance: Settings gains an MCP servers panel: register a server (name, command, credential ref — never a raw secret field, Law 8), see its discovered tools, toggle per-role allowlist entries and requiresApproval. Copy obeys VOCABULARY.md and defines any new term at first meeting.

The morning queue renders a tool-approval Decide card that SHOWS THE WORK: server, tool, and the requested arguments digest, with mechanism-true consequence copy under Approve/Reject (what approving actually executes) — the W13-61 standard, not a bare "a tool wants to run".
validate-ui-copy green with zero new baseline entries; axe passes on the new panel (the W13-52 contrast lesson).
RED FIXTURE: the approval card renders the actual requested arguments digest from the pending approval, and a card for a since-resolved approval says so instead of offering dead buttons.

tickets.title: the learning loop writes: parks become error→solution facts, recalled first on retry
notes: Verified 2026-08-20: insertFact has no production caller, so createMemoryAnchor recalls from an always-empty bank — the exact cautionary tale its own header names. Composition lives in apps/server: harbormaster may not import memory (ARCHITECTURE §4, the W13-23 seam).
acceptance: ESTABLISHED: nothing writes facts today. CITATION (source) packages/memory/src/store/anchor.ts: "an unwired memory engine recalls nothing and is worth nothing".

A parked/failed attempt inserts an error_solution fact (symptom: park reason + failing-verify head, ticket-scoped), redacted by the same redactor as park comments before insert (Law 8). When a later attempt closes the same ticket, the fact is marked verified with the closing commit.

Retry handoffs (attempt >= 2) assemble context via assembleErrorFirstContext so the prior failure+fix leads the packet — order asserted, not incidental (US-602). CITATION (source) packages/memory/src/consolidation/error-first-recall.ts.
The seam stays in apps/server (harbormaster gets an injected attempt-outcome hook, never a memory import) — same construction as run-build-spawn.ts’s memoryAnchor (W13-23).

RED FIXTURE: a park-then-retry run shows the second attempt’s context leading with the first attempt’s failure fact at position 0; a closing attempt marks that fact verified; a Law 8 planted credential in verify output never reaches the fact bank.

notes: runSleepConsolidation is the built job body waiting for its scheduler (its own header says so). ON by default per FR-M3; per-project toggle per US-603 AC-1.
acceptance: After a run completes, consolidation runs for the project unless the per-project setting disables it (ON by default, FR-M3). CITATION (source) packages/memory/src/consolidation/consolidate.ts: "runSleepConsolidation is what that scheduler calls once it decides".
The MorningPreBrief lands as a review-tier notification the morning queue renders, in VOCABULARY words.
Exactly one memory.consolidated event per real pass; a disabled project emits nothing and touches nothing — asserted at the wiring level, not only in the package.
