tickets.title: the review loop runs: landed work gets a cross-model reviewer verdict with independent re-run evidence
notes: Filed 2026-08-20 vision audit. Every primitive exists and none is wired: tickets land into in_review and no production path ever reviews them — the human approves from maker-produced evidence. BLUEPRINT: cross-model review is an integrity feature; a verdict without a re-ran-independently line is INCOMPLETE and is bounced, not counted.
acceptance: ESTABLISHED, not assumed (verified 2026-08-20): no production caller runs a reviewer session over an in_review ticket; evaluateScoreVerdict/classifyReviewSignal/isValidRerun/assertChallengerModelDistinct are tested with no ticket-path consumer. CITATION (source) docs/BLUEPRINT.md: "Every reviewer/challenger verdict must carry a `re-ran independently: <command, counts, exit code>` evidence line; a verdict without one is INCOMPLETE and is bounced, not counted."

After the land loop, a REVIEW PASS visits each in_review ticket with a close receipt: a code-reviewer role session (its own routing; maker!=verifier enforced mechanically — same-model collapse REFUSES the machine review and says so rather than laundering it, C-4/Law 9b honest degradation for single-model installs) reads the diff and manifest, independently re-runs the ticket verify command via the verify tool, and returns a verdict.

The verdict is parsed against the challenger contract: CONFIRMED/CONTRADICTED/UNVERIFIABLE + advisory 1-10 score + the rerun evidence line, validated by isValidRerun/evaluateScoreVerdict; INCOMPLETE verdicts are bounced (one retry), never counted. classifyReviewSignal runs only on a passing deterministic gate (its own refusal).

The verdict lands as a ticket comment and a review.verdict event (Law 4); NOTHING auto-accepts — accept stays a human verb until W13-32 decides autonomy defaults. A CONTRADICTED verdict flips the Decide evidence to warning copy.

Law 9(a): all tests use the fake gateway/injected spawn — never live calls. RED FIXTURES: a passing ticket gets CONFIRMED with a rerun line; a verdict missing the rerun line is bounced and the bounce is ledgered; a same-model install refuses machine review with the honest sentence; a CONTRADICTED verdict comments the contradiction.

tickets.title: calibration runs: model self-claims are scored against the gate and bias the borderline calls
notes: FR-L3. createCalibrationRecord/updateCalibration/applyCalibrationBias/gateDecision are built+tested with no production caller (validate-exports buried list, verified 2026-08-20).
acceptance: ESTABLISHED: nothing records a (model, role) self-claim vs verify outcome; the calibration module has no production caller.

Each attempt outcome updates a per-(model, role) calibration record in the project DB: manifest claimed done + gate result observed (the W14-05 hook seam — composition in apps/server, harbormaster stays memory-free).
The W15-01 review pass consults applyCalibrationBias on borderline scores (5-6): a chronically over-claiming maker biases toward escalate, never toward auto-accept (asymmetric threshold preserved).
RED FIXTURE: two synthetic histories — honest maker vs over-claimer — produce different review signals for the same raw score, and the over-claimer never gains acceptance from bias.

tickets.title: the wiggum coverage loop runs at the phase gate: uncovered deliverables retry to the mode cap with the byte-identical halt
notes: RALPH_WIGGUM_LOOP (R-B5, W5-08) shipped as static topology; STATUS.md records the residual verbatim: nothing binds CoverageLoopDeps to real dispatch. runCoverageLoopForMode is in the buried no-caller list (verified 2026-08-20).
acceptance: ESTABLISHED: runCoverageLoopForMode has no production caller; phase advance is a one-shot decideAdvance. CITATION (source) packages/pipeline/src/modes/coverage-loop.ts: "Macro coverage loop (RALPH_WIGGUM_LOOP.md, R-B5)".

The pipeline run’s deliverable-producing step runs INSIDE the coverage loop: INVENTORY = the phase’s deliverables, DISCOVER = generate the uncovered ones, VERIFY = the same receipt check decideAdvance trusts, capped per mode (3 new-product/onboard, 2 feature/improve) with the byte-identical-gap-set early halt.
Every iteration is ledgered (coverage.iteration event: attempted, uncovered, checksum, halt reason) so a novice can see WHY a phase stopped short — no silent cap.

RED FIXTURE: a deliverable that fails once and succeeds on retry advances the phase in one run; an ever-failing one halts at the cap with the halt reason ledgered; a byte-identical gap set halts EARLY (no_progress) before the cap.

tickets.title: the escalation ladder actually escalates the model — cheapest-first, rung-resolved per attempt, ledgered
notes: Challenger audit 2026-08-21: runEscalationPolicy (packages/gateway/src/escalation/policy.ts:147) is not re-exported and has zero callers; the wired loop-land-policy.ts maps R1-R3 to attempt count on ONE model ("no model-routed rungs of its own"), and run-build-spawn.ts:88 resolves a single model once with fallbackChain: []. BLUEPRINT 3.3 promises cheapest-first THEN one rung up THEN frontier. Law 9b: which ladder applies is the user's recorded model policy — local-only users get an honest single-rung ladder (FR-G5 degrades honestly), never a silent cloud call.

Scope amended 2026-08-21 pre-implementation: the model chain lives in apps/server/src/api/pipeline/model-resolution.ts (route() returns routed.chain; resolveModelTarget discards all but chain[0]) — that file moves into this ticket and OUT of W16-05's glob, which never needed it. Acceptance 1 reworded: loop-land-policy.ts's header documents why literal delegation to runEscalationPolicy is wrong (its R0 path skips the close gate); the honest wiring is the spawn-side rung->session seam.
acceptance: Each retry re-resolves the session for the current rung from the user's recorded model policy (local-only, pinned, cheapest-first via the matrix fallback chain, approval-gated) — the land loop stays model-agnostic (rung->session seam composed in apps/server, per loop-land-policy.ts's module header) and no policy path ever silently escalates past what the user chose.

Every rung advance is ledgered as an escalation event (FR-G3) carrying rung, model, and reason; the spawn path (run-build-spawn) receives the rung-resolved target instead of a once-resolved model with an empty fallback chain.

Tests use the fake-model gateway only (law 9a); a fixture proves a cheapest-first policy walks R1 -> R2 -> R3 across failed attempts and a pinned/local-only policy stays on its rung with an honest degradation note.
RED FIXTURE: a planted always-fails ticket under a cheapest-first policy must show a rung advance in the ledger; the fixture fails if all attempts ran on the same model with no escalation event.

tickets.title: berths run in parallel — the concurrency dial actually spawns N lane-assigned workers
notes: Challenger audit 2026-08-21: runBerths (packages/harbormaster/src/berths.ts:296) has zero callers and is not barrel-exported; run-build.ts:291 calls the sequential runLandLoop once, and run-build.ts:120 records "--berths was validated, stored, and read by nothing". GatewayPool and GlobalBerthGovernor (packages/gateway/src/pool/*) also have zero external callers. BLUEPRINT 3.6/3.11. The web ActiveBerthsStrip already renders the stored count — the UI is ahead of the engine.

Acceptance amended 2026-08-21 during implementation, three reality corrections: (1) the same-lane fixture originally demanded both tickets serialize-then-land in one run -- FR-T3 reserves a lane THROUGH in_review (unaccepted diff is not safe to build on), so the second ticket correctly waits at ready; the sequential loop behaves identically. (2) "a worker crash disposes its worktree and the run continues" contradicted berths.ts documented shared-abort: an error ESCAPING the engine (which already absorbs session/provider failures) is our own bug and halts every berth with evidence -- silent continue is the failure mode this product refuses. (3) GlobalBerthGovernor admissions are ledgered per ticket; its fleet-wide cap defaults to unbounded until a settings surface exists for it.
acceptance: executeBuildRun consumes command.berths: N > 1 drives runBerths over landClaimedTicket -- the SAME one-ticket engine the sequential loop uses (loop-land-ticket.ts chapter), one worktree per active ticket, per-berth machine identities on every verb (FR-H5); N = 1 keeps runLandLoop byte-identical.

Every provider chat flows through ONE process-wide GatewayPool (FR-F3: per-endpoint FairScheduler, fair by project, local endpoints one-at-a-time per FR-G1), and each berth ticket admission passes the GlobalBerthGovernor with the admission ledgered (berths.ticket_admitted) so pool decisions are observable.

All state transitions still go through the verbs APIs from every berth (C-2/C-3); C-6 single-writer holds mechanically: one process, one synchronous better-sqlite3 handle, pick+claim back-to-back with no await (berths-scheduler.ts documented atomicity).

Tests (fake sessions, real close gate): 2 berths land 2 independent-lane tickets with distinct claim actors; an engine-escaping error halts EVERY berth with the error preserved (an evidence-preserving halt -- session/provider failures are already absorbed inside the engine, so what escapes is our own bug and never silently continues).

RED FIXTURE: with 2 berths and two claimable same-lane tickets, the second is never in flight while the first is active, and it honestly waits at ready while the first sits un-accepted in review (FR-T3: a lane stays reserved through in_review).

tickets.title: the playbook resolves at rung 0 — a prior verified solution is consulted before any model attempt
notes: Memory-loop audit 2026-08-21: createPlaybookMemoryConsultHook (packages/memory/src/playbook/r0-hook.ts:30), listPlaybookHistory, and preparePlaybookPromotion are called only from inside packages/memory and tests — the BLUEPRINT 3.3 promise "a playbook hit resolves the ladder at rung 0 without re-attempting" has no live consult point. Same built-but-unwired defect class W14-05 fixed for facts. Wire through the same apps/server-composed seam as memoryAnchor/attemptOutcome in run-build-spawn.ts.

Acceptance reworded 2026-08-21 pre-close: the original "R0 hit lands with zero model calls" contradicted loop-land-policy.ts's documented refusal of gate-skipping R0 (a ticket would sit in_progress while "resolved") and C-2 — the honest form is consult-before-spend with the answer leading the handoff and the gate still deciding.
acceptance: Before the first model attempt on a ticket, the land loop consults the playbook (local -> global FR-F5 -> fact bank) through an apps/server-composed hook; a verified hit LEADS the maker's first handoff as a prior-solution block, and every consult is ledgered as playbook.r0_hit / playbook.r0_miss.

The close gate still decides (C-2): a hit never skips the attempt or the gate — loop-land-policy.ts's documented refusal of the gateway ladder's resolve-without-a-gate R0 stands; a stale hit simply fails the gate and the ladder proceeds. A consult failure is ledgered and swallowed, never parking the ticket.

Tests use recorded fixtures and the fake gateway (law 9a); fixtures prove a hit reaches the first prompt, a miss leaves it untouched with exactly one consult per ticket, and a promoted global entry answers for a project that never saw the task (FR-F5).
RED FIXTURE: a planted playbook answer must be ledgered and present in the first session prompt BEFORE the model runs; the fixture fails if the session ran without the consult ordered ahead of it.

tickets.title: a claimed ticket with no live session is not "nothing assigned"
notes: Confirmed live 2026-08-24: claimed and started PLAN-T-001 as coding-agent through the CLI. The Board shows it In Progress and says "an agent is working this" (so ownerId is populated and the projection is fine), but the Team view shows Sam idle in the break room reading "nothing assigned". Two surfaces, two truths — the exact defect W20-02 exists to prevent.

Root cause verified by reading the mapping rather than guessing: deriveMemberState derives working/reading/self-checking ONLY from a live heartbeat, and has no branch at all for a ticket that is owned and in_progress (or claimed) with no session running. It therefore falls through every branch to idle.

The fix is a state, not a relaxation. "Working" must keep meaning a live session — that distinction is real and worth having. What is missing is the honest middle: the ticket is theirs and nothing is running on it. That is ledger-backed by the claim/start events, so it does not weaken D-028.
In the office this reads as sitting at their own desk with the screen dark — occupied desk, no work happening — which is different from the break room, where nothing is assigned at all.

tickets.title: the standalone pages get a page shell — content that sits on something
notes: Live design pass 2026-08-24, every view screenshotted. The finding is systemic and has one cause: W13-03 gave the BOARD panes a raised surface, dividers and card borders, and the standalone views never got the same pass. Roster, Settings, Decisions and Describe render content directly onto the page background — no max-width, no gutters, no panel — so text runs the full 1500px, rows bleed to both edges, and Decisions is a single sentence floating in an empty black field.

The substring also matches --sw-border-strong, so that is not a dodge. Every new border must therefore live as a shared primitive in styles.css and be applied by class at the call site — the same fix .office__scene used.

tickets.title: the subprocess-spawning suites get a timeout that matches what they do
notes: Third stop-hook red this session with the same signature as W20-13: different suites fail on different full-suite runs, all pass in isolation, and every failure reads "Test timed out in 5000ms" — never an assertion. Confirmed from the run log rather than assumed.

These three suites are the slowest things in the suite because they SPAWN PROCESSES: runValidator shells out to a validator script (and one fixture deliberately spawns a hanging process to prove the watchdog kills it), and the two phase-gate suites run a real validator pack. Holding a subprocess test to the same 5s budget as a pure unit test is the actual defect — the suite has simply grown enough that the machine is busier at the moment they run.

Same remedy and same reasoning as W20-13: raise the timeout on exactly these suites, with the reason stated in-file, and change no assertion. A gate one busy machine away from red is not a gate, but neither is one that went green by asserting less.
acceptance: The three subprocess-spawning suites carry an explicit timeout with the reason written in the file

tickets.title: the rest of the process-spawning suites, chosen by measurement
notes: W21-07 fixed the three suites that had actually been OBSERVED failing. This finishes the class — but by measurement, not by grep. A grep for child_process/execa/spawn matches 27 test files; most of them import a helper and never spend real time in a subprocess, and blanket-editing all 27 would assert a problem nobody had measured.

Method, so it does not have to be re-derived: run the full suite twice at idle and once with the e2e suite deliberately in flight, then diff per-file durations. The load run is the one that matters — it reproduces the contention that produces the failures.

Measured under load, the heaviest suites were loop-land 23.2s (covered by W20-13), validate-history-secrets 9.7s (already 60s, documented), loop-gates 8.6s, gateway-session 8.1s, conductor-lib 6.8s (its one slow test already 30s), run-build 6.5s, artifacts-routes 4.9s, advance 4.6s (W21-07), berths 4.3s (W20-13). The four uncovered ones that ALSO genuinely spawn — git worktrees plus a real validator, or spawn()/execFile directly — are this ticket. plan-scheduler (4.5s) and providers-routes (4.3s) are heavy but spawn nothing, so there is no evidence of this failure mode there and they are left alone.

Worth recording because it changes the diagnosis: packages/validators/src/run.test.ts runs in 1.3s in a normal full run and took 43s on the run where it failed. These suites are not chronically close to the limit — they are vulnerable to occasional machine-level stalls, which is exactly why the fix is a budget that fits the work rather than shaving milliseconds.
acceptance: The four measured, genuinely-spawning suites carry an explicit timeout with the reason and the measurement in the file
No assertion is loosened, no fixture work is cut, and no suite without evidence is touched
The full suite passes at idle and with e2e in flight

tickets.title: write down how to tell a slow test from a starved one
notes: Three stop-hook reds this session had the same cause and were each diagnosed from scratch. The knowledge that stops a fourth is not a mechanism — it is a method: how to recognise the signature, how to measure it under the contention that causes it, and the rule for what may and may not be changed in response.

Deliberately NOT a validator. The obvious guard — "a test importing child_process must declare a timeout" — would force a timeout onto 20+ suites that import a helper and never spend real time in a subprocess, which is the unmeasured blanket edit W21-08 avoided. A guard that fires without evidence teaches people to silence it.
acceptance: docs/TESTING.md names the signature, the measurement method, and the rule about what may not be changed
It records which suites currently carry a raised timeout and why, so the list is auditable
